284.s:
dhanvantarir uvāca
siddhayogān punarvakṣe mṛtasañjīvanīkarān/
ātreyabhāṣitān divyān sarvavyādhivimardanān(3) //
284.d:
धन्वन्तरिर् उवाच
सिद्धयोगान् पुनर्वक्षे मृतसञ्जीवनीकरान्/
आत्रेयभाषितान् दिव्यान् सर्वव्याधिविमर्दनान्(3) //
284.m: Dhanvantari said: / I shall further declare proven recipes that revive the dead, / divine remedies spoken by Ātreya that crush all diseases.

284.s:
ātreya uvāca
vilvādipañcamūlasya kvāthaḥ syādvātike jvare /
pāvanaṃ pippalīmūlaṃ guḍūcī viṣvajo 'tha vā //
:n
1 vīrakārye iti kha..
2 ekanāmātha sarthakamiti kha.. , ña.. ca
3 sarvavyādhivināśakāniti kha..
:p 50
284.d:
आत्रेय उवाच
विल्वादिपञ्चमूलस्य क्वाथः स्याद्वातिके ज्वरे /
पावनं पिप्पलीमूलं गुडूची विष्वजो ऽथ वा //
:न्
1 वीरकार्ये इति ख..
2 एकनामाथ सर्थकमिति ख.. , ञ.. च
3 सर्वव्याधिविनाशकानिति ख..
:प् 50
284.m:
Ātreya said: / A decoction of the five roots beginning with bilva is [prescribed] in fever of vāta origin; / or pure long pepper root, guḍūcī, and dried ginger.
[Notes]
1. "vīrakārye" in manuscript kha.
2. "ekanāmātha sarthakam" in manuscripts kha and ña.
3. "sarvavyādhivināśakān" in manuscript kha. / [Page 50]

284.s:
āmalakyabhayā kṛṣṇa vahniḥ sarvajvarāntakaḥ /
vilvāgnimanthaśyonākakāśmaryaḥ pārlā sthirā //
284.d:
आमलक्यभया कृष्ण वह्निः सर्वज्वरान्तकः /
विल्वाग्निमन्थश्योनाककाश्मर्यः पार्ला स्थिरा //
284.m: Emblic myrobalan, chebulic myrobalan, black pepper, and leadwort destroy all fevers. / Bilva, agnimantha, śyonāka, kāśmarya, pāṭalā, sthirā,

284.s:
trikaṇṭakaṃ pṛśnaparṇī vṛhatī kaṇṭakārikāḥ /
jvarāvipākapārśvārtikāśanut kuśamūlakam //
284.d:
त्रिकण्टकं पृश्नपर्णी वृहती कण्टकारिकाः /
ज्वराविपाकपार्श्वार्तिकाशनुत् कुशमूलकम् //
284.m: trikaṇṭaka, pṛśniparṇī, bṛhatī, and kaṇṭakārī, / [along with] root of kuśa grass, remove fever, indigestion, flank pain, and cough.

284.s:
guḍūcī parpaṭī mustaṃ kirātaṃ viśvabheṣajam /
vātapittajvare deyaṃ pañcabhadramidaṃ smṛtam //
284.d:
गुडूची पर्पटी मुस्तं किरातं विश्वभेषजम् /
वातपित्तज्वरे देयं पञ्चभद्रमिदं स्मृतम् //
284.m: Guḍūcī, parpaṭī, mustā, kirātatikta, and ginger: / this is remembered as "the five auspicious remedies," to be given in fever caused by vāta and pitta.

284.s:
trivṛdviśālakaṭukātriphalāragbadhaiḥ kṛtaḥ /
sṃskāro bhedanakvāthaḥ peyaḥ sarvajvarāpahaḥ //
284.d:
त्रिवृद्विशालकटुकात्रिफलारग्बधैः कृतः /
स्ंस्कारो भेदनक्वाथः पेयः सर्वज्वरापहः //
284.m: Prepared with trivṛt, indravāruṇī, kaṭukā, triphalā, and āragvadha, / a purgative decoction should be drunk; it dispels all fevers.

284.s:
devadārubalāvāsātriphalāvyopapadmakaiḥ(1) /
saviḍaṅgaiḥ sitātulyaṃ taccurṇaṃ pañcakāśajit //
284.d:
देवदारुबलावासात्रिफलाव्योपपद्मकैः(1) /
सविडङ्गैः सितातुल्यं तच्चुर्णं पञ्चकाशजित् //
284.m: Devadāru, balā, vāsā, triphalā, the three pungents, and padmaka, / along with viḍaṅga, with sugar equal to the whole: that powder cures the five kinds of cough.

284.s:
daśamūlīśaṭīrāsnāpippalībilvapauṣkaraiḥ /
śṛṅgītāmalakībhārgīguḍūcīnāgavallibhiḥ //
284.d:
दशमूलीशटीरास्नापिप्पलीबिल्वपौष्करैः /
शृङ्गीतामलकीभार्गीगुडूचीनागवल्लिभिः //
284.m: With daśamūla, śaṭī, rāsnā, pippalī, bilva, puṣkaramūla, / śṛṅgī, āmalakī, bhārgī, guḍūcī, and betel leaves,

284.s:
yavāgraṃ vidhinā siddhaṃ kaśāyaṃ vā pivennaraḥ /
kāśahṛdgrahaṇīpārśvahikvāśvāsapraśāntaye //
284.d:
यवाग्रं विधिना सिद्धं कशायं वा पिवेन्नरः /
काशहृद्ग्रहणीपार्श्वहिक्वाश्वासप्रशान्तये //
284.m: or a decoction prepared properly from barley groats, a man should drink / for the relief of cough, heart disease, chronic diarrhoea, flank pain, hiccups, and asthma.

284.s:
madhukaṃ madhunā yuktaṃ vippalīṃ śarkarānvitāṃ /
nāgaraṃ guḍasaṃyuktaṃ hikvāghnaṃ lāvaṇatrayam //
284.d:
मधुकं मधुना युक्तं विप्पलीं शर्करान्वितां /
नागरं गुडसंयुक्तं हिक्वाघ्नं लावणत्रयम् //
284.m: Licorice mixed with honey, long pepper combined with sugar, / ginger combined with jaggery, [or] the three salts: these destroy hiccups.

284.s:
kāravyajājīmaricaṃ drākṣā vṛkṣāmladāḍimam /
sauvarcalaṃ guḍaṃ kṣaudraṃ sarvārocananāśanam //
284.d:
कारव्यजाजीमरिचं द्राक्षा वृक्षाम्लदाडिमम् /
सौवर्चलं गुडं क्षौद्रं सर्वारोचननाशनम् //
284.m: Black cumin, cumin, black pepper, raisins, kokum, pomegranate, / black salt, jaggery, and honey destroy all loss of appetite.

284.s:
śṛṅgaverarasañcaiva madhunā saha pāyayet /
aruciśvāsakāśaghnaṃ pratiśyāyakaphāntakam //
284.d:
शृङ्गवेररसञ्चैव मधुना सह पाययेत् /
अरुचिश्वासकाशघ्नं प्रतिश्यायकफान्तकम् //
284.m: And one should administer fresh ginger juice along with honey; / it cures loss of appetite, asthma, and cough, and ends catarrh and kapha disorders.

284.s:
vaṭaṃ śṛṅgī śilālodhradāḍimaṃ madhukaṃ madhu /
pivet taṇḍulatoyena ccharditṛṣṇānivāraṇam //
:n
1 devadārubalārāsnātriphalāvyoṣapadmakair iti kha..
:p 51
284.d:
वटं शृङ्गी शिलालोध्रदाडिमं मधुकं मधु /
पिवेत् तण्डुलतोयेन च्छर्दितृष्णानिवारणम् //
:न्
1 देवदारुबलारास्नात्रिफलाव्योषपद्मकैर् इति ख..
:प् 51
284.m:
Banyan, śṛṅgī, red ochre, lodhra, pomegranate, licorice, and honey: / one should drink [this] with rice water; it dispels vomiting and thirst.
[Notes]
1. "devadārubalārāsnātriphalāvyoṣapadmakaiḥ" in manuscript kha. / [Page 51]

284.s:
guḍucī vāsakaṃ lodhraṃ pippalīkṣaudrasaṃyutam /
kaphānvitañjayedraktaṃ tṛṣṇākāsajvarāpaham //
284.d:
गुडुची वासकं लोध्रं पिप्पलीक्षौद्रसंयुतम् /
कफान्वितञ्जयेद्रक्तं तृष्णाकासज्वरापहम् //
284.m: Guḍūcī, vāsā, and lodhra, combined with long pepper and honey, / conquer [bleeding] accompanied by kapha and dispel thirst, cough, and fever.

284.s:
vāsakasya rasastadvat samadhustāmrajo rasaḥ /
śirīṣapuṣpasurasabhāvitaṃ maricaṃ hitaṃ //
284.d:
वासकस्य रसस्तद्वत् समधुस्ताम्रजो रसः /
शिरीषपुष्पसुरसभावितं मरिचं हितं //
284.m: Likewise, juice of vāsā, [and] ash of copper with honey; / black pepper macerated in the juice of siris flowers and holy basil is beneficial.

284.s:
sarvārtinunmasūro 'tha pittamuk taṇḍlīyakaṃ /
nirguṇḍī śārivā śelu raṅgolaś ca(1) viṣāpahaḥ //
284.d:
सर्वार्तिनुन्मसूरो ऽथ पित्तमुक् तण्ड्लीयकं /
निर्गुण्डी शारिवा शेलु रङ्गोलश् च(1) विषापहः //
284.m: Lentils remove all pain; and spiny amaranth releases pitta; / nirguṇḍī, śārivā, śelu, and aṅkoṭha remove poison.

284.s:
mahauṣadhaṃ mṛtāṃ kṣudrāṃ puṣkaraṃ(2)granthikodbhavaṃ(3) /
pivet kaṇāyutaṃ kvāthaṃ mūrchāyāñca madeṣu ca //
284.d:
महौषधं मृतां क्षुद्रां पुष्करं(2)ग्रन्थिकोद्भवं(3) /
पिवेत् कणायुतं क्वाथं मूर्छायाञ्च मदेषु च //
284.m: Ginger, guḍūcī, kaṇṭakārī, puṣkaramūla, and pippalīmūla: / one should drink the decoction mixed with pippalī in cases of fainting and intoxications.

284.s:
hiṅgusaurcalavyoṣairdviplāṃśairghṛtāḍhakaṃ(?) /
caturguṇe gavāṃ mūtre siddhamunmādanāśanaṃ //
284.d:
हिङ्गुसौर्चलव्योषैर्द्विप्लांशैर्घृताढकं(?) /
चतुर्गुणे गवां मूत्रे सिद्धमुन्मादनाशनं //
284.m: One āḍhaka of clarified butter with asafoetida, black salt, and the three pungents, two palas of each, / boiled down in four times as much cow's urine, destroys madness.

284.s:
śaṅkhapuṣpīvattākuṣṭhaiḥ siddhaṃ brāhmīrasair yutaṃ /
purāṇaṃ hantyapasmāraṃ sonmādaṃ medhyamuttamaṃ //
284.d:
शङ्खपुष्पीवत्ताकुष्ठैः सिद्धं ब्राह्मीरसैर् युतं /
पुराणं हन्त्यपस्मारं सोन्मादं मेध्यमुत्तमं //
284.m: [Ghee] prepared with śaṅkhapuṣpī, vacā, and kuṣṭha, combined with juice of brāhmī, / aged, destroys epilepsy along with insanity; it is supreme for intellect.

284.s:
pañcagavyaṃ ghṛtaṃ tadvat kuṣṭhanuccābhayāyutaṃ /
paṭolatriphalānimbaguḍucīdhāvaṇīvṛṣaiḥ //
284.d:
पञ्चगव्यं घृतं तद्वत् कुष्ठनुच्चाभयायुतं /
पटोलत्रिफलानिम्बगुडुचीधावणीवृषैः //
284.m: Clarified butter [prepared with] the five products of the cow, likewise, combined with chebulic myrobalan, cures skin diseases. / With paṭola, triphalā, neem, guḍūcī, dhāvanī, and vāsā,

284.s:
sakarañjair ghṛtaṃ siddhaṃ kuṣṭhanudvajrakaṃ smṛtaṃ /
nimbaṃ paṭolaṃ vyāghrī ca guḍūcī vāsakaṃ tathā //
284.d:
सकरञ्जैर् घृतं सिद्धं कुष्ठनुद्वज्रकं स्मृतं /
निम्बं पटोलं व्याघ्री च गुडूची वासकं तथा //
284.m: clarified butter prepared along with karañja is considered the "Vajraka" [ghee], which cures skin diseases. / Neem, paṭola, kaṇṭakārī, guḍūcī, and vāsā:

284.s:
kuryāddaśapalān bhāgān ekaikasya sakuṭṭitān /
jaladroṇe vipaktavyaṃ yāvatpādāvaśeṣitaṃ //
284.d:
कुर्याद्दशपलान् भागान् एकैकस्य सकुट्टितान् /
जलद्रोणे विपक्तव्यं यावत्पादावशेषितं //
284.m: one should make portions of ten palas of each, crushed; / it is to be boiled in a droṇa of water until one quarter remains.

284.s:
ghṛtaprasthampacettena triphalāgarbhasaṃyutaṃ(4) /
pañcatiktamiti khyātaṃ sarpiḥ kuṣṭhavināśanaṃ //
284.d:
घृतप्रस्थम्पचेत्तेन त्रिफलागर्भसंयुतं(4) /
पञ्चतिक्तमिति ख्यातं सर्पिः कुष्ठविनाशनं //
284.m: With that, one should cook a prastha of ghee containing a paste of triphalā. / This clarified butter, renowned as pañcatikta, is the destroyer of skin disease (kuṣṭha).

284.s:
aśītiṃ vātajānrogān catvāriṃśacca paittikān /
:n
1 vaṅkolaśceti kha.. , ña.. , ca
2 puṣpakamiti ja..
3 granthilodbhavamiti kha..
4 triphalāśarkarāyutamiti kha.. , ña.. ca
:p 52
viṃśatiṃ ślaiṣmikān kāsapīnasārśovraṇādikān //
284.d:
अशीतिं वातजान्रोगान् चत्वारिंशच्च पैत्तिकान् /
:न्
1 वङ्कोलश्चेति ख.. , ञ.. , च
2 पुष्पकमिति ज..
3 ग्रन्थिलोद्भवमिति ख..
4 त्रिफलाशर्करायुतमिति ख.. , ञ.. च
:प् 52
विंशतिं श्लैष्मिकान् कासपीनसार्शोव्रणादिकान् //
284.m:
Eighty diseases born of vāta, forty born of pitta,
[Notes]
1. "vaṅkolaś ca" in kha, ña, ca
2. "puṣpakam iti" in ja
3. "granthilodbhavam iti" in kha
4. "triphalāśarkarāyutam iti" in kha, ña, ca / page 52
and twenty born of phlegm (śleṣman), as well as cough, chronic catarrh, piles, ulcers, and the like—

284.s:
hantyanyān yogarajo 'yaṃ yathārkastimiraṃ khalu /
triphalāyāḥ kaṣāyena bhṛṅnarājarasena ca //
284.d:
हन्त्यन्यान् योगरजो ऽयं यथार्कस्तिमिरं खलु /
त्रिफलायाः कषायेन भृङ्नराजरसेन च //
284.m: this king of formulations truly destroys these and others, just as the sun dispels darkness. / With a decoction of triphalā and the juice of bhṛṅgarāja,

284.s:
vraṇaprakṣālanaṅkuryādupadaṃśapraśāntaye /
paṭīladalacūrṇena dāḍimatvagrajo 'tha vā //
284.d:
व्रणप्रक्षालनङ्कुर्यादुपदंशप्रशान्तये /
पटीलदलचूर्णेन दाडिमत्वग्रजो ऽथ वा //
284.m: one should wash ulcers to alleviate venereal sores (upadaṃśa); / or with powder of leaves of paṭola or powder of pomegranate bark,

284.s:
guṇḍayecca gajenāpi(1) triphalācūrṇakena ca /
triphalāyorajoyaṣṭhimārkavotpalamāricaiḥ //
284.d:
गुण्डयेच्च गजेनापि(1) त्रिफलाचूर्णकेन च /
त्रिफलायोरजोयष्ठिमार्कवोत्पलमारिचैः //
284.m: one should dust [the wound], or with gaja, or with triphalā powder. / With triphalā, iron powder, liquorice, bhṛṅgarāja, blue water-lily, and black pepper,

284.s:
samaindhavaiḥ pacettailamabhyaṅgācchardikāpahaṃ /
sakṣīrān mārkavarasān dviprasthamadhukotpalaiḥ //
284.d:
समैन्धवैः पचेत्तैलमभ्यङ्गाच्छर्दिकापहं /
सक्षीरान् मार्कवरसान् द्विप्रस्थमधुकोत्पलैः //
284.m: along with rock salt, one should cook oil; applied by massage, it cures vomiting. / With juice of bhṛṅgarāja mixed with milk, two prasthas of madhuka and blue water-lily,

284.s:
pacettu tailakuḍavaṃ tannasyaṃ palitāpahaṃ /
nimbampaṭolaṃ triphalā guḍūcī svadiraṃ vṛṣaṃ //
284.d:
पचेत्तु तैलकुडवं तन्नस्यं पलितापहं /
निम्बम्पटोलं त्रिफला गुडूची स्वदिरं वृषं //
284.m: one should cook a kuḍava of oil; used as nasal drops, it cures greying hair. / Neem, paṭola, triphalā, guḍūcī, khadira, and vāsaka,

284.s:
bhūnimbapāṭhātriphalāguḍūcīraktacandanaṃ /
yogadvayaṃ jvaraṃ hanti kuṣṭhavisphoṭakādikaṃ //
284.d:
भूनिम्बपाठात्रिफलागुडूचीरक्तचन्दनं /
योगद्वयं ज्वरं हन्ति कुष्ठविस्फोटकादिकं //
284.m: or bhūnimba, pāṭhā, triphalā, guḍūcī, and red sandalwood— / these two formulations destroy fever, skin disease (kuṣṭha), eruptions, and the like.

284.s:
paṭolāmṛtabhūnimbavāsāriṣṭakaparpaṭaiḥ /
khadirāntayutaiḥ kvātho visphoṭajvaraśāntikṛt //
284.d:
पटोलामृतभूनिम्बवासारिष्टकपर्पटैः /
खदिरान्तयुतैः क्वाथो विस्फोटज्वरशान्तिकृत् //
284.m: A decoction of paṭola, amṛtā, bhūnimba, vāsā, ariṣṭaka, and parpaṭa, / ending with khadira, brings about the alleviation of eruptions and fever.

284.s:
daśamūlī cchinnaruhā pathyā dāru punarnavā /
jvaravidradhiśotheṣu śigruviśvajitā hitāḥ //
284.d:
दशमूली च्छिन्नरुहा पथ्या दारु पुनर्नवा /
ज्वरविद्रधिशोथेषु शिग्रुविश्वजिता हिताः //
284.m: Daśamūlī, chinnaruhā, pathyā, devadāru, and punarnavā, / along with śigru and viśvabheṣaja, are beneficial in fever, abscesses, and swellings.

284.s:
madhūkaṃ nimbapatrāṇi lepaḥ syadvraṇaśodhanaḥ /
triphalā khadiro dārvī nyagrodhātibalākuśāḥ //
284.d:
मधूकं निम्बपत्राणि लेपः स्यद्व्रणशोधनः /
त्रिफला खदिरो दार्वी न्यग्रोधातिबलाकुशाः //
284.m: A paste of madhūka and neem leaves cleanses ulcers. / Triphalā, khadira, dārvī, banyan, atibalā, and kuśa grass,

284.s:
nimbamūlakapatrāṇāṃ kaṣāyāḥ śodhane hitāḥ /
karañjāriṣṭanirguṇḍīraso hanyādvraṇakramīn //
:n
1 guṇḍayennagajenāpīti kha.. , ña.. ca
:p 53
284.d:
निम्बमूलकपत्राणां कषायाः शोधने हिताः /
करञ्जारिष्टनिर्गुण्डीरसो हन्याद्व्रणक्रमीन् //
:न्
1 गुण्डयेन्नगजेनापीति ख.. , ञ.. च
:प् 53
284.m:
decoctions of neem root and leaves are beneficial for cleansing. / The juice of karañja, ariṣṭa, and nirguṇḍī destroys maggots in ulcers.
[Notes]
1. "guṇḍayennagajenāpīti" in kha, ña, ca / page 53

284.s:
dhātakicandanabalāsamaṅgāmadhukotpalaiḥ /
dārvīmedonvitair lepaḥ samarpirvraṇaropaṇaḥ //
284.d:
धातकिचन्दनबलासमङ्गामधुकोत्पलैः /
दार्वीमेदोन्वितैर् लेपः समर्पिर्व्रणरोपणः //
284.m: A paste made with dhātakī, sandalwood, balā, samaṅgā, madhuka, blue water-lily, / dārvī, and medā, combined with clarified butter, heals ulcers.

284.s:
guggulutriphalāvyoṣasamāṃrśair ghṛtayogataḥ /
nāḍī duṣṭavraṇaṃ śūlambhagandaramukhaṃ haret //
284.d:
गुग्गुलुत्रिफलाव्योषसमांर्शैर् घृतयोगतः /
नाडी दुष्टव्रणं शूलम्भगन्दरमुखं हरेत् //
284.m: Guggulu, triphalā, and vyoṣa in equal parts, combined with ghee, / will cure sinus tract (nāḍī), malignant ulcers, colic, and fistula-in-ano.

284.s:
haritakīṃ mūtrasiddhāṃ satailalavaṇānvitāṃ /
prātaḥ prātaś ca seveta kaphavātāmayāpahāṃ(1) //
284.d:
हरितकीं मूत्रसिद्धां सतैललवणान्वितां /
प्रातः प्रातश् च सेवेत कफवातामयापहां(1) //
284.m: One should consume every morning harītakī cooked in urine, / combined with oil and salt; it dispels diseases of kapha and vāta.

284.s:
trikaṭutriphalākvāthaṃ(2) sakṣāralavaṇaṃ pivet /
kaphavātātmakeṣveva virekaḥ kaphavṛddhinut //
284.d:
त्रिकटुत्रिफलाक्वाथं(2) सक्षारलवणं पिवेत् /
कफवातात्मकेष्वेव विरेकः कफवृद्धिनुत् //
284.m: One should drink a decoction of trikaṭu and triphalā with alkali and salt; / it is a purgative in conditions of kapha and vāta that removes increases in kapha.

284.s:
pappalīpippalīmūlavacācitrakanāgaraiḥ /
kvāthitaṃ vā pivetpeyamāmavātavināśanaṃ //
284.d:
पप्पलीपिप्पलीमूलवचाचित्रकनागरैः /
क्वाथितं वा पिवेत्पेयमामवातविनाशनं //
284.m: Or one should drink a draught decocted with long pepper, root of long pepper, / vacā, citraka, and dry ginger, which destroys rheumatoid conditions (āmavāta).

284.s:
rāsnāṃ guḍucīmeraṇḍadevadārumahauṣadhaṃ /
pivet sarvāṅgike vāte sāme sandhyasthimajjage //
284.d:
रास्नां गुडुचीमेरण्डदेवदारुमहौषधं /
पिवेत् सर्वाङ्गिके वाते सामे सन्ध्यस्थिमज्जगे //
284.m: One should drink rāsnā, guḍūcī, castor, devadāru, and dry ginger / in vāta affecting all limbs, accompanied by āma, and located in joints, bones, and marrow.

284.s:
daśamūlakaśāyaṃ vā piveddhā nāgarāmbhasā /
śuṇṭhīgokṣurakakvāthaḥ prātaḥ prātir niṣevitaḥ //
284.d:
दशमूलकशायं वा पिवेद्धा नागराम्भसा /
शुण्ठीगोक्षुरकक्वाथः प्रातः प्रातिर् निषेवितः //
284.m: Or one should drink a decoction of daśamūla, or drink it with ginger-water. / A decoction of dry ginger and gokṣura taken every morning

284.s:
sāmavātakaṭīśūlapācano rukpraṇāśanaḥ /
samūlapatraśākhāyāḥ prasāraṇyāś ca tailakaṃ //
284.d:
सामवातकटीशूलपाचनो रुक्प्रणाशनः /
समूलपत्रशाखायाः प्रसारण्याश् च तैलकं //
284.m: digests āmavāta and lumbar colic, and destroys pain. / Oil prepared from the roots, leaves, and branches of prasāraṇī,

284.s:
guḍucyāḥ surasaḥ kalkaḥ cūrṇaṃ vā kvāthameva ca /
prabhūtakālamāsevya mucyate vātaśoṇitāt //
284.d:
गुडुच्याः सुरसः कल्कः चूर्णं वा क्वाथमेव च /
प्रभूतकालमासेव्य मुच्यते वातशोणितात् //
284.m: or the fresh juice, paste, powder, or decoction of guḍūcī, / taken for a long time, frees one from gout (vātaśoṇita).

284.s:
pippalī vardhamānaṃ vā sevyaṃ pathyā guḍena vā /
paṭolatriphalātīvrakaṭukāsṛtasādhitaṃ(3) //
284.d:
पिप्पली वर्धमानं वा सेव्यं पथ्या गुडेन वा /
पटोलत्रिफलातीव्रकटुकासृतसाधितं(3) //
284.m: Or an increasing dose of long pepper should be taken, or pathyā with jaggery. / Prepared with paṭola, triphalā, intense kaṭukā, and asṛt,

284.s:
pakvaṃ pītvā jayatyāśu sadāhaṃ vātaśoṇitaṃ /
:n
1 kaphavātavināśinīmiti ja..
2 trikaṭutriphalākuṣṭhamiti ña..
3 paṭolatriphalābhirukaṭukāmṛtasādhitamiti kha.. , cha.. , ña.. ca
:p 54
guggulaṃ koṣṇaśīte(1) tu guḍucī triphalāmbhasā //
284.d:
पक्वं पीत्वा जयत्याशु सदाहं वातशोणितं /
:न्
1 कफवातविनाशिनीमिति ज..
2 त्रिकटुत्रिफलाकुष्ठमिति ञ..
3 पटोलत्रिफलाभिरुकटुकामृतसाधितमिति ख.. , छ.. , ञ.. च
:प् 54
गुग्गुलं कोष्णशीते(1) तु गुडुची त्रिफलाम्भसा //
284.m:
boiled and drunk, it quickly overcomes vātaśoṇita accompanied by burning sensations.
[Notes]
1. "kaphavātavināśinīm iti" in ja
2. "trikaṭutriphalākuṣṭham iti" in ña
3. "paṭolatriphalābhirukaṭukāmṛtasādhitam iti" in kha, cha, ña, ca / page 54
Guggulu with lukewarm or cold water, or with water of guḍūcī and triphalā,

284.s:
balāpunar navair aṇḍavṛhatīdvayagokṣuraiḥ /
sahiṅgu lavanaiḥ pītaṃ sadyo vātarujāpahaṃ //
284.d:
बलापुनर् नवैर् अण्डवृहतीद्वयगोक्षुरैः /
सहिङ्गु लवनैः पीतं सद्यो वातरुजापहं //
284.m: or drunk with balā, punarnavā, castor, the two bṛhatīs, and gokṣura, / along with asafoetida and salts, immediately dispels pain from vāta.

284.s:
kārṣikaṃ pippalīmūlaṃ pañcaiva lavaṇāni ca /
pippalī citrakaṃ śuṇṭhī triphalā trivṛtā vacā //
284.d:
कार्षिकं पिप्पलीमूलं पञ्चैव लवणानि च /
पिप्पली चित्रकं शुण्ठी त्रिफला त्रिवृता वचा //
284.m: A karṣa each of long pepper root, the five salts, / long pepper, citraka, dry ginger, triphalā, trivṛt, and vacā,

284.s:
dvau kṣārau śādvalā dantī svarṇakṣīrī viṣāṇikā /
kolapramāṇāṃ guṭikāṃ pivet sauvīrakāyutāṃ //
284.d:
द्वौ क्षारौ शाद्वला दन्ती स्वर्णक्षीरी विषाणिका /
कोलप्रमाणां गुटिकां पिवेत् सौवीरकायुतां //
284.m: the two alkalis, śādvalā, dantī, svarṇakṣīrī, and viṣāṇikā— / one should drink a pill the size of a jujube berry taken with sauvīraka vinegar.

284.s:
śothāvapāke trivṛtā pravṛddhe codarādike /
kṣīraṃ śothaharaṃ dāru varṣābhūrnāgaraiḥ śubham //
284.d:
शोथावपाके त्रिवृता प्रवृद्धे चोदरादिके /
क्षीरं शोथहरं दारु वर्षाभूर्नागरैः शुभम् //
284.m: Trivṛt is beneficial in the suppurative stage of swelling, and when abdominal enlargement or the like is advanced. / Milk prepared with devadāru, varṣābhū, and dry ginger is auspicious and removes swelling.

284.s:
sekas tathārkavarṣābhūnimbakvāthena śothajit /
vyoṣagarbhaṃ palāśasya triguṇe bhasmavāriṇi //
284.d:
सेकस् तथार्कवर्षाभूनिम्बक्वाथेन शोथजित् /
व्योषगर्भं पलाशस्य त्रिगुणे भस्मवारिणि //
284.m: Likewise, affusion with a decoction of arka, varṣābhū, and neem overcomes swelling. / Clarified butter prepared with vyoṣa inside, cooked in thrice the amount

284.s:
sādhitaṃ pivataḥ sarpiḥ patatyarśo na saṃśayaḥ /
viśvaksenāvanirguṇḍīsādhitaṃ cāpi lāvaṇaṃ //
284.d:
साधितं पिवतः सर्पिः पतत्यर्शो न संशयः /
विश्वक्सेनावनिर्गुण्डीसाधितं चापि लावणं //
284.m: of ash-water of palāśa—for one drinking it, piles fall off without doubt. / Also salt prepared with viśvaksenā and nirguṇḍī,

284.s:
viḍaṅgānalasindhūttharāsnāgrakṣāradārubhiḥ /
tailañcaturguṇaṃ siddhaṃ kaṭudravyaṃ jalena vā //
284.d:
विडङ्गानलसिन्धूत्थरास्नाग्रक्षारदारुभिः /
तैलञ्चतुर्गुणं सिद्धं कटुद्रव्यं जलेन वा //
284.m: or pungent substances with viḍaṅga, citraka, rock salt, rāsnā, agrakṣāra, / and devadāru cooked in four times the amount of oil, or with water,

284.s:
gaṇḍamālāpahaṃ tailamabhyaṅgāt galagaṇḍanut /
śaṭīkunāgabalayakvāthaḥ kṣīrarase yutam //
284.d:
गण्डमालापहं तैलमभ्यङ्गात् गलगण्डनुत् /
शटीकुनागबलयक्वाथः क्षीररसे युतम् //
284.m: is an oil that removes cervical adenitis (gaṇḍamālā); through massage, it cures goitre. / A decoction of śaṭī, kunāga, and balā, combined with milk and meat soup,

284.s:
payasyāpippalīvāsākalkaṃ siddhaṃ kṣaye hitam /
vacāviḍabhayāśuṇṭhīhiṅgukuṣṭhāgnidīpyakān //
284.d:
पयस्यापिप्पलीवासाकल्कं सिद्धं क्षये हितम् /
वचाविडभयाशुण्ठीहिङ्गुकुष्ठाग्निदीप्यकान् //
284.m: prepared with a paste of payasyā, long pepper, and vāsā, is beneficial in wasting. / Vacā, black salt, abhayā, dry ginger, asafoetida, kuṣṭha, citraka, and carom seeds,

284.s:
dvitriṣaṭcaturekāṃśasaptapañcāśikāḥ kramāt /
cūrṇaṃ pītaṃ hanti gulmaṃ udaraṃ śūlakāsanut //
284.d:
द्वित्रिषट्चतुरेकांशसप्तपञ्चाशिकाः क्रमात् /
चूर्णं पीतं हन्ति गुल्मं उदरं शूलकासनुत् //
284.m: in two, three, six, four, one, seven, and five parts respectively— / the powder drunk destroys abdominal tumors (gulma) and enlargement, and cures colic and cough.

284.s:
pāṭhānikumbhatrikaṭutriphalāgniṣu sādhitam /
:n
1 ktoṣṭuśīte 'theti kha..
:p 55
mūtreṇa cūrṇaguṭikā gulmaplīhādimardanī //
284.d:
पाठानिकुम्भत्रिकटुत्रिफलाग्निषु साधितम् /
:न्
1 क्तोष्टुशीते ऽथेति ख..
:प् 55
मूत्रेण चूर्णगुटिका गुल्मप्लीहादिमर्दनी //
284.m:
Cooked with pāṭhā, nikumbha, trikaṭu, triphalā, and citraka,
[Notes]
1. "ktoṣṭuśīte 'theti" in kha / page 55
a powder or pill taken with urine crushes abdominal tumors (gulma), spleen diseases, and the like.

284.s:
vāsānimbapaṭīlāni triphalā vātapittanut(1) /
lihyāt kṣaudreṇa viḍaṅgaṃ cūrṇaṃ kṛmivināśanam //
284.d:
वासानिम्बपटीलानि त्रिफला वातपित्तनुत्(1) /
लिह्यात् क्षौद्रेण विडङ्गं चूर्णं कृमिविनाशनम् //
284.m: Vāsā, neem, and paṭola with triphalā remove vāta and pitta. / One should lick viḍaṅga powder with honey to destroy parasites.

284.s:
viḍaṅgasaindhavakṣāramūtrenāpi harītakī /
śallakīvadarījambupiyālāmrārjunatvacaḥ //
284.d:
विडङ्गसैन्धवक्षारमूत्रेनापि हरीतकी /
शल्लकीवदरीजम्बुपियालाम्रार्जुनत्वचः //
284.m: Harītakī with viḍaṅga, rock salt, and alkali, or with urine; / barks of śallakī, vadarī, jambu, piyāla, mango, and arjuna,

284.s:
pītāḥ kṣīreṇa madhvaktāḥ pṛthakśīṇitavāraṇāḥ /
vilvāmraghātakīpāṭhāśuṇṭhīmocarasāḥ samāḥ //
284.d:
पीताः क्षीरेण मध्वक्ताः पृथक्शीणितवारणाः /
विल्वाम्रघातकीपाठाशुण्ठीमोचरसाः समाः //
284.m: drunk individually with milk and smeared with honey, arrest bleeding. / Equal parts of vilva, mango, dhātakī, pāṭhā, dry ginger, and mocārasa,

284.s:
pītā rundhantyatīsāraṃ guḍatakreṇa durjayam /
cāṅgerīkoladadhyambunāgarakṣārasaṃyutam //
284.d:
पीता रुन्धन्त्यतीसारं गुडतक्रेण दुर्जयम् /
चाङ्गेरीकोलदध्यम्बुनागरक्षारसंयुतम् //
284.m: drunk with jaggery and buttermilk, check obstinate diarrhoea. / Combined with cāṅgerī, jujube fruit, curd-water, dry ginger, and alkali,

284.s:
ghṛtayukkvāthitaṃ peyaṃ gudaṃbhrase rujāpaham /
viḍaṅgātiviṣāmustaṃ dārupāthākaliṅgakam //
284.d:
घृतयुक्क्वाथितं पेयं गुदंभ्रसे रुजापहम् /
विडङ्गातिविषामुस्तं दारुपाथाकलिङ्गकम् //
284.m: a decocted potion mixed with ghee relieves pain in prolapse of the rectum. / Viḍaṅga, ativiṣā, mustā, devadāru, pāṭhā, and holarrhena seeds,

284.s:
marīcena samāyuktaṃ śothātīsāranāśanam /
śarkarāsindhuśuṇṭhībhiḥ kṛṣṇāmadhuguḍena vā //
284.d:
मरीचेन समायुक्तं शोथातीसारनाशनम् /
शर्करासिन्धुशुण्ठीभिः कृष्णामधुगुडेन वा //
284.m: combined with black pepper, destroy swellings and diarrhoea. / With sugar, rock salt, and dry ginger, or with long pepper, honey, and jaggery,

284.s:
dve dve khādeddharītakyau jīvedvarṣaśataṃ sukhī /
triphalā pippalīyuktā samdhvājyā tathaiva sā //
284.d:
द्वे द्वे खादेद्धरीतक्यौ जीवेद्वर्षशतं सुखी /
त्रिफला पिप्पलीयुक्ता सम्ध्वाज्या तथैव सा //
284.m: one should eat two harītakī fruits each time; one will live happily for a hundred years. / Likewise triphalā combined with long pepper, honey, and clarified butter.

284.s:
cūrnamāmalakaṃ tena surasena tu bhavitam /
madhvājyaśarkarāyuktaṃ liḍhvā strīśaḥ payaḥ pivet //
284.d:
चूर्नमामलकं तेन सुरसेन तु भवितम् /
मध्वाज्यशर्करायुक्तं लिढ्वा स्त्रीशः पयः पिवेत् //
284.m: Powder of āmalaka macerated with its own fresh juice, / licked with honey, clarified butter, and sugar, makes one master over women; one should then drink milk.

284.s:
māsapippaliśālīnāṃ yavagodhūmayos tathā /
cūrṇabhāgaiḥ samāṃśaiś ca pacet pippalīkāṃ śubhāṃ //
284.d:
मासपिप्पलिशालीनां यवगोधूमयोस् तथा /
चूर्णभागैः समांशैश् च पचेत् पिप्पलीकां शुभां //
284.m: With equal parts of flour of black gram, long pepper, rice, / barley, and wheat, one should prepare a wholesome cake.

284.s:
tāṃ bhakṣayitvā ca pivet śarkarāmadhuraṃ payaḥ /
navaś caṭakavajjambhed daśavārān striyaṃ dhruvam //
284.d:
तां भक्षयित्वा च पिवेत् शर्करामधुरं पयः /
नवश् चटकवज्जम्भेद् दशवारान् स्त्रियं ध्रुवम् //
284.m: Having eaten it, one should drink milk sweetened with sugar; / like a young sparrow, he will certainly copulate ten times with a woman.

284.s:
samaṅgādhātakīpuṣpalodhranīlotpalāni ca /
:n
1 tripalā cāmlapittanuditi kha.. , ña.. ca
:p 56
etat kṣīrena dātavyaṃ strīṇāṃ pradaranaśanaṃ //
284.d:
समङ्गाधातकीपुष्पलोध्रनीलोत्पलानि च /
:न्
1 त्रिपला चाम्लपित्तनुदिति ख.. , ञ.. च
:प् 56
एतत् क्षीरेन दातव्यं स्त्रीणां प्रदरनशनं //
284.m:
Samaṅgā, dhātakī flowers, lodhra, and blue water lily—
[Footnote]
1. "Triphalā cures acid dyspepsia" in Kha and Ña.
[Page 56]
this should be administered with milk to women to destroy menorrhagia.

284.s:
vījaṅkauraṇṭakañcāpi madhukaṃ śvetacandanaṃ /
padmotpalasya mūlāni madhukaṃ śarkarātilān //
284.d:
वीजङ्कौरण्टकञ्चापि मधुकं श्वेतचन्दनं /
पद्मोत्पलस्य मूलानि मधुकं शर्करातिलान् //
284.m:
Seeds of kuraṇṭaka, madhuka, white sandalwood,
roots of lotus and blue water lily, licorice, sugar, and sesame seeds

284.s:
dravamāṇeṣu garbheṣu garbhasyāpanamuttamaṃ /
devadāru nabhaḥ kuṣṭhaṃ(1) naladaṃ viśvabheṣajaṃ //
284.d:
द्रवमाणेषु गर्भेषु गर्भस्यापनमुत्तमं /
देवदारु नभः कुष्ठं(1) नलदं विश्वभेषजं //
284.m:
provide the best stabilization of the fetus when the embryo is slipping away.
Devadāru, nabhas, kuṣṭha, spikenard, and dry ginger,

284.s:
lepaḥ kāñcikamampaṣṭastailayuktaḥ śirortinut /
vastrapūtaṃ kṣipet koṣṇaṃ mindhūtyaṃ karṇaśūlanut //
284.d:
लेपः काञ्चिकमम्पष्टस्तैलयुक्तः शिरोर्तिनुत् /
वस्त्रपूतं क्षिपेत् कोष्णं मिन्धूत्यं कर्णशूलनुत् //
284.m:
applied as a paste with fermented sour gruel and ambaṣṭhā, combined with oil, relieves headache.
Warm rock-salt water filtered through cloth and dropped [into the ear] relieves earache.

284.s:
laśunārdrakaśigrūṇāṃ kadalyā vā rasaḥpṛthak /
balāśatāvarīrāsnāmṛtāḥ mairīyakeḥ pivet //
284.d:
लशुनार्द्रकशिग्रूणां कदल्या वा रसःपृथक् /
बलाशतावरीरास्नामृताः मैरीयकेः पिवेत् //
284.m:
The separate juices of garlic, ginger, and śigru, or of banana, [relieve earache].
One should drink balā, śatāvarī, rāsnā, and amṛtā, or with mairīyaka wine;

284.s:
triphalāsahitaṃ sarpistimiraghnamanuttamaṃ /
triphalāvyoṣasindhūptyair ghṛtaṃ siddhaṃ pivennaraḥ //
284.d:
त्रिफलासहितं सर्पिस्तिमिरघ्नमनुत्तमं /
त्रिफलाव्योषसिन्धूप्त्यैर् घृतं सिद्धं पिवेन्नरः //
284.m:
ghee along with triphalā is unsurpassed in destroying cataracts.
A man should drink ghee prepared with triphalā, the three pungents, and rock salt;

284.s:
cākṣuṣyambhedanaṃ hṛdyaṃ(2) dīpanaṃ krapharoganut /
nīlotpalasya kiñjalkaṃ gośakṛdrasasaṃyutaṃ //
284.d:
चाक्षुष्यम्भेदनं हृद्यं(2) दीपनं क्रफरोगनुत् /
नीलोत्पलस्य किञ्जल्कं गोशकृद्रससंयुतं //
284.m:
it is beneficial to the eyes, purgative, pleasing to the heart, digestive, and relieves phlegm disorders.
The filaments of a blue water lily mixed with the juice of cow dung,

284.s:
guṭikāñjanametat syāt dinarātryandhayorhitaṃ /
yaṣṭīmadhuvacākṛṣṇāvījānāṃ kuṭajasya ca //
284.d:
गुटिकाञ्जनमेतत् स्यात् दिनरात्र्यन्धयोर्हितं /
यष्टीमधुवचाकृष्णावीजानां कुटजस्य च //
284.m:
formed into a pill for collyrium, is beneficial for day-blindness and night-blindness.
With a paste of licorice, vacā, black pepper, and seeds of kuṭaja,

284.s:
kalkenāloḍya nimbasya kaṣāyo vamanāya saḥ /
snigdhasvinnayavantoyaṃ pradātavyaṃ virecanam //
284.d:
कल्केनालोड्य निम्बस्य कषायो वमनाय सः /
स्निग्धस्विन्नयवन्तोयं प्रदातव्यं विरेचनम् //
284.m:
stirred into a decoction of neem, [the formulation] serves to induce vomiting.
To one who has been lubricated and sweated, purgative barley-water should be administered.

284.s:
anyathā yojitaṃ kuryāt mandāgniṃ gauravāruciṃ /
pathyāsaindhavakṛṣṇānāṃ(3) cūrṇamuṣṇāmbunā pivet //
284.d:
अन्यथा योजितं कुर्यात् मन्दाग्निं गौरवारुचिं /
पथ्यासैन्धवकृष्णानां(3) चूर्णमुष्णाम्बुना पिवेत् //
284.m:
Applied otherwise, it causes sluggish digestion, heaviness, and loss of appetite.
One should drink the powder of harītakī, rock salt, and pippalī with hot water;

284.s:
virekaḥ sarvarogaghnaḥ śreṣṭho nārācasaṃjñakaḥ /
:n
1 kṛṣṇamiti kha..
2 kuṣṭhamiti ña..
3 pathyāsaindhavakuṣṭhānāmiti kha..
:p 57
siddhayogā munibhyo ye ātreyeṇa pradarśitāḥ /
sarvarogaharāḥ sarvayogāgryāḥ suśrutena hi //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe mṛtasañjīvanīkarasiddhayogo nāma
caturaśītyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:ś atha pañcāśītyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
kalpasāgaraḥ
284.d:
विरेकः सर्वरोगघ्नः श्रेष्ठो नाराचसंज्ञकः /
:न्
1 कृष्णमिति ख..
2 कुष्ठमिति ञ..
3 पथ्यासैन्धवकुष्ठानामिति ख..
:प् 57
सिद्धयोगा मुनिभ्यो ये आत्रेयेण प्रदर्शिताः /
सर्वरोगहराः सर्वयोगाग्र्याः सुश्रुतेन हि //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे मृतसञ्जीवनीकरसिद्धयोगो नाम
चतुरशीत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
:श् अथ पञ्चाशीत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
कल्पसागरः
284.m:
this purgative called Nārāca is superior and destroys all diseases.
[Footnote]
1. "kṛṣṇam" in Kha.
2. "kuṣṭham" in Ña.
3. "pathyāsaindhavakuṣṭhānām" in Kha.
[Page 57]
These proven formulations, shown to the sages by Ātreya,
destroy all diseases and are the foremost among all formulations [recorded] by Suśruta.
Thus in the great Āgneya Purāṇa, the two hundred and eighty-fourth chapter, entitled "Proven Formulations Reviving the Dead."
Now the two hundred and eighty-fifth chapter.
Ocean of Rejuvenation

285.s:
dhanvantarir uvāca
kalpāmmṛtyuñcayānvakṣye hy āyurdānrogasardanān /
triśatī rogahā sevyā madhvājyatriphalāmṛtā //
285.d:
धन्वन्तरिर् उवाच
कल्पाम्मृत्युञ्चयान्वक्ष्ये ह्य् आयुर्दान्रोगसर्दनान् /
त्रिशती रोगहा सेव्या मध्वाज्यत्रिफलामृता //
285.m:
Dhanvantari said:
I shall proclaim the rejuvenating recipes that conquer death, bestow long life, and destroy diseases.
Triphalā and guḍūcī taken with honey and ghee destroys disease and grants three hundred years of life.

285.s:
palaṃ palārdhaṃ karṣaṃ vā triphalāṃ sakalāṃ tathā /
bilvatailasya nasyañca māsaṃ pañcaśatī kaviḥ //
285.d:
पलं पलार्धं कर्षं वा त्रिफलां सकलां तथा /
बिल्वतैलस्य नस्यञ्च मासं पञ्चशती कविः //
285.m:
One pala, half a pala, or a karṣa of the complete triphalā,
and nasal therapy of bilva oil for a month, makes one a wise poet living five hundred years.

285.s:
rogāpamṛtyubalijit tilaṃ(1) bhallātakaṃ tathā /
pañcāṅgaṃ vākūcīcūṇaṃ ṣaṇmāsaṃ khadirodakaiḥ //
285.d:
रोगापमृत्युबलिजित् तिलं(1) भल्लातकं तथा /
पञ्चाङ्गं वाकूचीचूणं षण्मासं खदिरोदकैः //
285.m:
Sesame, bhallātaka, and powder of the five parts of bākucī
conquer disease, untimely death, and wrinkles when taken for six months with water decoctions of khadira.

285.s:
kvāthaiḥ kuṣṭhañjayet sevyaṃ cūrṇaṃ nīlakuruṇṭajam /
kṣireṇa madhunā vāpi śatāyuḥ khaṇḍadugdhabhuk //
285.d:
क्वाथैः कुष्ठञ्जयेत् सेव्यं चूर्णं नीलकुरुण्टजम् /
क्षिरेण मधुना वापि शतायुः खण्डदुग्धभुक् //
285.m:
Through decoctions one conquers leprosy. Powder from blue kuruṇṭaka, taken regularly
with milk or honey, makes one live a hundred years, eating sugar and milk.

285.s:
madhvājyaśuṇṭhīṃ saṃsevya palaṃ prātaḥ samṛdyujit /
balīpalitajijjīvenmāṇḍakīcūrṇadugdhapāḥ //
285.d:
मध्वाज्यशुण्ठीं संसेव्य पलं प्रातः समृद्युजित् /
बलीपलितजिज्जीवेन्माण्डकीचूर्णदुग्धपाः //
285.m:
Having taken a pala of ginger with honey and ghee in the morning, one conquers death.
Drinking milk with powder of māṇḍakī, one conquers wrinkles and gray hair and lives long.

285.s:
uccaṭāmadhunā karṣaṃ payaḥpā mṛtyujinnaraḥ /
madhvājyaiḥ payasā vāpi nirguṇḍī rogamṛtyujit //
:n
1 tailamiti ña..
:p 58
285.d:
उच्चटामधुना कर्षं पयःपा मृत्युजिन्नरः /
मध्वाज्यैः पयसा वापि निर्गुण्डी रोगमृत्युजित् //
:न्
1 तैलमिति ञ..
:प् 58
285.m:
Drinking milk with a karṣa of uccaṭā and honey, a man conquers death.
Nirguṇḍī taken with honey and ghee, or with milk, conquers disease and death.
[Footnote]
1. "tailam" in Ña.
[Page 58]

285.s:
palāśatailaṃ karṣaikaṃ ṣaṇmāsaṃ madhunā pivet /
dugdhabhojī pañcaśatī sahasrāyurbhavennaraḥ //
285.d:
पलाशतैलं कर्षैकं षण्मासं मधुना पिवेत् /
दुग्धभोजी पञ्चशती सहस्रायुर्भवेन्नरः //
285.m:
One should drink one karṣa of palāśa oil with honey for six months;
eating a diet of milk, a man lives for five hundred or a thousand years.

285.s:
jyotiṣmatīpatrarasaṃ payasā triphalāṃ pivet /
madhunājyantatastadvat śatāvaryā rajaḥ palaṃ //
285.d:
ज्योतिष्मतीपत्ररसं पयसा त्रिफलां पिवेत् /
मधुनाज्यन्ततस्तद्वत् शतावर्या रजः पलं //
285.m:
One should drink juice of jyotiṣmatī leaves, or triphalā with milk;
likewise, honey and ghee with a pala of powdered śatāvarī.

285.s:
kṣaudrājyaiḥ payasā vāpi nirguṇḍī rogamṛtyujit /
pañcāṅgaṃ nimbacūrṇasya khadirakvāthabhāvitaṃ //
285.d:
क्षौद्राज्यैः पयसा वापि निर्गुण्डी रोगमृत्युजित् /
पञ्चाङ्गं निम्बचूर्णस्य खदिरक्वाथभावितं //
285.m:
Nirguṇḍī taken with honey and ghee, or with milk, conquers disease and death.
The powder of the five parts of neem, macerated with a decoction of khadira,

285.s:
karṣaṃ bhṛṅgarasenāpi rogajiccāmaro(1) bhavet /
rudantikājyamadhubhuk dugdhabhojī ca mṛtyujit //
285.d:
कर्षं भृङ्गरसेनापि रोगजिच्चामरो(1) भवेत् /
रुदन्तिकाज्यमधुभुक् दुग्धभोजी च मृत्युजित् //
285.m:
[taken in the measure of] a karṣa with the juice of bhṛṅgarāja, conquers disease and makes one immortal.
Eating rudantikā with ghee and honey, subsisting on milk, one conquers death.

285.s:
karṣacūrṇaṃ harītakyā bhāvitaṃ bhṛṅgarāḍrasaiḥ /
ghṛtena madhunā sevya triśatāyuś ca rogajit //
285.d:
कर्षचूर्णं हरीतक्या भावितं भृङ्गराड्रसैः /
घृतेन मधुना सेव्य त्रिशतायुश् च रोगजित् //
285.m:
A karṣa of harītakī powder, macerated with juices of bhṛṅgarāja,
to be taken with ghee and honey, grants three hundred years of life and conquers disease.

285.s:
vārāhikā bhṛṅgarasaṃ lohacūrṇaṃ śatāvarī /
sājyaṃ karṣaṃ(2) pañcaśatī kartacūrṇaṃ śatāvarī //
285.d:
वाराहिका भृङ्गरसं लोहचूर्णं शतावरी /
साज्यं कर्षं(2) पञ्चशती कर्तचूर्णं शतावरी //
285.m:
Vārāhī, bhṛṅgarāja juice, iron powder, and śatāvarī,
taken with ghee in a karṣa dose, grants five hundred years. Powder of […] and śatāvarī,

285.s:
bhāvitaṃ bhṛṅgarājena madhvājyantriśatī bhavet /
tāmraṃ mṛtaṃ(3) sṛtatulyaṃ(4) gandhakañca kumārikā //
285.d:
भावितं भृङ्गराजेन मध्वाज्यन्त्रिशती भवेत् /
ताम्रं मृतं(3) सृततुल्यं(4) गन्धकञ्च कुमारिका //
285.m:
macerated with bhṛṅgarāja, taken with honey and ghee, grants three hundred years.
Calcined copper, equal parts of purified mercury and sulphur, ground with aloe vera

285.s:
rasair vimṛjya dve guñje sājyaṃ pañcaśatābdavān /
aśvagandhā palaṃ tailaṃ sājyaṃ khaṇḍaṃ śatābdavān //
285.d:
रसैर् विमृज्य द्वे गुञ्जे साज्यं पञ्चशताब्दवान् /
अश्वगन्धा पलं तैलं साज्यं खण्डं शताब्दवान् //
285.m:
juices, taken in the amount of two guñjās with ghee, makes one live five hundred years.
A pala of aśvagandhā in oil, taken with ghee and candied sugar, makes one live a hundred years.

285.s:
palampunar navācūrṇaṃ madhvājyapayasā pivam /
aśokacūrṇasya palaṃ madhvājyaṃ payasārtinut //
285.d:
पलम्पुनर् नवाचूर्णं मध्वाज्यपयसा पिवम् /
अशोकचूर्णस्य पलं मध्वाज्यं पयसार्तिनुत् //
285.m:
Drinking a pala of punarnavā powder with honey, ghee, and milk, [one lives long];
a pala of aśoka powder with honey, ghee, and milk relieves suffering.

285.s:
tilasya tailaṃ samadhu nasyāt kṛṣṇakacaḥ śatī /
karṣamakṣaṃ samadhvājyaṃ śatāyuḥ payasā pivan //
:n
1 roganuccāmaro bhavediti ña..
2 sājyaṃ sarvamiti kha..
3 tāmrāmṛtamiti kha..
4 suratusyamiti ja.. , ña.. ca
:p 59
285.d:
तिलस्य तैलं समधु नस्यात् कृष्णकचः शती /
कर्षमक्षं समध्वाज्यं शतायुः पयसा पिवन् //
:न्
1 रोगनुच्चामरो भवेदिति ञ..
2 साज्यं सर्वमिति ख..
3 ताम्रामृतमिति ख..
4 सुरतुस्यमिति ज.. , ञ.. च
:प् 59
285.m:
Sesame oil with honey used as nasal drops makes the hair black for a hundred years.
Drinking a karṣa of bibhītaka with honey, ghee, and milk, one lives a hundred years.
[Footnote]
1. "roganuccāmaro bhavet" in Ña.
2. "sājyaṃ sarvam" in Kha.
3. "tāmrāmṛtam" in Kha.
4. "suratusyam" in Ja and Ña.
[Page 59]

285.s:
abhayaṃ saguḍañcagdhvā ghṛtena madhurādibhiḥ /
dugdhānnabhuk kṛṣṇakeśo 'rogī pañcaśatābdavān //
285.d:
अभयं सगुडञ्चग्ध्वा घृतेन मधुरादिभिः /
दुग्धान्नभुक् कृष्णकेशो ऽरोगी पञ्चशताब्दवान् //
285.m:
Having consumed harītakī with jaggery, ghee, sweets, and the like,
eating milk and rice, one becomes free of disease with black hair, living for five hundred years.

285.s:
palaṅkuṣmāṇḍikācūrṇaṃ madhvājyapayasā pivan /
māsaṃ dugdhānnabhojī ca sahasrāyurvirogavān //
285.d:
पलङ्कुष्माण्डिकाचूर्णं मध्वाज्यपयसा पिवन् /
मासं दुग्धान्नभोजी च सहस्रायुर्विरोगवान् //
285.m:
Drinking a pala of kuṣmāṇḍikā powder with honey, ghee, and milk,
and consuming a diet of milk and rice for a month, one lives a thousand years, free of disease.

285.s:
śālūkacūrṇaṃ bhṛṅgājyaṃ samadhvājyaṃ śatābdakṛt /
kaṭutumbītailanasyaṃ karṣaṃ śatadvayābdavān //
285.d:
शालूकचूर्णं भृङ्गाज्यं समध्वाज्यं शताब्दकृत् /
कटुतुम्बीतैलनस्यं कर्षं शतद्वयाब्दवान् //
285.m:
Powder of lotus root, bhṛṅga, and ghee, taken with honey and ghee, grants a hundred years of life.
A karṣa of bitter-gourd oil used as nasal therapy grants two hundred years of life.

285.s:
triphalā pippalī śuṇṭhī sevitā triśatābdakṛt /
śatāvaryāḥ pūrvayogaḥ sahasrāyurbalātikṛt //
285.d:
त्रिफला पिप्पली शुण्ठी सेविता त्रिशताब्दकृत् /
शतावर्याः पूर्वयोगः सहस्रायुर्बलातिकृत् //
285.m:
Triphalā, pippalī, and dried ginger, taken regularly, grant three hundred years.
The aforementioned formulation of śatāvarī grants a thousand years of life and tremendous strength.

285.s:
citrakena tathā purvas tathā śuṇṭhīviḍaṅgataḥ /
lohena bhṛṅgarājena balayā nimbapañcakaiḥ //
285.d:
चित्रकेन तथा पुर्वस् तथा शुण्ठीविडङ्गतः /
लोहेन भृङ्गराजेन बलया निम्बपञ्चकैः //
285.m:
Likewise the former [formula] with citraka; likewise with dry ginger and viḍaṅga;
with iron, bhṛṅgarāja, balā, and the five parts of neem;

285.s:
khadireṇa ca nirguṇḍyā kaṇṭakāryātha vāsakāt /
varṣābhuvā tadrasair vā bhāvito vaṭikākṛtaḥ //
285.d:
खदिरेण च निर्गुण्ड्या कण्टकार्याथ वासकात् /
वर्षाभुवा तद्रसैर् वा भावितो वटिकाकृतः //
285.m:
with khadira, nirguṇḍī, kaṇṭakārī, or vāsaka,
or with punarnavā; macerated with their juices and made into pills,

285.s:
cūrṇaṅghṛtair vā madhunā guḍādyair vāriṇā tathā /
oṃ hrūṃ sa itimantreṇa mantrato yogarājakaḥ //
285.d:
चूर्णङ्घृतैर् वा मधुना गुडाद्यैर् वारिणा तथा /
ओं ह्रूं स इतिमन्त्रेण मन्त्रतो योगराजकः //
285.m:
or as powder taken with ghee, honey, jaggery, or water,
consecrated with the mantra "Oṃ hrūṃ saḥ"—this king of formulations,

285.s:
mṛtasañjīvanīkalpo rogamṛtyuñjayo bhavet /
surāsuraiś ca munibhiḥ sevitāḥ kalpasāgarāḥ //
gajāyurvedaṃ provāca pālakāpye 'ṅgarājakaṃ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe kalpasāgaro nāma
pañcāśītyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:p 60
:ś atha ṣaḍaśītyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
gajacikitsā
pālakāpya uvāca(1)
285.d:
मृतसञ्जीवनीकल्पो रोगमृत्युञ्जयो भवेत् /
सुरासुरैश् च मुनिभिः सेविताः कल्पसागराः //
गजायुर्वेदं प्रोवाच पालकाप्ये ऽङ्गराजकं //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे कल्पसागरो नाम
पञ्चाशीत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
:प् 60
:श् अथ षडशीत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
गजचिकित्सा
पालकाप्य उवाच(1)
285.m:
a rejuvenation method reviving the dead, conquers disease and death.
The oceans of rejuvenation have been practiced by gods, asuras, and sages.
Pālakāpya taught the elephant-ayurveda to the king of Aṅga.
Thus in the great Āgneya Purāṇa, the two hundred and eighty-fifth chapter, entitled "The Ocean of Rejuvenation."
[Page 60]
Now the two hundred and eighty-sixth chapter.
Treatment of Elephants
Pālakāpya said:

286.s:
gajalakṣma cikitsāñca lomapāda yadāmi te /
dīrghahastā mahocchvāsāḥ prasastāste mahiṣṇavaḥ //
286.d:
गजलक्ष्म चिकित्साञ्च लोमपाद यदामि ते /
दीर्घहस्ता महोच्छ्वासाः प्रसस्तास्ते महिष्णवः //
286.m: I shall tell you, O Romapāda, the characteristics and treatment of elephants: / Those having long trunks, deep breathing, and great endurance are praised.

286.s:
viṃśatyaṣṭādaśanakhāḥ śītakālamadāś ca ye /
dakṣiṇañconnatandantaṃ vṛṃhitaṃ jaladopamaṃ //
286.d:
विंशत्यष्टादशनखाः शीतकालमदाश् च ये /
दक्षिणञ्चोन्नतन्दन्तं वृंहितं जलदोपमं //
286.m: Those with twenty or eighteen nails, whose rut flows in the cold season, / whose right tusk is elevated, and whose trumpeting resembles a cloud,

286.s:
karṇaur ca vipūlau yeṣāṃ sūkṣmavindvanvitatvacau /
te dhāryā na tathā dhāryā vāmanā ye ca saṅkuśāḥ(2) //
286.d:
कर्णौर् च विपूलौ येषां सूक्ष्मविन्द्वन्वितत्वचौ /
ते धार्या न तथा धार्या वामना ये च सङ्कुशाः(2) //
286.m: and whose ears are broad with skin dotted with tiny speckles— / these should be kept; dwarf elephants and those that are crooked should not be kept.

286.s:
hastinyaḥ pārśvagarbhiṇyo ca mūḍhā mataṅgajāḥ /
varṇaṃ satvaṃ balaṃ rūpaṃ kāntiḥ saṃhananañjavaḥ //
286.d:
हस्तिन्यः पार्श्वगर्भिण्यो च मूढा मतङ्गजाः /
वर्णं सत्वं बलं रूपं कान्तिः संहननञ्जवः //
286.m: Elephants pregnant sideways and dull elephants [are likewise avoided]. / Color, temperament, strength, form, luster, compactness, and speed:

286.s:
saptasthito gajaścedṛk saṅgrāmerīñjayetsa ca /
kuñjarāḥ paramā śobhā śivirasya balasya ca //
286.d:
सप्तस्थितो गजश्चेदृक् सङ्ग्रामेरीञ्जयेत्स च /
कुञ्जराः परमा शोभा शिविरस्य बलस्य च //
286.m: An elephant established in these seven virtues conquers enemies in battle. / Elephants are the supreme splendor of the camp and of the army.

286.s:
āyattaṃ kuñjaraiś caiva vijayaṃ pṛthivīkṣitāṃ /
pākaleṣu ca sarveṣu kartavyamanuvāsanaṃ //
286.d:
आयत्तं कुञ्जरैश् चैव विजयं पृथिवीक्षितां /
पाकलेषु च सर्वेषु कर्तव्यमनुवासनं //
286.m: Victory for kings depends upon elephants alone. / An unctuous enema must be administered in all forms of pākala fever;

286.s:
ghṛtatailaparīpākaṃ sthānaṃ vātavivarjitaṃ /
skandheṣu ca kriyā karyā tathā pālakavannṛpāḥ //
286.d:
घृततैलपरीपाकं स्थानं वातविवर्जितं /
स्कन्धेषु च क्रिया कर्या तथा पालकवन्नृपाः //
286.m: a decoction cooked with ghee and oil [is given], and a stall free from wind [is maintained]. / And treatment must be performed on the shoulders, O kings, according to the keeper.

286.s:
gomūtraṃ pāṇḍurogeṣu rajanībhyāṃ ghṛtandvija /
ānāhe tailasiktasya niṣekastasya śasyate //
286.d:
गोमूत्रं पाण्डुरोगेषु रजनीभ्यां घृतन्द्विज /
आनाहे तैलसिक्तस्य निषेकस्तस्य शस्यते //
286.m: In jaundice, cow's urine with both turmerics and ghee [is prescribed], O twice-born; / in constipation, pouring [warm water] over one smeared with oil is recommended,

286.s:
lavaṇaiḥ pañcabhirmaśrā pratipānāya vāruṇī /
:n
1 dhanvantariruvāceti ña..
2 mardanā iti ña..
:p 61
viḍaṅgatriphalāvyoṣasaindhavaiḥ kavalān kṛtān //
286.d:
लवणैः पञ्चभिर्मश्रा प्रतिपानाय वारुणी /
:न्
1 धन्वन्तरिरुवाचेति ञ..
2 मर्दना इति ञ..
:प् 61
विडङ्गत्रिफलाव्योषसैन्धवैः कवलान् कृतान् //
286.m:
along with vāruṇī liquor mixed with the five salts for drinking.
[Footnote]
[Variant reading note: "1 Dhanvantari said" in manuscript ña.]
[Variant reading note: "2 mardanāḥ" in manuscript ña. / Page 61]
Mouthfuls prepared with viḍaṅga, triphalā, the three pungents, and rock salt

286.s:
mūrchāsu bhojayennāgaṃ kṣaudrantoyañca pāyayet /
agyaṅgaḥ śirasaḥ śūle nasyañcaiva praśasyate //
286.d:
मूर्छासु भोजयेन्नागं क्षौद्रन्तोयञ्च पाययेत् /
अग्यङ्गः शिरसः शूले नस्यञ्चैव प्रशस्यते //
286.m: should be fed to the elephant in swoons, and honey and water should be given to drink. / An ointment and nasal medication are praised for headache.

286.s:
nāgānāṃ snehapuṭakaḥ pādarogānupakramet /
paścāt kalkakaṣāyeṇa śodhanañca vidhīyate //
286.d:
नागानां स्नेहपुटकः पादरोगानुपक्रमेत् /
पश्चात् कल्ककषायेण शोधनञ्च विधीयते //
286.m: An oily poultice applied to elephants cures diseases of the feet; / thereafter, cleansing with a paste and decoction is prescribed.

286.s:
śikhitittirilāvānāṃ pippalīmaricānvitaiḥ /
rasaiḥ sambhojayennagaṃ vepathuryasya jāyate //
286.d:
शिखितित्तिरिलावानां पिप्पलीमरिचान्वितैः /
रसैः सम्भोजयेन्नगं वेपथुर्यस्य जायते //
286.m: One should feed an elephant suffering from tremors with the broths / of peafowl, francolins, and quails mixed with long pepper and black pepper.

286.s:
bālabilvaṃ tathā lodhraṃ dhātakī sitayā saha /
atīsāravināśāya piṇḍīṃ bhuñjīta kuñjaraḥ //
286.d:
बालबिल्वं तथा लोध्रं धातकी सितया सह /
अतीसारविनाशाय पिण्डीं भुञ्जीत कुञ्जरः //
286.m: Tender bilva, lodhra, and dhātakī along with white sugar: / the elephant should eat [this] bolus for the destruction of diarrhea.

286.s:
nasyaṃ karagrahe deyaṃ ghṛtaṃ layaṇasaṃyutam /
māgadhīnāgarājājīyavāgūrmustasādhitā //
286.d:
नस्यं करग्रहे देयं घृतं लयणसंयुतम् /
मागधीनागराजाजीयवागूर्मुस्तसाधिता //
286.m: In stiffness of the trunk, nasal administration of ghee mixed with salt should be given. / Gruel prepared with long pepper, ginger, cumin, and nut grass

286.s:
utkarṇake tu dātavyā vārāhañca tathā rasam /
daśamūlakulatthāmlakākamācīvipācitam //
286.d:
उत्कर्णके तु दातव्या वाराहञ्च तथा रसम् /
दशमूलकुलत्थाम्लकाकमाचीविपाचितम् //
286.m: should be given in stiffness of the ears, as well as boar broth. / Cooked with the ten roots, horse gram, sour gruel, and black nightshade,

286.s:
tailamūṣaṇasaṃyuktaṃ galagrahagadāpaham /
aṣṭabhirlavaṇaiḥ piṣṭhaiḥ prasannāḥ pāyayedghṛtam //
286.d:
तैलमूषणसंयुक्तं गलग्रहगदापहम् /
अष्टभिर्लवणैः पिष्ठैः प्रसन्नाः पाययेद्घृतम् //
286.m: oil mixed with pungent spices cures the affliction of throat spasms. / One should make [the elephant] drink ghee in clear liquor with eight ground salts.

286.s:
mūtrabhaṅge 'tha vā vījaṃ kvathitaṃ trapūṣasya ca /
tvagdoṣeṣu pivennimbaṃ vṛṣaṃ vā kvathitaṃ dvipaḥ //
286.d:
मूत्रभङ्गे ऽथ वा वीजं क्वथितं त्रपूषस्य च /
त्वग्दोषेषु पिवेन्निम्बं वृषं वा क्वथितं द्विपः //
286.m: In retention of urine, a decoction of cucumber seeds [is given]; / in skin diseases, the elephant should drink a decoction of nimba or vāśā.

286.s:
gavāṃ mūtraṃ viḍaṅgāni kṛmikoṣṭheṣu śasyate /
śṛṅgaverakaṇādrākṣāśarkarābhiḥ śṛtaṃ payaḥ //
286.d:
गवां मूत्रं विडङ्गानि कृमिकोष्ठेषु शस्यते /
शृङ्गवेरकणाद्राक्षाशर्कराभिः शृतं पयः //
286.m: Cow's urine and viḍaṅga are recommended for intestinal worms. / Milk boiled with ginger, long pepper, grapes, and sugar

286.s:
kṣatakṣayakaraṃ pānaṃ tathā māṃsarasaḥ śubhaḥ /
mudgodanaṃ vyoṣayutamarucau tu praśasyate //
286.d:
क्षतक्षयकरं पानं तथा मांसरसः शुभः /
मुद्गोदनं व्योषयुतमरुचौ तु प्रशस्यते //
286.m: is a drink that cures wounds and wasting; likewise meat broth is beneficial. / Boiled rice with mung beans mixed with the three pungents is praised in loss of appetite.

286.s:
trivṛdvyoṣāgnidantyarkaśyāmākṣīrebhapippalī /
etair gulmaharaḥ snehaḥ kṛtaś caiva tathāparaḥ //
:p 62
286.d:
त्रिवृद्व्योषाग्निदन्त्यर्कश्यामाक्षीरेभपिप्पली /
एतैर् गुल्महरः स्नेहः कृतश् चैव तथापरः //
:प् 62
286.m:
Trivṛt, the three pungents, agni, danti, arka, milky syāmā, and gajapippalī: / an oil prepared with these removes abdominal tumors; likewise another [preparation]:
[Page 62]

286.s:
bhedanadrāvaṇābhyaṅgasnehapānānuvāsanaiḥ /
sarvāneva samutpannan vidravān samupāharet //
286.d:
भेदनद्रावणाभ्यङ्गस्नेहपानानुवासनैः /
सर्वानेव समुत्पन्नन् विद्रवान् समुपाहरेत् //
286.m: By means of purgation, liquefaction, massage, unctuous drinks, and unctuous enemas, / one should completely remove all arising swellings.

286.s:
yaṣṭikaṃ mudgasūpena(1) śāradena tathā pivet /
bālabilvais tathā lepaḥ phaṭurogeṣu śasyate //
286.d:
यष्टिकं मुद्गसूपेन(1) शारदेन तथा पिवेत् /
बालबिल्वैस् तथा लेपः फटुरोगेषु शस्यते //
286.m: One should have [the elephant] drink sixty-day rice with autumn mung bean soup; / likewise a plaster made of tender bilva is praised in flatulence.

286.s:
viḍaṅgendrayavau hiṅgu saralaṃ rajanīdvayam /
pūrvāhṇe pāyayet piṇḍān sarvaśūlopaśāntaye //
286.d:
विडङ्गेन्द्रयवौ हिङ्गु सरलं रजनीद्वयम् /
पूर्वाह्णे पाययेत् पिण्डान् सर्वशूलोपशान्तये //
286.m: Viḍaṅga, indrayava, asafoetida, pine, and the two turmerics: / one should administer balls [of these] in the morning to alleviate all colicky pains.

286.s:
pradhānabhojane teṣāṃ yaṣṭikavrīhiśālayaḥ /
madhyamau yavagodhūmau śeṣā dantini cādhamāḥ //
286.d:
प्रधानभोजने तेषां यष्टिकव्रीहिशालयः /
मध्यमौ यवगोधूमौ शेषा दन्तिनि चाधमाः //
286.m: Among their primary foods are sixty-day rice, vrīhi rice, and winter rice; / barley and wheat are middling, and the rest are inferior for the elephant.

286.s:
yavaś caiva tathaivekṣurnāgānāṃ balavardhanaḥ /
nāgānāṃ yavasaṃ śuṣkaṃ tathā dhātuprakopaṇaṃ //
286.d:
यवश् चैव तथैवेक्षुर्नागानां बलवर्धनः /
नागानां यवसं शुष्कं तथा धातुप्रकोपणं //
286.m: Barley and likewise sugarcane increase the strength of elephants. / Dry fodder aggravates the bodily humors of elephants.

286.s:
madakṣiṇasya nāgasya payaḥpānaṃ praśasyate /
dīpanīyais tathā dravyaiḥ śṛto māṃsarasaḥ śubhaḥ //
286.d:
मदक्षिणस्य नागस्य पयःपानं प्रशस्यते /
दीपनीयैस् तथा द्रव्यैः शृतो मांसरसः शुभः //
286.m: For an elephant depleted of rut, drinking milk is praised; / meat broth boiled with digestive ingredients is likewise beneficial.

286.s:
vāyasaḥ kukkuraścobhau kākolūkakulo hariḥ /
bhavet kṣaudreṇa saṃyuktaḥ piṇḍo yuddhe mahāpadi(2) //
286.d:
वायसः कुक्कुरश्चोभौ काकोलूककुलो हरिः /
भवेत् क्षौद्रेण संयुक्तः पिण्डो युद्धे महापदि(2) //
286.m: Crow and dog, both; a raven, an owl, and a monkey, / combined with honey, become a bolus [to be given] in battle in great danger.

286.s:
kaṭumatsyaviḍaṅgāni kṣāraḥ koṣātakī payaḥ /
haridrā ceti dhūpoyaṃ kuñjarasya jayāvahaḥ //
286.d:
कटुमत्स्यविडङ्गानि क्षारः कोषातकी पयः /
हरिद्रा चेति धूपोयं कुञ्जरस्य जयावहः //
286.m: Pungent fish, viḍaṅga, alkali, koṣātakī, milk, / and turmeric: this fumigation brings victory to an elephant.

286.s:
pippalītaṇḍulāstailaṃ mādhvīkaṃ mākṣikam tathā /
netrayoḥ pariṣekoyaṃ dīpanīyaḥ praśasyate //
286.d:
पिप्पलीतण्डुलास्तैलं माध्वीकं माक्षिकम् तथा /
नेत्रयोः परिषेकोयं दीपनीयः प्रशस्यते //
286.m: Long pepper, broken rice, oil, mādhvīka wine, and honey: / this wash for the eyes is praised as stimulating.

286.s:
pūrīṣañcaṭakāyāś ca tathā pārāvatasya ca /
kṣīravṛkṣakarīṣāś ca(3) prasannayeṣṭamañjanaṃ //
:n
1 mudgyūṣeṇeti ja.. , ña.. ca
2 madāya hīti ña..
3 kṣīravṛkṣakarīrāśceti ña..
:p 63
286.d:
पूरीषञ्चटकायाश् च तथा पारावतस्य च /
क्षीरवृक्षकरीषाश् च(3) प्रसन्नयेष्टमञ्जनं //
:न्
1 मुद्ग्यूषेणेति ज.. , ञ.. च
2 मदाय हीति ञ..
3 क्षीरवृक्षकरीराश्चेति ञ..
:प् 63
286.m:
Dung of a sparrow and of a pigeon, / and dung of milky trees: a clear collyrium is desired.
[Footnote]
[Variant reading note: "1 mudgayūṣeṇa" in ja. and ña.]
[Variant reading note: "2 madāya hi" in ña.]
[Variant reading note: "3 kṣīravṛkṣakarīrāḥ" in ña. / Page 63]

286.s:
anenāñjitanetrastu karoti kadanaṃ raṇe /
utpalāni ca nīlāni sustantagarameva ca //
286.d:
अनेनाञ्जितनेत्रस्तु करोति कदनं रणे /
उत्पलानि च नीलानि सुस्तन्तगरमेव च //
286.m: One whose eyes are smeared with this works slaughter in battle. / Blue water lilies and fragrant cyperus grass with tagara,

286.s:
taṇḍulodakapiṣṭāni netranirvāpanaṃ param /
nakhavṛddhau nakhacchedastailasekaś ca māsyapi //
286.d:
तण्डुलोदकपिष्टानि नेत्रनिर्वापनं परम् /
नखवृद्धौ नखच्छेदस्तैलसेकश् च मास्यपि //
286.m: ground with rice water, provide the supreme cooling for the eyes. / In overgrowth of the nails, clipping the nails and sprinkling with oil is done monthly.

286.s:
śayyāsthānaṃ bhaveccāsya karīṣaiḥ pāṃśubhis tathā /
śarannidāghayoḥ sekaḥ sarpiṣā ca tatheṣyate //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe gajacikitsā nāma
ṣaḍaśītyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:ś atha saptāśītyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
aśvavāhanasāraḥ
286.d:
शय्यास्थानं भवेच्चास्य करीषैः पांशुभिस् तथा /
शरन्निदाघयोः सेकः सर्पिषा च तथेष्यते //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे गजचिकित्सा नाम
षडशीत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
:श् अथ सप्ताशीत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
अश्ववाहनसारः
286.m:
Its bedding area should be made of dry dung and dust; / and in autumn and summer, sprinkling with ghee is desired.
Thus in the great Purāṇa of Agni, the two hundred and eighty-sixth chapter, named "The Treatment of Elephants."
Now, the two hundred and eighty-seventh chapter:
The Essence of Horsemanship

287.s:
dhanvantarir uvāca
aśvavāhanasārañca vakṣye cāśvacikitsanam /
vājināṃ saṃgrahaḥ kāryo dharmakamārthasiddhaye //
287.d:
धन्वन्तरिर् उवाच
अश्ववाहनसारञ्च वक्ष्ये चाश्वचिकित्सनम् /
वाजिनां संग्रहः कार्यो धर्मकमार्थसिद्धये //
287.m: Dhanvantari said: / I shall declare the essence of horsemanship and the medical treatment of horses. / Acquisition of steeds should be made for the accomplishment of virtue, pleasure, and wealth.

287.s:
aśvinī śraṇaṃ hastaṃ uttarātritayantathā /
nakṣatrāṇi praśastāni hayānāmādivāhane //
287.d:
अश्विनी श्रणं हस्तं उत्तरात्रितयन्तथा /
नक्षत्राणि प्रशस्तानि हयानामादिवाहने //
287.m: Aśvinī, Śravaṇa, Hasta, and the triad of Uttarās: / these lunar mansions are praised for the first riding of horses.

287.s:
hemantaḥ śiśiraś caiva vasantaścāśvavāhane /
grīṣmeśaradi varṣāsu niṣiddhaṃ vāhanaṃ haye //
287.d:
हेमन्तः शिशिरश् चैव वसन्तश्चाश्ववाहने /
ग्रीष्मेशरदि वर्षासु निषिद्धं वाहनं हये //
287.m: Late autumn, winter, and spring are suitable for riding a horse; / in summer, autumn, and the rainy season, riding a horse is prohibited.

287.s:
tīvrair na ca parair daṇḍair adeśe na ca tāḍayet /
kīlāsthisaṃkule caiva viṣame kaṇṭakānvite //
:p 64
287.d:
तीव्रैर् न च परैर् दण्डैर् अदेशे न च ताडयेत् /
कीलास्थिसंकुले चैव विषमे कण्टकान्विते //
:प् 64
287.m:
One should not strike [it] with fierce sticks or on improper spots, / nor in a place crowded with pegs and bones, uneven, full of thorns,
[Page 64]

287.s:
vālukāpaṅgasaṃcchanne gartāgartapradūṣite /
acittajño vinopāyair vāhanaṃ kurutetu haḥ //
287.d:
वालुकापङ्गसंच्छन्ने गर्तागर्तप्रदूषिते /
अचित्तज्ञो विनोपायैर् वाहनं कुरुतेतु हः //
287.m: covered with sand and mud, or spoiled with pit after pit. / A man who, ignorant of its mind and lacking skillful means, undertakes riding—

287.s:
sa vāhyate hayenaiva pṛṣṭhasthaḥ kaṭikāṃ vinā(1)
chandaṃ vijñāpayet kopi sakṛtī dhīmatāṃ varaḥ //
287.d:
स वाह्यते हयेनैव पृष्ठस्थः कटिकां विना(1)
छन्दं विज्ञापयेत् कोपि सकृती धीमतां वरः //
287.m: he is driven about by the horse itself, seated upon its back without control. / A skilled rider, foremost among the wise, should make known its inclination.

287.s:
abhyāsādabhiyogācca vināśāstraṃ svavāhakaḥ /
snātasya praṅmukhasyātha devān vapuṣi yojayet //
287.d:
अभ्यासादभियोगाच्च विनाशास्त्रं स्ववाहकः /
स्नातस्य प्रङ्मुखस्याथ देवान् वपुषि योजयेत् //
287.m: Through practice and concentration, a rider controls his horse without weapons. / Then, when it is bathed and facing east, he should assign the deities to its body

287.s:
praṇavādinamontena svavījena yathākramam /
brahmā citte vale viṣṇurvainateyaḥ parākrame //
287.d:
प्रणवादिनमोन्तेन स्ववीजेन यथाक्रमम् /
ब्रह्मा चित्ते वले विष्णुर्वैनतेयः पराक्रमे //
287.m: in due order, beginning with Om, ending with namaḥ, with each one's seed-syllable: / Brahmā in the mind, Viṣṇu in strength, Garuḍa in valor,

287.s:
pārśve rudrā gururbuddhau viśvedevātha marmasu /
dṛgāvarte dṛśīndvarkau karṇayoraśvinau tathā //
287.d:
पार्श्वे रुद्रा गुरुर्बुद्धौ विश्वेदेवाथ मर्मसु /
दृगावर्ते दृशीन्द्वर्कौ कर्णयोरश्विनौ तथा //
287.m: the Rudras in the flanks, Bṛhaspati in the intellect, the Viśvedevas in the vital spots, / the Sun and Moon in the eyes and whorls of the eyes, and the Aśvins in the ears;

287.s:
jaṭhare 'gniḥ svadhā svede vagjihvāyāṃ jave 'nilaḥ /
pṛṣṭhato nākapṛṣṭhastu khurāgre sarvaparvatāḥ //
287.d:
जठरे ऽग्निः स्वधा स्वेदे वग्जिह्वायां जवे ऽनिलः /
पृष्ठतो नाकपृष्ठस्तु खुराग्रे सर्वपर्वताः //
287.m: Agni in the belly, Svadhā in the sweat, Sarasvatī in the tongue, Vāyu in speed, / heaven upon its back, and all the mountains on the tips of its hooves;

287.s:
tārāś ca romakūpeṣu hṛdi cāndramasī kalā /
tejasyagnīratiḥ śroṇyāṃ lalāṭe ca jagatpatiḥ //
287.d:
ताराश् च रोमकूपेषु हृदि चान्द्रमसी कला /
तेजस्यग्नीरतिः श्रोण्यां ललाटे च जगत्पतिः //
287.m: the stars in the hair-follicles, the lunar digit in the heart, / Agni in splendor, Rati in the hips, and the Lord of the World on the forehead;

287.s:
grahāś ca heṣite caiva tathaivorasi vāsukiḥ /
upoṣito 'rcayet sādī hayaṃ dakṣaśrutau japet //
287.d:
ग्रहाश् च हेषिते चैव तथैवोरसि वासुकिः /
उपोषितो ऽर्चयेत् सादी हयं दक्षश्रुतौ जपेत् //
287.m: the planets in its neighing, and Vāsuki upon its chest. / Fasting, the horseman should worship the horse and recite [the mantra] into its right ear.

287.s:
haya gandharvarājastvaṃ śṛṇuṣva vacanaṃ gama /
gandharvakulajātastvaṃ mābhūstvaṃ kuladūṣakaḥ //
287.d:
हय गन्धर्वराजस्त्वं शृणुष्व वचनं गम /
गन्धर्वकुलजातस्त्वं माभूस्त्वं कुलदूषकः //
287.m:
“O horse, you are the king of the Gandharvas! Listen to my word, go!
You are born of the lineage of the Gandharvas; do not become a disgrace to your line!

287.s:
dvijānāṃ satyavākyena somasya garuḍasya ca /
rudrasya varuṇasyaiva pavanasya balena ca //
287.d:
द्विजानां सत्यवाक्येन सोमस्य गरुडस्य च /
रुद्रस्य वरुणस्यैव पवनस्य बलेन च //
287.m:
By the true word of the Brahmins, and of Soma and Garuḍa,
and by the power of Rudra, Varuṇa, and Pavana,

287.s:
hutāśanasya dīptyā ca smara jātiṃ turaṅgama /
smara rājendraputrastvaṃ satyavākyamanusmara //
:n
1 kaṇikāṃ vineti ka.. , ña.. ca
:p 65
287.d:
हुताशनस्य दीप्त्या च स्मर जातिं तुरङ्गम /
स्मर राजेन्द्रपुत्रस्त्वं सत्यवाक्यमनुस्मर //
:न्
1 कणिकां विनेति क.. , ञ.. च
:प् 65
287.m:
and by the radiance of the fire oblation-eater [Agni], remember your breed, O steed!
Remember, you are the son of a king of kings; recall your truthful pledge!
[Footnote]
[Variant reading: 'kaṇikāṃ vinā' in ka. and ña.]
[Page 65]

287.s:
smara tvaṃ vāruṇīṃ kanyāṃ smara tvaṃ kaustubhaṃ maṇiṃ /
kṣirodasāgare caiva mathyamāne surāsuraiḥ //
287.d:
स्मर त्वं वारुणीं कन्यां स्मर त्वं कौस्तुभं मणिं /
क्षिरोदसागरे चैव मथ्यमाने सुरासुरैः //
287.m:
Remember the maiden Vāruṇī; remember the Kaustubha gem
when the ocean of milk was being churned by the gods and demons!

287.s:
tatra devakule jātaḥ svavākyaṃ paripālaya /
kule jātastvamaśvānāṃ mitraṃ me bhava śāsvatam //
287.d:
तत्र देवकुले जातः स्ववाक्यं परिपालय /
कुले जातस्त्वमश्वानां मित्रं मे भव शास्वतम् //
287.m:
Born there in the family of the gods, keep your word!
Born in the line of horses, become my eternal friend!

287.s:
śṛṇu mitra tvametacca siddho me bhava vāhana /
vijayaṃ rakṣa māñcaiva samare siddhimāvaha //
287.d:
शृणु मित्र त्वमेतच्च सिद्धो मे भव वाहन /
विजयं रक्ष माञ्चैव समरे सिद्धिमावह //
287.m:
Listen, O friend, to this: become an accomplished mount for me;
protect victory and me as well, and bring success in battle!

287.s:
tava pṛṣṭhaṃ samāruhya hatā daityāḥ suraiḥ purā /
adhunā tvāṃ samāruhya jeṣyāmi ripuvāhinīṃ //
287.d:
तव पृष्ठं समारुह्य हता दैत्याः सुरैः पुरा /
अधुना त्वां समारुह्य जेष्यामि रिपुवाहिनीं //
287.m:
Mounting your back, the Daityas were slain by the gods of old;
now, mounting you, I will conquer the army of the enemy.”

287.s:
karṇajāpantataḥ kṛtvā vimuhya ca tathā pyarīn(1) /
paryānayeddhayaṃ sādī vahayedyuddhato jayaḥ //
287.d:
कर्णजापन्ततः कृत्वा विमुह्य च तथा प्यरीन्(1) /
पर्यानयेद्धयं सादी वहयेद्युद्धतो जयः //
287.m:
Then, having performed the whispered recitation in its ear, and thus confusing the enemies,
the rider should saddle the horse and ride it; from battle comes victory.

287.s:
sañjātāḥ svaśarīreṇa(2) doṣāḥ prāyeṇa vājināṃ /
hanyante 'tiprayatnena guṇāḥ sādivaraiḥ punaḥ //
287.d:
सञ्जाताः स्वशरीरेण(2) दोषाः प्रायेण वाजिनां /
हन्यन्ते ऽतिप्रयत्नेन गुणाः सादिवरैः पुनः //
287.m:
The faults of horses generally arise with their own body;
moreover, excellent qualities are produced with great effort by the best of riders.

287.s:
sahajā iva dṛśyante guṇāḥ sādivarodbhavāḥ /
nāśayanti guṇānanye sādinaḥ sahajānapi //
287.d:
सहजा इव दृश्यन्ते गुणाः सादिवरोद्भवाः /
नाशयन्ति गुणानन्ये सादिनः सहजानपि //
287.m:
Qualities born of the best riders appear as if innate;
other riders destroy even their innate qualities.

287.s:
guṇāneko vijānāti vetti doṣāṃs tathāparaḥ /
dhanyo dhīmān hayaṃ vetti mandadhīḥ //
287.d:
गुणानेको विजानाति वेत्ति दोषांस् तथापरः /
धन्यो धीमान् हयं वेत्ति मन्दधीः //
287.m:
One knows the virtues, and another knows the faults;
fortunate and wise is he who knows the horse; the dull-witted does not.

287.s:
akarmajño 'nupāyajño vegāsakto 'tikopanaḥ /
ghanadaṇḍaraticchidre yaḥ mamopi na śasyate //
287.d:
अकर्मज्ञो ऽनुपायज्ञो वेगासक्तो ऽतिकोपनः /
घनदण्डरतिच्छिद्रे यः ममोपि न शस्यते //
287.m:
He who knows not the proper actions, knows not the methods, is addicted to speed, is exceedingly angry,
and delights in frequent beating even at the slightest flaw, is not praised, even if he were like Yama.

287.s:
upāyajño 'tha cittajño viśuddho doṣanāśanaḥ /
guṇārjanaparo nityaṃ sarvakarmaviśāradaḥ //
287.d:
उपायज्ञो ऽथ चित्तज्ञो विशुद्धो दोषनाशनः /
गुणार्जनपरो नित्यं सर्वकर्मविशारदः //
287.m:
One who knows the methods, understands the mind [of the mount], is pure, removes faults,
is ever intent on acquiring good qualities, and is skilled in all operations [is praised].

287.s:
pragraheṇa gṛhītvātha praviṣṭo vāhabhūtalam /
savyāpasavyabhedena vāhanīyaḥ svasādinā //
:n
1 tathāsuraniti ja.. , ña.. , ṭa.. ca
2 saha jātāḥ śarīreṇeti ña..
:p 66
287.d:
प्रग्रहेण गृहीत्वाथ प्रविष्टो वाहभूतलम् /
सव्यापसव्यभेदेन वाहनीयः स्वसादिना //
:न्
1 तथासुरनिति ज.. , ञ.. , ट.. च
2 सह जाताः शरीरेणेति ञ..
:प् 66
287.m:
Then, having taken the reins, entering the riding arena,
[the horse] is to be ridden by its rider with variations of left and right.
[Footnote]
[Variant reading: 'tathāsurān' in ja., ña., and ṭa.]
[Variant reading: 'saha jātāḥ śarīreṇa' in ña.]
[Page 66]

287.s:
āruhya sahasā naiva tāḍnīyo hayottamaḥ /
tāḍanādubhayamāpnoti bhayānmohaś ca jāyate //
287.d:
आरुह्य सहसा नैव ताड्नीयो हयोत्तमः /
ताडनादुभयमाप्नोति भयान्मोहश् च जायते //
287.m:
Having mounted, an excellent horse should never be struck hastily;
from beating it incurs fear, and from fear comes bewilderment.

287.s:
prātaḥ sādī plutenaiva valgāmuddhṛtya cālayet /
mandaṃ mandaṃ vinā nālaṃ dhṛtavalgo dināntare //
287.d:
प्रातः सादी प्लुतेनैव वल्गामुद्धृत्य चालयेत् /
मन्दं मन्दं विना नालं धृतवल्गो दिनान्तरे //
287.m:
In the morning, lifting the reins, the rider should move it at a canter;
on another day, holding the reins, gently and slowly without the bit.

287.s:
proktamāśvasanaṃ sāmabhedo 'śvena niyojyate /
kaṣāditāḍnaṃ daṇḍo dānaṃ kālasahiṣṇutā //
287.d:
प्रोक्तमाश्वसनं सामभेदो ऽश्वेन नियोज्यते /
कषादिताड्नं दण्डो दानं कालसहिष्णुता //
287.m:
Conciliation is declared to be soothing; division is applied by means of the horse;
punishment is striking with a whip and the like; gift is patience regarding time.

287.s:
parvapūrvaviśuddhau tu vidadhyāduttarottaram /
jihvātale vināyogaṃ vidadhyādvāhane haye //
287.d:
पर्वपूर्वविशुद्धौ तु विदध्यादुत्तरोत्तरम् /
जिह्वातले विनायोगं विदध्याद्वाहने हये //
287.m:
When the previous stage is mastered, he should apply the subsequent ones one after another;
he should apply [the bit] beneath the tongue in riding a horse without excessive force.

287.s:
guṇetaraśatāṃ valgāṃ sṛkkaṇyā saha gāhayet /
vismārya vāhanaṃ kuryācchithilānāṃ śanaiḥ śanaiḥ //
287.d:
गुणेतरशतां वल्गां सृक्कण्या सह गाहयेत् /
विस्मार्य वाहनं कुर्याच्छिथिलानां शनैः शनैः //
287.m:
He should plunge the reins, with hundreds of non-faulty strands, along with the corners of the mouth;
making it forget, he should gradually loosen the riding gear.

287.s:
hayaṃ jihvāṅgamāhīne jihvāgranthiṃ vimocayet /
gāṭatāṃ mocayettāvadyāvat stobhaṃ na suñcati //
287.d:
हयं जिह्वाङ्गमाहीने जिह्वाग्रन्थिं विमोचयेत् /
गाटतां मोचयेत्तावद्यावत् स्तोभं न सुञ्चति //
287.m:
On a horse deficient in the limb of the tongue, he should loosen the knot on the tongue;
he should relieve its stiffness as long as it does not throw off its pace.

287.s:
kuryācchatamurastrāṇamavilālañca muñcati /
ūrdhānanaḥ svabhādyastasyorastrāṇamaślatham //
287.d:
कुर्याच्छतमुरस्त्राणमविलालञ्च मुञ्चति /
ऊर्धाननः स्वभाद्यस्तस्योरस्त्राणमश्लथम् //
287.m:
He should make the breastplate firm and release it without looseness;
for a horse that naturally holds its face raised, its breastplate [should be] unslackened.

287.s:
vidhāya vāhayeddṛṣṭyā līlayā sādisattamaḥ /
tasya savyena pūrveṇa saṃyuktaṃ savyavalgayā //
287.d:
विधाय वाहयेद्दृष्ट्या लीलया सादिसत्तमः /
तस्य सव्येन पूर्वेण संयुक्तं सव्यवल्गया //

287.s:
yaḥ kuryātpaścimaṃ pādaṃ gṛhītastena dakṣiṇaḥ /
krameṇānena yo sevāṃ kurute vāmavalgayā //
287.d:
यः कुर्यात्पश्चिमं पादं गृहीतस्तेन दक्षिणः /
क्रमेणानेन यो सेवां कुरुते वामवल्गया //
287.m:
by him the right foot is taken control of;
he who in this sequence works it with the right rein,

287.s:
pādau tenāpi pādaḥ syādgṛhīto vāma eva hi /
agre ceccaraṇe tyakte jāyate sudṛḍhāsanaṃ //
287.d:
पादौ तेनापि पादः स्याद्गृहीतो वाम एव हि /
अग्रे चेच्चरणे त्यक्ते जायते सुदृढासनं //
287.m:
by him also the left foot would surely be taken control of in the legs;
if the forward feet are released, a very firm seat is achieved.

287.s:
yau hṛtau duṣkare caiva moṭake nāṭakāyanaṃ /
savyahīnaṃ khalīkāro hanena guṇane tatha //
287.d:
यौ हृतौ दुष्करे चैव मोटके नाटकायनं /
सव्यहीनं खलीकारो हनेन गुणने तथ //
287.m:
The two that are restrained in difficult motion and twisting constitute the dramatic gait;
deprived of the left, it is humiliation; likewise in striking and multiplying.

287.s:
svahāvaṃ hi turaṅgasya mukhavyāvartanaṃ puraḥ /
:p 67
na caivetthaṃ turaṅgāṇāṃ pādagrahaṇahetavaḥ //
287.d:
स्वहावं हि तुरङ्गस्य मुखव्यावर्तनं पुरः /
:प् 67
न चैवेत्थं तुरङ्गाणां पादग्रहणहेतवः //

287.s:
viśvastaṃ hayamālokya gāḍhamāpīḍya cāsanaṃ /
rokayitvā mukhe pādaṃ grāhyato lokanaṃ hitaṃ //
287.d:
विश्वस्तं हयमालोक्य गाढमापीड्य चासनं /
रोकयित्वा मुखे पादं ग्राह्यतो लोकनं हितं //
287.m:
Seeing that the horse is confident, firmly pressing down the seat,
checking the foot at the mouth, training [it] to look is beneficial.

287.s:
gāḍhamāpīḍya rāgābhyāṃ valgāmākṛṣya gṛhyate /
tadvandhanād yugmapādaṃ(1) tadvadvakvanamucyate //
287.d:
गाढमापीड्य रागाभ्यां वल्गामाकृष्य गृह्यते /
तद्वन्धनाद् युग्मपादं(1) तद्वद्वक्वनमुच्यते //
287.m:
Firmly pressing with both thighs and pulling the reins, it is controlled;
from that binding of a pair of legs, it is called vadvakvana.

287.s:
saṃyojya valgayā pādān valgāmāmocya vāñchitam /
vāhyapārṣṇiprayogāttu(2) yatra tattāḍanaṃ matam //
287.d:
संयोज्य वल्गया पादान् वल्गामामोच्य वाञ्छितम् /
वाह्यपार्ष्णिप्रयोगात्तु(2) यत्र तत्ताडनं मतम् //
287.m:
Having aligned the feet with the reins, releasing the reins as desired,
by the application of the outer spur, where that occurs, it is considered striking.

287.s:
pralayāviplave jñātvā krameṇānena buddhimān /
moṭanena caturthena vidhireṣa bidhīyate //
287.d:
प्रलयाविप्लवे ज्ञात्वा क्रमेणानेन बुद्धिमान् /
मोटनेन चतुर्थेन विधिरेष बिधीयते //
287.m:
Knowing the absence of agitation at dissolution, in this sequence the wise man
prescribes this procedure with a fourth twist.

287.s:
nādhatte 'dhaś ca pādaṃ yo 'śvo laghuni maṇḍale /
moṭanodvakkanābhyāntu grāhayet pādamīśitaṃ //
287.d:
नाधत्ते ऽधश् च पादं यो ऽश्वो लघुनि मण्डले /
मोटनोद्वक्कनाभ्यान्तु ग्राहयेत् पादमीशितं //
287.m:
The horse which does not place its foot down in a small circle,
he should cause to take the desired pace by means of twisting and bounding.

287.s:
vaṭayitvāsane(3) gāṭaṃ mandamādāya yo brajet /
grāhyate saṃgrahādyatra tatsaṃgrahaṇamucyate //
287.d:
वटयित्वासने(3) गाटं मन्दमादाय यो ब्रजेत् /
ग्राह्यते संग्रहाद्यत्र तत्संग्रहणमुच्यते //
287.m:
When, having rolled firmly in the seat, it goes slowly taking its stride,
where it is made to take it from restraint, that is called saṃgrahaṇa.

287.s:
hatvā parśve prahāreṇa sthānastho vyagramānasam /
valgāmākṛṣya pādena grāhyakaṇṭakapāyanam(4) //
287.d:
हत्वा पर्श्वे प्रहारेण स्थानस्थो व्यग्रमानसम् /
वल्गामाकृष्य पादेन ग्राह्यकण्टकपायनम्(4) //
287.m:
Striking the flank with a blow, standing in place, with an agitated mind,
pulling the reins with the foot, the thorn-drinking is to be checked.

287.s:
utthito yo 'ṅghraṇānena pārṣṇnipādātturaṅgamaḥ /
gṛhyate yat khalīkṛtya khalīkāraḥ sa ceṣyate //
287.d:
उत्थितो यो ऽङ्घ्रणानेन पार्ष्ण्निपादात्तुरङ्गमः /
गृह्यते यत् खलीकृत्य खलीकारः स चेष्यते //
287.m:
The horse which rises up with this foot-movement from the heel-foot,
and which is restrained after humbling it, that is considered khalīkāra.

287.s:
gatitraye piyaḥ pādamādatte naiva vāñchitaḥ /
hatvā tu yatra daṇḍena grāhyate gahanaṃ hi tat //
287.d:
गतित्रये पियः पादमादत्ते नैव वाञ्छितः /
हत्वा तु यत्र दण्डेन ग्राह्यते गहनं हि तत् //
287.m:
The desired foot which it does not take in the three paces,
where it is made to take it by striking with a stick, that indeed is gahana.

287.s:
khalīkṛtya catuṣkeṇa turaṅgo valgayānyayā /
ucchāsya grāhyate 'nyatra tatsyāducchāsanaṃ punaḥ //
:n
1 bhaṭhakālādyanutpādamiti ja..
2 bāhyapārśve prayogāttviti kha..
3 vaṇṭayitvāsane iti kha..
4 grāhakaṇṭakapāyanamiti kha..
:p 68
287.d:
खलीकृत्य चतुष्केण तुरङ्गो वल्गयान्यया /
उच्छास्य ग्राह्यते ऽन्यत्र तत्स्यादुच्छासनं पुनः //
:न्
1 भठकालाद्यनुत्पादमिति ज..
2 बाह्यपार्श्वे प्रयोगात्त्विति ख..
3 वण्टयित्वासने इति ख..
4 ग्राहकण्टकपायनमिति ख..
:प् 68
287.m:
Subduing the horse with the fourfold [pace], by means of another rein,
raising it and checking it elsewhere, that would again be ucchāsana.
[Footnote]
[Variant reading: 'bhaṭhakālādyanutpādam' in ja.]
[Variant reading: 'bāhyapārśve prayogāttu' in kha.]
[Variant reading: 'vaṇṭayitvāsane' in kha.]
[Variant reading: 'grāhakaṇṭakapāyanam' in kha.]
[Page 68]

287.s:
svabhāvaṃ bahirasyantaṃ tasyāṃ diśi padāyanaṃ /
niyojya grāhayettattu mukhavyāpartanaṃ matam //
287.d:
स्वभावं बहिरस्यन्तं तस्यां दिशि पदायनं /
नियोज्य ग्राहयेत्तत्तु मुखव्यापर्तनं मतम् //
287.m:
Applying the foot-movement in that direction cast outward by nature,
and making it take it, that is considered turning of the face.

287.s:
grāhayitvā tataḥ pādaṃ trividhāsu yathākramam /
sādhayet pañcadhārāsu kramaśo maṇḍalādiṣu //
287.d:
ग्राहयित्वा ततः पादं त्रिविधासु यथाक्रमम् /
साधयेत् पञ्चधारासु क्रमशो मण्डलादिषु //
287.m:
Then, having caused it to grasp the step in the three kinds in due order,
he should train it gradually in the five paces in circles and the like.

287.s:
ājanordhānanaṃ vāhaṃ śithilaṃ vāhayet sudhīḥ /
aṅgeṣu lāghavaṃ yāvattāvattaṃ vāhayeddhayaṃ //
287.d:
आजनोर्धाननं वाहं शिथिलं वाहयेत् सुधीः /
अङ्गेषु लाघवं यावत्तावत्तं वाहयेद्धयं //
287.m:
The wise rider should ride the mount that holds its face up from birth with loose reins;
he should ride that horse until lightness [appears] in its limbs.

287.s:
mṛduḥ skandhe laghurvaktre śithilaḥ sarvasandhiṣu /
yadā sasādino vaśyaḥ saṅgṛhṇīyāttadā hayaṃ //
287.d:
मृदुः स्कन्धे लघुर्वक्त्रे शिथिलः सर्वसन्धिषु /
यदा ससादिनो वश्यः सङ्गृह्णीयात्तदा हयं //
287.m:
When it is soft in the shoulder, light in the mouth, loose in all its joints,
and submissive to the rider, then he should restrain the horse.

287.s:
na tyajet paścimaṃ pādaṃ yadā sādhurbhavettadā /
tadākṛṣṭirvidhātavyā pāṇibhyāmiha balgayā //
287.d:
न त्यजेत् पश्चिमं पादं यदा साधुर्भवेत्तदा /
तदाकृष्टिर्विधातव्या पाणिभ्यामिह बल्गया //
287.m:
When it does not drop its hind leg, then it becomes well trained;
then the pulling [of the reins] must be performed with both hands on the reins here.

287.s:
tatratriko yathā tiṣṭhedudgrīvośvaḥ samānanaḥ /
dharāyāṃ paścimau pādau antarīkṣe yadāśrayau //
287.d:
तत्रत्रिको यथा तिष्ठेदुद्ग्रीवोश्वः समाननः /
धरायां पश्चिमौ पादौ अन्तरीक्षे यदाश्रयौ //
287.m:
So that the horse stands with its sacrum [balanced], high-necked, and level-faced,
when its hind legs rest on the ground and [the forelegs] are in the air,

287.s:
tadā sandharaṇaṃ kuryādgāṭhavāhañca muṣṭinā /
sahasaivaṃ samākṛṣṭo yasturaṅgo na tiṣṭhati //
287.d:
तदा सन्धरणं कुर्याद्गाठवाहञ्च मुष्टिना /
सहसैवं समाकृष्टो यस्तुरङ्गो न तिष्ठति //
287.m:
then he should execute steady holding and tight guidance with the fist;
a horse which, when thus pulled suddenly, does not stop,

287.s:
śarīraṃ vikṣipantañca sādhayenmaṇḍalabhramaiḥ /
kṣipet skandhañca yo vāhaṃ sa ca sthāpyo hi valgayā //
287.d:
शरीरं विक्षिपन्तञ्च साधयेन्मण्डलभ्रमैः /
क्षिपेत् स्कन्धञ्च यो वाहं स च स्थाप्यो हि वल्गया //
287.m:
and throws its body about, he should subdue by circulating in circles;
and a mount which throws its shoulder should indeed be restrained with the rein.

287.s:
gomayaṃ lavaṇaṃ mūtraṃ kvathitaṃ mṛtsamanvitam /
aṅgalepo makṣikādidaṃśaśramavināśanaḥ //
287.d:
गोमयं लवणं मूत्रं क्वथितं मृत्समन्वितम् /
अङ्गलेपो मक्षिकादिदंशश्रमविनाशनः //
287.m:
Cow dung, salt, and urine boiled together with clay,
anointed upon the limbs, destroys fatigue and bites of flies and other insects.

287.s:
madhye bhadrādijātīnāṃ maṇḍo deyo hi sādinā /
darśanaṃ bhotatīkṣasya nirutsāhaḥ kṣudhā hayaḥ //
287.d:
मध्ये भद्रादिजातीनां मण्डो देयो हि सादिना /
दर्शनं भोततीक्षस्य निरुत्साहः क्षुधा हयः //
287.m: In the middle of the breeds such as the Bhadra and others, the scum should be given by the rider. / If the horse is blunt, sharp, dispirited, or hungry,

287.s:
yathā vaśyas tathā śikṣā vinaśyantyativāhitāḥ /
avāhitā na midhyanti tuṅgavaktrāṃś ca vāhayet //
287.d:
यथा वश्यस् तथा शिक्षा विनश्यन्त्यतिवाहिताः /
अवाहिता न मिध्यन्ति तुङ्गवक्त्रांश् च वाहयेत् //
287.m: it should be trained according as it is tractable. Horses perish if excessively driven, / and they do not succeed if not driven at all; one should drive those that hold their heads high.

287.s:
sampīḍya jānuyugmena sthiramuṣṭisturaṅgamaṃ /
:p 69
gomūtrākuṭilā veṇī padmamaṇḍalamālikā //
287.d:
सम्पीड्य जानुयुग्मेन स्थिरमुष्टिस्तुरङ्गमं /
:प् 69
गोमूत्राकुटिला वेणी पद्ममण्डलमालिका //
287.m:
Pressing the horse firmly with both knees, with steady fists,
[Page 69]
in the serpentine course of cow-urine, the braid pattern, the lotus-circle garland,

287.s:
pañcolūkhalikā kāryā garvitāste 'tikīrtitāḥ(1) /
saṃkṣiptañcaiva vikṣiptaṃ kuñcitañca yathācitam(2) //
287.d:
पञ्चोलूखलिका कार्या गर्वितास्ते ऽतिकीर्तिताः(1) /
संक्षिप्तञ्चैव विक्षिप्तं कुञ्चितञ्च यथाचितम्(2) //
287.m: and the five mortar-courses should be performed; these are described as proud. / The contracted, the expanded, the bent, according as it is arranged,

287.s:
valgitāvalgitau caiva ṣoṭā cetthamudāhṛtam /
vīthīdhanuḥśataṃ yāvadaśītir navatis tathā //
287.d:
वल्गितावल्गितौ चैव षोटा चेत्थमुदाहृतम् /
वीथीधनुःशतं यावदशीतिर् नवतिस् तथा //
287.m: the cantering, galloping, and trotting: thus it is proclaimed. / The track may be up to one hundred bow-lengths, or eighty or ninety.

287.s:
bhadraḥ susādhyo vājī syānmando daṇḍaikamānasaḥ /
mṛgajaṅgho(3) mṛgo vājī saṅkīrṇastatsamanviyāt //
287.d:
भद्रः सुसाध्यो वाजी स्यान्मन्दो दण्डैकमानसः /
मृगजङ्घो(3) मृगो वाजी सङ्कीर्णस्तत्समन्वियात् //
287.m: The Bhadra horse is easily trained; the Manda is set only upon the stick; / the Mṛga horse has deer-like shanks; and the mixed breed shares their qualities.

287.s:
śarkarāmadhulājādaḥ sugandho 'śvaḥ śucirdvijaḥ /
tejasvī kṣatriyaścāśbo vinīto buddhimāṃś ca yaḥ //
287.d:
शर्करामधुलाजादः सुगन्धो ऽश्वः शुचिर्द्विजः /
तेजस्वी क्षत्रियश्चाश्बो विनीतो बुद्धिमांश् च यः //
287.m: A horse that eats sugar, honey, and parched grain, sweet-smelling and clean, is a brāhmaṇa. / A horse that is spirited, disciplined, and intelligent is a kṣatriya.

287.s:
śūdro 'śuciś calo mando virūpo vimatiḥ khalaḥ /
valgayā dhāryamāṇo 'śvo lālakaṃ yaś ca darśayet //
287.d:
शूद्रो ऽशुचिश् चलो मन्दो विरूपो विमतिः खलः /
वल्गया धार्यमाणो ऽश्वो लालकं यश् च दर्शयेत् //
287.m: A śūdra horse is unclean, unsteady, dull, deformed, unintelligent, and vicious. / A horse that, when restrained with the bridle, reveals its saliva,

287.s:
dhārāsu yojanīyo 'sau pragrahagrahamokṣaṇaiḥ /
aśvādilakṣaṇam vakṣye śālihotro yathāvadat //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe aśvavāhanasāro nāma
saptāśītyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:n
1 gorjitāste 'tikīrtitā iti kha..
2 yathāñcitamiti ña..
3 mṛgañjaya iti kha.. , ña.. ca
:p 70
:ś athāṣṭāśītyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
aśvacikitsā
śālihotra uvāca
aśvānāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ vakṣye
cikitsāñcaiva(1)suśrutaAP_288.001ab/
287.d:
धारासु योजनीयो ऽसौ प्रग्रहग्रहमोक्षणैः /
अश्वादिलक्षणम् वक्ष्ये शालिहोत्रो यथावदत् //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे अश्ववाहनसारो नाम
सप्ताशीत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:न्
1 गोर्जितास्ते ऽतिकीर्तिता इति ख..
2 यथाञ्चितमिति ञ..
3 मृगञ्जय इति ख.. , ञ.. च
:प् 70
:श् अथाष्टाशीत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
अश्वचिकित्सा
शालिहोत्र उवाच
अश्वानां लक्षणं वक्ष्ये
चिकित्साञ्चैव(1)सुश्रुतअप्_288.001अब्/
287.m:
should be trained in the paces by tightening and releasing the reins. / I shall describe the characteristics of horses and other animals, as told by Śālihotra.
Thus ends the two hundred and eighty-seventh chapter, entitled “The Essence of Horsemanship,” in the Mahāpurāṇa of Agni.
[Notes]
1. Variant reading: "gorjitāste 'tikīrtitāḥ" in manuscript kha.
2. Variant reading: "yathāñcitam" in manuscript ña.
3. Variant reading: "mṛgañjayaḥ" in manuscripts kha and ña. / [Page 70]
Now, the two hundred and eighty-eighth chapter.
Medical Treatment of Horses
Śālihotra said:
I shall state the characteristics of horses,
and their treatment, O Suśruta. / [288.1ab]

288.s: hīnadanto vidantaś cakarālī kṛṣṇatālukaḥ //
288.d: हीनदन्तो विदन्तश् चकराली कृष्णतालुकः //
288.m: A horse that has deficient teeth, is toothless, has protruding teeth, or has a black palate,

288.s:
kṛṣṇajihvaś ca yamajojātamuṣkaś ca yas tathā /
dviśaphaś ca tathā śṛṅgī trivarṇo vyāghravarṇakaḥ //
288.d:
कृष्णजिह्वश् च यमजोजातमुष्कश् च यस् तथा /
द्विशफश् च तथा शृङ्गी त्रिवर्णो व्याघ्रवर्णकः //
288.m: or has a black tongue, is born a twin, or has congenital testicle abnormalities, / or has split hooves, or has horns, or is tri-colored, or tiger-colored,

288.s:
kharavarṇo bhasmavarṇo jātavarṇaś ca kākudī /
śvitrī ca kākasādī ca kharasārastathaiva ca //
288.d:
खरवर्णो भस्मवर्णो जातवर्णश् च काकुदी /
श्वित्री च काकसादी च खरसारस्तथैव च //
288.m: or is donkey-colored, ash-colored, congenital-colored, or has a hump on the palate, / or has white leprosy, or has a raven's walk, or has the strength of an ass,

288.s:
vānarākṣaḥ kṛṣṇaśaṭaḥ kṛṣṇaguhyastathaiva ca /
kṛṣṇaprothaś ca śūkaś ca yaś ca tittirisannibhaḥ //
288.d:
वानराक्षः कृष्णशटः कृष्णगुह्यस्तथैव च /
कृष्णप्रोथश् च शूकश् च यश् च तित्तिरिसन्निभः //
288.m: or has monkey-eyes, a black mane, or a black anus, / or a black muzzle, or is bristly, or resembles a partridge,

288.s:
viṣamaḥ śvetapādaś ca dhruvāvartavivarjitaḥ /
aśubhāvartasaṃyukto varjanīyasturaṅgamaḥ //
288.d:
विषमः श्वेतपादश् च ध्रुवावर्तविवर्जितः /
अशुभावर्तसंयुक्तो वर्जनीयस्तुरङ्गमः //
288.m: or has uneven white legs, or is devoid of auspicious whorls, / or is endowed with inauspicious whorls, such a horse is to be shunned.

288.s:
randhroparandhrayordvau dvau dvau dvau mastakavakṣasoḥ /
prayāṇe ca lalāṭe ca kaṇṭhāvartāḥ śubhā daśa //
288.d:
रन्ध्रोपरन्ध्रयोर्द्वौ द्वौ द्वौ द्वौ मस्तकवक्षसोः /
प्रयाणे च ललाटे च कण्ठावर्ताः शुभा दश //
288.m: Two whorls each on the nostrils and upper nostrils, two each on the crown of the head and the chest, / one on the seat of the saddle and one on the forehead, and two on the neck: these ten whorls are auspicious.

288.s:
mṛkkaṇyāñca lalāṭe ca karṇamūle nigālake /
bāhumūle gale śreṣṭhā āvartāstvaśubhāḥ pare //
288.d:
मृक्कण्याञ्च ललाटे च कर्णमूले निगालके /
बाहुमूले गले श्रेष्ठा आवर्तास्त्वशुभाः परे //
288.m: Whorls at the corners of the mouth, on the forehead, at the base of the ears, at the throat, / at the base of the shoulders, and on the neck are excellent; other whorls are inauspicious.

288.s:
śukendragopacandrābhā ye ca vāyasasannibhāḥ /
suvarṇavarṇāḥ snigdhāś ca praśasyāstu sadaiva hi //
288.d:
शुकेन्द्रगोपचन्द्राभा ये च वायससन्निभाः /
सुवर्णवर्णाः स्निग्धाश् च प्रशस्यास्तु सदैव हि //
288.m: Those with the color of a parrot, an indragopa insect, or the moon, or resembling a crow, / golden-colored and glossy: these are always praiseworthy.

288.s:
dīrghagrīvākṣikūṭāś ca hrasvakarṇāś ca śobhanāḥ /
:n
1 cikitsantaveti ña..
:p 71
rākṣānturaṅgamā yatra(1) vijayaṃ varjayettataḥ //
288.d:
दीर्घग्रीवाक्षिकूटाश् च ह्रस्वकर्णाश् च शोभनाः /
:न्
1 चिकित्सन्तवेति ञ..
:प् 71
राक्षान्तुरङ्गमा यत्र(1) विजयं वर्जयेत्ततः //
288.m:
Those with long necks, well-formed eye-sockets, and short ears are handsome.
[Notes]
1. Variant reading: "cikitsantave" in manuscript ña. / [Page 71]
Where horses are monstrous, victory should be considered lost.

288.s:
pālitastu hayo dantī śubhado duḥkhado 'nyathā /
śriyaḥ putrāstu gandharvā vājino ratnamuttamam //
288.d:
पालितस्तु हयो दन्ती शुभदो दुःखदो ऽन्यथा /
श्रियः पुत्रास्तु गन्धर्वा वाजिनो रत्नमुत्तमम् //
288.m: A properly cared-for horse and elephant grant good fortune, but otherwise they bring sorrow. / For horses are the sons of Śrī, the Gandharvas; they are the supreme gem.

288.s:
aśvamedhe tu turagaḥ pavitratvāttu hūyate /
