vṛṣo nimbavṛhatyau ca guḍūcī ca samākṣikā //
288.d:
अश्वमेधे तु तुरगः पवित्रत्वात्तु हूयते /
वृषो निम्बवृहत्यौ च गुडूची च समाक्षिका //
288.m: In the horse-sacrifice, the steed is offered because of its purity. / Malabar nut, neem, the two nightshades, guḍūcī, together with honey,

288.s:
siṃhā gandhakārī piṇḍī svedaś ca śirasas tathā /
hiṅgu puṣkaramūlañca nāgaraṃ sāmlavetasaṃ //
288.d:
सिंहा गन्धकारी पिण्डी स्वेदश् च शिरसस् तथा /
हिङ्गु पुष्करमूलञ्च नागरं साम्लवेतसं //
288.m: siṃhī, gandhakārī, piṇḍī, and fomentation of the head; / asafetida, costus root, dry ginger, with sour wild cane,

288.s:
pippalīsaindhavayutaṃ śūlaghnaṃ cīṣṇavāriṇā /
nāgarātiviṣā mustā sānantā bilvamālikā //
288.d:
पिप्पलीसैन्धवयुतं शूलघ्नं चीष्णवारिणा /
नागरातिविषा मुस्ता सानन्ता बिल्वमालिका //
288.m: combined with long pepper and rock salt, taken with warm water, cures colic. / Dry ginger, aconite, nut grass, together with anantā and the garland of bilva,

288.s:
kvāthameṣāṃ pivedvājī sarvātīsāranāśanam /
priyaṅgusārivābhyāñca yuktamājaṃ śṛtaṃ(2) payaḥ //
288.d:
क्वाथमेषां पिवेद्वाजी सर्वातीसारनाशनम् /
प्रियङ्गुसारिवाभ्याञ्च युक्तमाजं शृतं(2) पयः //
288.m: the horse should drink a decoction of these: it cures all forms of diarrhea. / Boiled goat's milk combined with priyaṅgu and sārivā,

288.s:
paryāptaśarkaraṃ pītvā śramādvājī vimucyate /
droṇikāyāntu dātavyā tailavastisturaṅgame //
288.d:
पर्याप्तशर्करं पीत्वा श्रमाद्वाजी विमुच्यते /
द्रोणिकायान्तु दातव्या तैलवस्तिस्तुरङ्गमे //
288.m: drunk with sufficient sugar, frees the horse from exhaustion. / An oil enema should be administered to the horse in a trough,

288.s:
koṣṭhajā ca śirā vedhyā tena tasya sukhaṃ bhavet /
dāṛimaṃ triphalā vyoṣaṃ guḍañca samabhāvikam //
288.d:
कोष्ठजा च शिरा वेध्या तेन तस्य सुखं भवेत् /
दाऋइमं त्रिफला व्योषं गुडञ्च समभाविकम् //
288.m: and the vein arising from the belly should be pierced; by that, relief will come to it. / Pomegranate, the three fruits, the three spices, and jaggery in equal portions:

288.s:
piṇḍametat pradātavyamaśvānāṃ kāśanāśanam /
priyaṅgulodhramadhubhiḥ pivedvṛṣarasaṃ hayaḥ //
288.d:
पिण्डमेतत् प्रदातव्यमश्वानां काशनाशनम् /
प्रियङ्गुलोध्रमधुभिः पिवेद्वृषरसं हयः //
288.m: this bolus should be given to destroy cough in horses. / The horse should drink the juice of Malabar nut with priyaṅgu, lodhra, and honey,

288.s:
kṣīraṃ vā pañcakolādyaṃ kāśanāddhi pramucyate /
praskandheṣu ca sarveṣu śreya ādau viśodhaṇam //
288.d:
क्षीरं वा पञ्चकोलाद्यं काशनाद्धि प्रमुच्यते /
प्रस्कन्धेषु च सर्वेषु श्रेय आदौ विशोधणम् //
288.m: or milk cooked with the five spices: then it is indeed freed from cough. / In all cases of severe diarrhea, purgation is beneficial at first.

288.s:
abhyaṅgodvartanaiḥ snehaṃ nasyavartikramaḥ smṛtaḥ /
jvaritānāṃ turaṅgāṇāṃ payasaiva kriyākramaḥ //
288.d:
अभ्यङ्गोद्वर्तनैः स्नेहं नस्यवर्तिक्रमः स्मृतः /
ज्वरितानां तुरङ्गाणां पयसैव क्रियाक्रमः //
288.m: Unction by massage and body-anointing, and the course of nasal drops and suppositories are taught. / For horses suffering from fever, the regimen consists of milk alone.

288.s:
lodhrakandharayormūlaṃ mātulāṅgāgnināgarāḥ /
:n
1 rājñīturaṅgamā yatreti kha..
2 ghṛtamiti kha..
:p 72
kuṣṭhahiṅguvacārāsnālepoyaṃ śothanāśanaḥ //
288.d:
लोध्रकन्धरयोर्मूलं मातुलाङ्गाग्निनागराः /
:न्
1 राज्ञीतुरङ्गमा यत्रेति ख..
2 घृतमिति ख..
:प् 72
कुष्ठहिङ्गुवचारास्नालेपोयं शोथनाशनः //
288.m:
The root of lodhra and leadwort, citron, leadwort, and dry ginger,
[Notes]
1. Variant reading: "rājñīturaṅgamā yatra" in manuscript kha.
2. Variant reading: "ghṛtam" in manuscript kha. / [Page 72]
with costus, asafetida, sweet flag, and rāsnā: this paste cures swellings.

288.s:
mañjiṣṭhā madhukaṃ drākṣāvṛhatyau raktacandanam /
trapuṣīvījamūlāni śṛṅgāṭakakaśerukam //
288.d:
मञ्जिष्ठा मधुकं द्राक्षावृहत्यौ रक्तचन्दनम् /
त्रपुषीवीजमूलानि शृङ्गाटककशेरुकम् //
288.m: Indian madder, liquorice, raisins, the two nightshades, red sandalwood, / seeds and roots of cucumber, water chestnut, and kaśeruka:

288.s:
ajāpayaḥśṛtamidaṃ suśītaṃ śarkarānvitaṃ /
pītvā nīraśano vājī raktamehāt pramucyate //
288.d:
अजापयःशृतमिदं सुशीतं शर्करान्वितं /
पीत्वा नीरशनो वाजी रक्तमेहात् प्रमुच्यते //
288.m: boiled in goat's milk, thoroughly cooled, and mixed with sugar, / when drunk by a horse that has fasted, frees it from bloody urinary disease.

288.s:
manyāhanunigālasthaśirāśotho galagrahaḥ /
abhyaṅgaḥ kaṭutailena(1) tatra teṣveva śasyate //
288.d:
मन्याहनुनिगालस्थशिराशोथो गलग्रहः /
अभ्यङ्गः कटुतैलेन(1) तत्र तेष्वेव शस्यते //
288.m: For swelling of the veins situated in the nape of the neck, jaw, and throat, known as galagraha, / massage with pungent mustard oil is praised in those very conditions.

288.s:
galagrahagado śothaḥ prāyaśo galadeśake /
pratyakpuṣpī tathā bahniḥ saindhavaṃ sauraso rasaḥ //
288.d:
गलग्रहगदो शोथः प्रायशो गलदेशके /
प्रत्यक्पुष्पी तथा बह्निः सैन्धवं सौरसो रसः //
288.m: In the disease galagraha, swelling occurs mostly in the region of the throat. / Chaff-flower, as well as leadwort, rock salt, and basil juice:

288.s:
kṛṣṇāhiṅguyutair ebhiḥ kṛtvā nasyaṃ na sīdati /
niśe jyotiṣmatī pāṭhā kṛṣṇā kuṣṭhaṃ vacā madhu //
288.d:
कृष्णाहिङ्गुयुतैर् एभिः कृत्वा नस्यं न सीदति /
निशे ज्योतिष्मती पाठा कृष्णा कुष्ठं वचा मधु //
288.m: having administered a nasal medication with these together with black pepper and asafetida, it does not fail. / The two turmerics, jyotiṣmatī, pāṭhā, black pepper, costus, sweet flag, and honey:

288.s:
jihvāstambhe ca lepo 'yaṃ guḍamūtrayuto hitaḥ /
tilair yaṣṭyā rajanyā ca nimbapatraiś ca yojitā //
288.d:
जिह्वास्तम्भे च लेपो ऽयं गुडमूत्रयुतो हितः /
तिलैर् यष्ट्या रजन्या च निम्बपत्रैश् च योजिता //
288.m: this paste mixed with jaggery and cow-urine is beneficial in stiffness of the tongue. / Sesame seeds, liquorice, turmeric, and neem leaves combined,

288.s:
kṣaudreṇa śodhanī piṇḍī sarpiṣā vraṇaropaṇī /
abhighātena khañjanti ye hy aścāstīvravedanāḥ //
288.d:
क्षौद्रेण शोधनी पिण्डी सर्पिषा व्रणरोपणी /
अभिघातेन खञ्जन्ति ये ह्य् अश्चास्तीव्रवेदनाः //
288.m: made into a bolus with honey cleanses wounds; with ghee, it heals wounds. / Horses that limp due to injury and suffer severe pain

288.s:
pariṣekakriyā teṣāṃ tailenāśu rujāpahā /
doṣakopābhighātābhyāṃ pakvabhinne vraṇakramaḥ //
288.d:
परिषेकक्रिया तेषां तैलेनाशु रुजापहा /
दोषकोपाभिघाताभ्यां पक्वभिन्ने व्रणक्रमः //
288.m: have their pain quickly removed by irrigation with oil. / In wounds that have ripened and burst due to aggravation of the humors or injury, the wound regimen applies.

288.s: aśvatthoḍumbaraplakṣamadhūkavaṭakalkanaiḥ //29//
288.d: अश्वत्थोडुम्बरप्लक्षमधूकवटकल्कनैः //29//
288.m: With pastes of sacred fig, glomerous fig, wavy-leaved fig, madhūka, and banyan: //29

288.s:
prabhūtasalilaḥ kvāthaḥ sukhoṣṇaḥ vraṇaśodhanaḥ /
śatāhvā nāgaraṃ rāsnā mañjiṣṭhākuṣṭhasaindhavaiḥ //
288.d:
प्रभूतसलिलः क्वाथः सुखोष्णः व्रणशोधनः /
शताह्वा नागरं रास्ना मञ्जिष्ठाकुष्ठसैन्धवैः //
288.m: a warm decoction with copious water cleanses wounds. / Dill, dry ginger, rāsnā, Indian madder, costus, and rock salt,

288.s:
devadāruvacāyugmarajanīraktacandanaiḥ /
tailasiddhaṃ kaṣāyeṇa guḍūcyāḥ payasā saha //
:n
1 tilataileneti kha..
:p 73
288.d:
देवदारुवचायुग्मरजनीरक्तचन्दनैः /
तैलसिद्धं कषायेण गुडूच्याः पयसा सह //
:न्
1 तिलतैलेनेति ख..
:प् 73
288.m:
deodar cedar, the two varieties of sweet flag, the two turmerics, and red sandalwood, / cooked in oil with a decoction of guḍūcī together with milk,
[Footnote]
[Variant: 'tilatailena' in ms. kha...] / [page 73]

288.s:
mrakṣeṇa vastinaśye ca yojyaṃ sarvatra liṅgine /
raktasrāvo jalaukābhir netrānte netrarogitaḥ //
288.d:
म्रक्षेण वस्तिनश्ये च योज्यं सर्वत्र लिङ्गिने /
रक्तस्रावो जलौकाभिर् नेत्रान्ते नेत्ररोगितः //
288.m: With anointing, enema, and nasal drops, it is to be applied in all cases to one suffering from symptoms. / Bleeding [should be induced] by leeches at the corner of the eye for one suffering from eye disease.

288.s:
khāditoḍumbarāśvatthakaṣāyeṇa ca sādhanam /
dhātrīdurālabhātiktāpriyaṅgukuṅkumaiḥ samaiḥ //
288.d:
खादितोडुम्बराश्वत्थकषायेण च साधनम् /
धात्रीदुरालभातिक्ताप्रियङ्गुकुङ्कुमैः समैः //
288.m: And treatment [is performed] with a decoction of khādira, uḍumbara, and aśvattha; / with equal parts of dhātrī, durālabhā, tiktā, priyaṅgu, and saffron,

288.s:
guḍūcyā ca kṛtaḥ kalko hito yuktāvalambine /
utpāte ca śile śrāvye śuṣkaśephe tathaiva ca //
288.d:
गुडूच्या च कृतः कल्को हितो युक्तावलम्बिने /
उत्पाते च शिले श्राव्ये शुष्कशेफे तथैव च //
288.m: and a paste made with guḍūcī is beneficial for one suffering from swelling of the joints. / And in case of a sprain, a stone [in the bladder], an ear discharge, and likewise an emaciated penis,

288.s:
kṣiprakāriṇi doṣe ca sadyo vidalamiṣyate(1) /
gośakṛnmañjikākuṣṭharajanītilamarṣapaiḥ //
288.d:
क्षिप्रकारिणि दोषे च सद्यो विदलमिष्यते(1) /
गोशकृन्मञ्जिकाकुष्ठरजनीतिलमर्षपैः //
288.m: and when the humour is swift-acting, an immediate splitting [or incision] is desired. / With cow dung, mañjiṣṭhā, kuṣṭha, turmeric, sesame seeds, and mustard,

288.s:
gavāṃ mūtreṇa piṣṭaiś ca mardanaṃ kaṇḍunāśanam /
śīto madhuyutaḥ kvātho nāśikāyāṃ saśarkaraḥ //
288.d:
गवां मूत्रेण पिष्टैश् च मर्दनं कण्डुनाशनम् /
शीतो मधुयुतः क्वाथो नाशिकायां सशर्करः //
288.m: ground with cow urine, inunction destroys itching. / A cold decoction combined with honey and sugar, [applied] in the nostril,

288.s:
raktapittaharaḥ pānādaśvakarṇaistathaiva ca /
saptame saptame deyamaśvānāṃ lavaṇaṃ dine //
288.d:
रक्तपित्तहरः पानादश्वकर्णैस्तथैव च /
सप्तमे सप्तमे देयमश्वानां लवणं दिने //
288.m: removes bleeding disorders when drunk, and likewise with aśvakarṇa. / Salt should be given to horses on every seventh day.

288.s:
tathā bhuktavatāndeyā atipāne tu vāruṇī /
jīvanīyaiḥ samadhurair mṛdvīkāśarkarāyutaiḥ //
288.d:
तथा भुक्तवतान्देया अतिपाने तु वारुणी /
जीवनीयैः समधुरैर् मृद्वीकाशर्करायुतैः //
288.m: Likewise, vāruṇī [liquor] should be given after eating to those that drink excessively. / In autumn, an after-drink [should be given] with vitalising sweet [herbs],

288.s:
sapippalīkaiḥ śaradi pratipānaṃ sapadmakaiḥ /
viḍaṅgāpippalīdhānyaśatāhvālodhrasaindhavaiḥ //
288.d:
सपिप्पलीकैः शरदि प्रतिपानं सपद्मकैः /
विडङ्गापिप्पलीधान्यशताह्वालोध्रसैन्धवैः //
288.m: combined with raisins and sugar, along with pippalī and lotus petals; / at the onset of winter, an after-drink for horses [should be prepared] with viḍaṅga, pippalī, coriander, śatāhvā, lodhra, rock salt,

288.s:
macitrakaisturaṅgāṇāṃ pratipānaṃ himāgame /
lodhrapriyaṅgukāmustāpippalīviśvabheṣajaiḥ //
288.d:
मचित्रकैस्तुरङ्गाणां प्रतिपानं हिमागमे /
लोध्रप्रियङ्गुकामुस्तापिप्पलीविश्वभेषजैः //
288.m: and with citraka; / with lodhra, priyaṅgu, mustā, pippalī, and ginger,

288.s:
sakṣaudraiḥ pratipānaṃ syādvasante kaphanāśanam /
priyaṅgupippalīlodhrayaṣṭyākṣaiḥ samahauṣadhaiḥ //
288.d:
सक्षौद्रैः प्रतिपानं स्याद्वसन्ते कफनाशनम् /
प्रियङ्गुपिप्पलीलोध्रयष्ट्याक्षैः समहौषधैः //
288.m: along with honey, the after-drink in spring destroys phlegm; / with priyaṅgu, pippalī, lodhra, yaṣṭyāhva, akṣa, and ginger,

288.s:
nidāghe saguḍā deyā madirā pratipānake /
:n
vedhanamisyata iti ja.. , ña.. ca
:p 74
lodhrakāṣṭhaṃ salavaṇaṃ pippalyo viśvabheṣajam //
288.d:
निदाघे सगुडा देया मदिरा प्रतिपानके /
:न्
वेधनमिस्यत इति ज.. , ञ.. च
:प् 74
लोध्रकाष्ठं सलवणं पिप्पल्यो विश्वभेषजम् //
288.m:
in summer, wine with jaggery should be given as an after-drink.
[Footnote]
[Variant: 'vedhanam iṣyate' in mss. ja and ña...] / [page 74]
Lodhra wood with salt, pippalī, and ginger—

288.s:
bhavettailayutair ebhiḥ pratipānaṃ ghanāgame /
nidāghodvṛtapittārtāḥ śaratsu puṣṭaśoṇitāḥ //
288.d:
भवेत्तैलयुतैर् एभिः प्रतिपानं घनागमे /
निदाघोद्वृतपित्तार्ताः शरत्सु पुष्टशोणिताः //
288.m: an after-drink prepared with these together with oil is [prescribed] at the onset of the monsoon. / Horses afflicted by pitta aggravated in summer, whose blood is replenished in autumn,

288.s:
prāvṛḍbhinnapurīṣāś ca piveyurvājino ghṛtam /
piveyurvājinastailaṃ kaphavāyvadhikāstu ye //
288.d:
प्रावृड्भिन्नपुरीषाश् च पिवेयुर्वाजिनो घृतम् /
पिवेयुर्वाजिनस्तैलं कफवाय्वधिकास्तु ये //
288.m: and who suffer from loose stools in the rainy season, should drink ghee; / while horses that have an excess of phlegm and wind should drink oil.

288.s:
snehavyāpadbhavo yeṣāṃ kāryaṃ teṣāṃ virūkṣaṇam /
tryahaṃ yavāgūrūkṣā syād bhojanaṃ takrasaṃyutam //
288.d:
स्नेहव्यापद्भवो येषां कार्यं तेषां विरूक्षणम् /
त्र्यहं यवागूरूक्षा स्याद् भोजनं तक्रसंयुतम् //
288.m: For those in whom disorders arise from oleation, drying therapy should be administered: / for three days there should be dry gruel, and food combined with buttermilk.

288.s:
śarannidāghayoḥ sarpistailaṃ śītavasantayoḥ /
varṣāsu śiśire caiva vastau yamakamiṣyate //
288.d:
शरन्निदाघयोः सर्पिस्तैलं शीतवसन्तयोः /
वर्षासु शिशिरे चैव वस्तौ यमकमिष्यते //
288.m: Ghee [is recommended] in autumn and summer, and oil in the cold season and spring; / in the rainy season and dewy season, a combination of both is desired in an enema.

288.s:
gurvabhiṣyandibhaktāni vyāyāmaṃ snājamātapam /
vāyuvarjañca vāhasya snehapītasya varjitam //
288.d:
गुर्वभिष्यन्दिभक्तानि व्यायामं स्नाजमातपम् /
वायुवर्जञ्च वाहस्य स्नेहपीतस्य वर्जितम् //
288.m: Heavy, channel-blocking foods, physical exercise, bathing, and sunlight / are forbidden to a horse that has drunk oleaginous substance, except for fresh air.

288.s:
snānaṃ pānaṃ śakṛtkrūṣṭhamaśvānāṃ salilāgame /
atyarthaṃ durdine kāle pānamekaṃ praśasyate //
288.d:
स्नानं पानं शकृत्क्रूष्ठमश्वानां सलिलागमे /
अत्यर्थं दुर्दिने काले पानमेकं प्रशस्यते //
288.m: At the onset of the rains, a single bath and drink are prescribed for horses; / in excessively cloudy weather, a single drink is recommended.

288.s:
yuktaśītātape kāle dviḥpānaṃ snapanaṃ sakṛt /
grīṣme trisnānapānaṃ syacciraṃ tasyāyagāhanam //
288.d:
युक्तशीतातपे काले द्विःपानं स्नपनं सकृत् /
ग्रीष्मे त्रिस्नानपानं स्यच्चिरं तस्यायगाहनम् //
288.m: In season with moderate cold and sunshine, drinking twice and bathing once [is proper]; / in summer, drinking and bathing three times, and long immersion [in water].

288.s:
nistūṣāṇāṃ pradātavyā yavānāṃ caturāṭakī /
caṇakavrīhimaudgāni kalāyaṃ vāpi dāpayet //
288.d:
निस्तूषाणां प्रदातव्या यवानां चतुराटकी /
चणकव्रीहिमौद्गानि कलायं वापि दापयेत् //
288.m: Four āḍhakas of husked barley should be given; / or one should give chickpeas, rice, green gram, or peas.

288.s:
ahorātreṇa cārdhasya yavasasya tulā daśa /
aṣṭau śuṣkasya dātavyāś catasro 'tha vuṣasya vā //
288.d:
अहोरात्रेण चार्धस्य यवसस्य तुला दश /
अष्टौ शुष्कस्य दातव्याश् चतस्रो ऽथ वुषस्य वा //
288.m: And in a day and night, ten tulās of half-[dried] grass [should be given], / eight [tulās] of dry [grass] should be given, or four of chaff.

288.s:
dūrvā pittaṃ yavaḥ kāsaṃ vuṣaś ca śloṣmasañcayam /
nāśayatyarjunaḥ śvāsaṃ tathā māno balakṣayam //
288.d:
दूर्वा पित्तं यवः कासं वुषश् च श्लोष्मसञ्चयम् /
नाशयत्यर्जुनः श्वासं तथा मानो बलक्षयम् //
288.m: Dūrvā destroys pitta, barley destroys cough, and chaff destroys accumulation of phlegm; / arjuna destroys shortness of breath, and likewise māna destroys loss of strength.

288.s:
vātikāḥ paittikāś caiva śleṣmajāḥ sānnipātikāḥ /
na rogāḥ pīḍayiṣyanti dūrvāhāranturaṅgamam //
:p 75
288.d:
वातिकाः पैत्तिकाश् चैव श्लेष्मजाः सान्निपातिकाः /
न रोगाः पीडयिष्यन्ति दूर्वाहारन्तुरङ्गमम् //
:प् 75
288.m:
Diseases born of wind, pitta, phlegm, and all three combined / will not afflict a horse that feeds on dūrvā grass.
[page 75]

288.s:
dvau rajjubandhau duṣṭānāṃ pakṣayorubhayorapi /
paścāddhanuś ca kartarvyo dūrakīlavyapāśrayaḥ //
288.d:
द्वौ रज्जुबन्धौ दुष्टानां पक्षयोरुभयोरपि /
पश्चाद्धनुश् च कर्तर्व्यो दूरकीलव्यपाश्रयः //
288.m: Two rope-bindings on both flanks [should be arranged] for vicious [horses], / and behind, a bow[-shaped cord] supported by distant pegs should be made.

288.s:
vāseyustvāstṛte sthāne kṛtadhūpanabhūmayaḥ /
yatropanyastayavasāḥ sapradīpāḥ surakṣitāḥ /
kṛkavākvajakapayo dhāryaścāśvagṛhe mṛgāḥ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe aśvāyurvedo
nāmāṣṭāśītyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:ś athonanavatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
aśvaśāntiḥ
288.d:
वासेयुस्त्वास्तृते स्थाने कृतधूपनभूमयः /
यत्रोपन्यस्तयवसाः सप्रदीपाः सुरक्षिताः /
कृकवाक्वजकपयो धार्यश्चाश्वगृहे मृगाः //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे अश्वायुर्वेदो
नामाष्टाशीत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
:श् अथोननवत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
अश्वशान्तिः
288.m:
They should dwell in an enclosed stall, on grounds that have been fumigated, / where fodder is supplied, provided with lamps, and well guarded; / roosters, goats, monkeys, and deer should be kept in the horse stable.
Thus ends the two hundred and eighty-eighth chapter, called The Medicine of Horses, in the Great Agni Purāṇa.
Now begins the two hundred and eighty-ninth chapter:
Pacification Rites for Horses.

289.s:
śālihotra uvāca
aśvaśāntiṃ pravakṣyāmi vajirogavimardanīṃ /
nityāṃ naimittakīṃ kamyāṃ trividhāṃ śṛṇu suśruta //
289.d:
शालिहोत्र उवाच
अश्वशान्तिं प्रवक्ष्यामि वजिरोगविमर्दनीं /
नित्यां नैमित्तकीं कम्यां त्रिविधां शृणु सुश्रुत //
289.m:
Śālihotra said:
I shall explain the pacification rite for horses that crushes equine diseases.
Listen, Suśruta, to the three kinds: regular, occasional, and for specific desires.

289.s:
śubhe dine śrīdharañca śriyamuccaiḥśravāś ca taṃ /
hayarājaṃ samabhyarcya sāvitrair jujuyādghṛtaṃ //
289.d:
शुभे दिने श्रीधरञ्च श्रियमुच्चैःश्रवाश् च तं /
हयराजं समभ्यर्च्य सावित्रैर् जुजुयाद्घृतं //
289.m:
On an auspicious day, having worshipped Śrīdhara, Śrī, and Uccaiḥśravas,
and that king of horses, one should offer ghee [into the fire] with mantras to Savitṛ.

289.s:
dvijebhyo dakṣiṇāndadyādaśvavṛddhis tathā bhavet /
aśvayuk śuklapakṣasya pañcadaśyāñca śāntikaṃ //
289.d:
द्विजेभ्यो दक्षिणान्दद्यादश्ववृद्धिस् तथा भवेत् /
अश्वयुक् शुक्लपक्षस्य पञ्चदश्याञ्च शान्तिकं //
289.m:
One should give a sacrificial fee to twice-borns; thereby increase of horses will occur.
And on the fifteenth day of the bright fortnight of the month of Āśvina, the pacification rite

289.s:
vahiḥ kuryādviśeṣeṇa nāsatyau varuṇaṃ yajet /
samullikhya tato devīṃ śākhābhiḥ parivārayet //
289.d:
वहिः कुर्याद्विशेषेण नासत्यौ वरुणं यजेत् /
समुल्लिख्य ततो देवीं शाखाभिः परिवारयेत् //
289.m:
should be performed outside [the city] in particular. One should worship the two Nāsatyas and Varuṇa.
Having drawn [an image of] the goddess, one should surround it with branches.

289.s:
ghatānsarvarasaiḥ pūrṇān dikṣu dadyātsavastrakān /
yavājyaṃ juhuyāt prārcya yajedaśvāṃś ca sāśvinān //
:p 76
289.d:
घतान्सर्वरसैः पूर्णान् दिक्षु दद्यात्सवस्त्रकान् /
यवाज्यं जुहुयात् प्रार्च्य यजेदश्वांश् च साश्विनान् //
:प् 76
289.m:
One should place pots filled with all fluids, wrapped in cloth, in the cardinal directions.
Having worshipped, one should offer barley and ghee [into the fire], and worship the horses along with the Aśvins.
[Page 76]

289.s:
viprebhyo dakṣiṇāndadyānnaimittikamataḥ śṛṇu /
makarādau hayānāñca padmair viṣṇuṃ śriyaṃ yajet //
289.d:
विप्रेभ्यो दक्षिणान्दद्यान्नैमित्तिकमतः शृणु /
मकरादौ हयानाञ्च पद्मैर् विष्णुं श्रियं यजेत् //
289.m:
One should give a sacrificial fee to Brahmins. Now hear the occasional [rite].
At the entrance [of the sun] into Capricorn and other [astrological occasions], one should worship Viṣṇu and Śrī with lotuses for the sake of horses,

289.s:
brahmāṇaṃ śaṅkaraṃ somamādityañca tathāśvinau /
revantamuccaiḥśravasandikpālāṃś ca daleṣvapi //
289.d:
ब्रह्माणं शङ्करं सोममादित्यञ्च तथाश्विनौ /
रेवन्तमुच्चैःश्रवसन्दिक्पालांश् च दलेष्वपि //
289.m:
as well as Brahmā, Śaṅkara, Soma, Āditya, and the two Aśvins,
Revanta, Uccaiḥśravas, and the regents of the directions on the petals [of the lotus].

289.s:
pratyekaṃ pūrṇakumbhaiś ca vedyāntatsaumyataḥ sthale /
tilākṣatājyasiddhārthān devatānāṃ śataṃ śataṃ /
upoṣitena kartavyaṃ karma cāsvarujāpahaṃ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe aśvaśāntirnāmonanavatyadhikadviśatatamo
'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha navatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
gajaśāntiḥ
289.d:
प्रत्येकं पूर्णकुम्भैश् च वेद्यान्तत्सौम्यतः स्थले /
तिलाक्षताज्यसिद्धार्थान् देवतानां शतं शतं /
उपोषितेन कर्तव्यं कर्म चास्वरुजापहं //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे अश्वशान्तिर्नामोननवत्यधिकद्विशततमो
ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ नवत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
गजशान्तिः
289.m:
Each [should be worshipped] with full pots on the altar, in a place to the north of it.
One who has fasted should perform the rite that removes equine illness,
[offering] sesame, unhusked rice, ghee, and white mustard seeds a hundred times for each of the deities.
Thus in the Mahāpurāṇa composed by Agni, the two hundred and eighty-ninth chapter, entitled “Pacification Rite for Horses.”
Now the two hundred and ninetieth chapter.
Pacification rite for elephants.

290.s:
śālihotra uvāca
gajaśāntiṃ pravakṣyāmi gajarogavimardanīm /
viṣṇuṃ śriyañca pañcamyāṃ nāgam airāvataṃ yajet //
290.d:
शालिहोत्र उवाच
गजशान्तिं प्रवक्ष्यामि गजरोगविमर्दनीम् /
विष्णुं श्रियञ्च पञ्चम्यां नागम् ऐरावतं यजेत् //
290.m:
Śālihotra said:
I shall explain the pacification rite for elephants that crushes elephant diseases.
On the fifth [lunar day], one should worship Viṣṇu, Śrī, and the elephant Airāvata,

290.s:
brahmāṇaṃ śaṅkaraṃ viṣṇuṃ śakraṃ vaiśnavaṇaṃyamaṃ /
candrārkau varuṇaṃ vāyumagniṃ pṛthvīṃ tathā ca khaṃ //
290.d:
ब्रह्माणं शङ्करं विष्णुं शक्रं वैश्नवणंयमं /
चन्द्रार्कौ वरुणं वायुमग्निं पृथ्वीं तथा च खं //
290.m:
Brahmā, Śaṅkara, Viṣṇu, Indra, Kubera, Yama,
the moon and the sun, Varuṇa, Vāyu, Agni, the earth, and space,

290.s:
śeṣaṃ śailān kuñjarāṃś ca ye te 'ṣṭau devayonayaḥ /
virupākṣaṃ mahāpadmaṃ bhadraṃ sumanasantathā //
290.d:
शेषं शैलान् कुञ्जरांश् च ये ते ऽष्टौ देवयोनयः /
विरुपाक्षं महापद्मं भद्रं सुमनसन्तथा //
290.m:
Śeṣa, the mountains, and those eight elephants that have divine origin:
Virūpākṣa, Mahāpadma, Bhadra, Sumanas,

290.s:
kumudairāvaṇaḥ padmaḥ puṣpadanto 'tha vāmanaḥ /
supratīkoñjano nāgā aṣṭau homo 'tha dakṣiṇāṃ //
:p 77
290.d:
कुमुदैरावणः पद्मः पुष्पदन्तो ऽथ वामनः /
सुप्रतीकोञ्जनो नागा अष्टौ होमो ऽथ दक्षिणां //
:प् 77
290.m:
Kumuda, Airāvaṇa, Padma, Puṣpadanta, Vāmana,
Supratīka, and Añjana. Then a fire oblation to the eight elephants, and a sacrificial fee.
[Page 77]

290.s:
gajāḥ śāntyudakāsiktā vṛddhau naimittikaṃ sṛṇu /
gajānāmmakarādau ca aiśānyāṃ nagarādvahiḥ //
290.d:
गजाः शान्त्युदकासिक्ता वृद्धौ नैमित्तिकं सृणु /
गजानाम्मकरादौ च ऐशान्यां नगराद्वहिः //
290.m:
Elephants sprinkled with pacifying water [prosper] in growth. Hear the occasional [rite].
For elephants, at the entrance [of the sun] into Capricorn and other [occasions], outside the city in the north-east,

290.s:
sthaṇḍile kamale madhye viṣṇuṃ lakṣmīñca keśare /
brahmāṇaṃ bhāskaraṃ pṛthvīṃ yajet skandaṃ hy anantakaṃ //
290.d:
स्थण्डिले कमले मध्ये विष्णुं लक्ष्मीञ्च केशरे /
ब्रह्माणं भास्करं पृथ्वीं यजेत् स्कन्दं ह्य् अनन्तकं //
290.m:
on an earthen altar, inside a lotus, one should worship Viṣṇu in the center and Lakṣmī on the pericarp;
Brahmā, the Sun, the Earth, Skanda, and Ananta;

290.s:
khaṃ śivaṃ somamindrādīṃstadastrāṇi dale kramāt /
vajraṃ śaktiñca daṇḍañca tomaraṃ pāśakaṃ gadāṃ //
290.d:
खं शिवं सोममिन्द्रादींस्तदस्त्राणि दले क्रमात् /
वज्रं शक्तिञ्च दण्डञ्च तोमरं पाशकं गदां //
290.m:
Space, Śiva, the Moon, Indra and the rest, and their weapons on the petals in order:
the thunderbolt, the spear, the staff, the javelin, the noose, the mace,

290.s:
śūlaṃ padmambahirvṛnte cakre sūryantathāśvinau /
vasūnaṣṭhau tathā sādhyān yāmye 'tha nairṛte dale //
290.d:
शूलं पद्मम्बहिर्वृन्ते चक्रे सूर्यन्तथाश्विनौ /
वसूनष्ठौ तथा साध्यान् याम्ये ऽथ नैरृते दले //
290.m:
the trident, and the lotus; on the outer stem and wheel, the Sun and the two Aśvins;
the eight Vasus and the Sādhyas on the southern and south-western petals;

290.s:
devānāṅgirasaścāśvibhṛgavo maruto 'nile(1) /
viśvedevāṃs tathā dakṣe rudrā śaidre 'tha maṇḍale //
290.d:
देवानाङ्गिरसश्चाश्विभृगवो मरुतो ऽनिले(1) /
विश्वेदेवांस् तथा दक्षे रुद्रा शैद्रे ऽथ मण्डले //
290.m:
the gods born of Aṅgiras, the Aśvins, the Bhṛgus, and the Maruts in the north-west;
the Viśvedevas in the south, and the Rudras in the circle of Indra.

290.s:
tato vṛttayā rekhayā tu devān vai vāhyato yajet /
sūtrakārānṛṣīn vāṇīṃ pūrvādau sarito girīn //
290.d:
ततो वृत्तया रेखया तु देवान् वै वाह्यतो यजेत् /
सूत्रकारानृषीन् वाणीं पूर्वादौ सरितो गिरीन् //
290.m:
Then with a circular line, one should worship the deities on the outside:
the authors of the sūtras, the ṛṣis, Sarasvatī, and beginning from the east, the rivers and mountains.

290.s:
mahābhūtāni koṇeṣu aiśānyādiṣu saṃyajet /
padmaṃ cakraṃ gadāṃ śaṅkhaṃ caturaśrantu maṇḍalaṃ //
290.d:
महाभूतानि कोणेषु ऐशान्यादिषु संयजेत् /
पद्मं चक्रं गदां शङ्खं चतुरश्रन्तु मण्डलं //
290.m:
One should worship the great elements in the corners, beginning with the north-east;
a lotus, a discus, a mace, and a conch; and a square maṇḍala,

290.s:
caturdhāraṃ tataḥ kumbhāḥ(2) agnyādau ca patākikāḥ(3) /
catvārastoraṇā dvāri nāgān airavatādikān //
290.d:
चतुर्धारं ततः कुम्भाः(2) अग्न्यादौ च पताकिकाः(3) /
चत्वारस्तोरणा द्वारि नागान् ऐरवतादिकान् //
290.m:
with four gates. Then pots and banners at the south-east and other [corners];
four archways at the door; and the elephants beginning with Airāvata

290.s:
pūrvādau cauṣadhībhiś ca devānāṃ bhājanaṃ pṛthak /
pṛthakśatāhutīścājyair gajānarcya pradakṣiṇaṃ //
290.d:
पूर्वादौ चौषधीभिश् च देवानां भाजनं पृथक् /
पृथक्शताहुतीश्चाज्यैर् गजानर्च्य प्रदक्षिणं //
290.m:
in the east and other directions with herbs. There should be a separate vessel for the deities,
and one hundred oblations of ghee for each. Having worshipped the elephants, [they should make] a circumambulation.

290.s:
nāgaṃ vahniṃ devatādīn vāhyair jagmuḥ svakaṃ gṛham /
dvijebhyo dikṣiṇāṃ dadyāt hayavaidyādikas tathā //
290.d:
नागं वह्निं देवतादीन् वाह्यैर् जग्मुः स्वकं गृहम् /
द्विजेभ्यो दिक्षिणां दद्यात् हयवैद्यादिकस् तथा //
290.m:
Having [worshipped] the elephant, fire, deities, and others with external [rites], they went to their own house.
One should give a sacrificial fee to twice-borns, as well as to horse-physicians and others.

290.s:
kariṇīntu samāruhya vadet karṇantu kālavit /
:n
1 maruto 'nala iti ja
2 catuḥkumbhā iti ña..
3 patākina iti ja..
:p 78
nāgarāje 'mṛte śāntiṃ kṛtvāmusmin(1) japenmanum //
290.d:
करिणीन्तु समारुह्य वदेत् कर्णन्तु कालवित् /
:न्
1 मरुतो ऽनल इति ज
2 चतुःकुम्भा इति ञ..
3 पताकिन इति ज..
:प् 78
नागराजे ऽमृते शान्तिं कृत्वामुस्मिन्(1) जपेन्मनुम् //
290.m:
Having mounted a cow-elephant, the knower of auspicious times should whisper into its ear:
[Footnote]
[Footnote 1: "maruto 'nala" in ms. ja]
[Footnote 2: "catuḥkumbhāḥ" in ms. ña]
[Footnote 3: "patākinaḥ" in ms. ja]
[Page 78]
“Having performed the pacification rite over the king of elephants, the immortal one, one should recite this mantra over it:

290.s:
śrīgajastvaṃ kṛto rājñā bhavānasya gajāgraṇīḥ /
prabhūrmālyāgrabhaktaistvāṃ pūjayiṣpati pārthivaḥ //
290.d:
श्रीगजस्त्वं कृतो राज्ञा भवानस्य गजाग्रणीः /
प्रभूर्माल्याग्रभक्तैस्त्वां पूजयिष्पति पार्थिवः //
290.m:
‘You have been made the royal elephant by the king; you are his foremost elephant.
The ruler, the king, will worship you with garlands and offerings of the finest food.

290.s:
lokastadājñayā pūjāṃ kariṣyati tadā tava /
pālanīyastvayā rājā yuddhe 'dhvani tathā gṛhe //
290.d:
लोकस्तदाज्ञया पूजां करिष्यति तदा तव /
पालनीयस्त्वया राजा युद्धे ऽध्वनि तथा गृहे //
290.m:
By his order, the people will then worship you.
You must protect the king in battle, on the road, and at home.

290.s:
tiryagbhāvaṃ samutsṛjya divyaṃ bhāvamanusmara /
devāsure purā yuddhe śrīgajastridaśaiḥ kṛtaḥ //
290.d:
तिर्यग्भावं समुत्सृज्य दिव्यं भावमनुस्मर /
देवासुरे पुरा युद्धे श्रीगजस्त्रिदशैः कृतः //
290.m:
Abandoning the nature of a beast, remember your divine nature.
Long ago in the war between the gods and asuras, a royal elephant was created by the thirty [gods].

290.s:
airāvaṇasutaḥ śrīmānariṣṭo nāma vāraṇaḥ /
śrīgajānāntu tat tejaḥ sarvamevopatiṣṭhate //
290.d:
ऐरावणसुतः श्रीमानरिष्टो नाम वारणः /
श्रीगजानान्तु तत् तेजः सर्वमेवोपतिष्ठते //
290.m:
The son of Airāvaṇa was the glorious elephant named Ariṣṭa.
All that splendor of royal elephants attends you.

290.s:
tattejastava nāgendra divyabhāvasamanvitaṃ /
upatiṣṭhatu bhadrante rakṣa rājānamāhave //
290.d:
तत्तेजस्तव नागेन्द्र दिव्यभावसमन्वितं /
उपतिष्ठतु भद्रन्ते रक्ष राजानमाहवे //
290.m: May that splendor, endowed with divine nature, attend you, O king of elephants! Hail to you! Protect the king in battle!’”

290.s:
ityevamabhiṣiktainamāroheta śubhe nṛpaḥ /
tasyānugamanaṃ kuryuḥ saśastranavasadgajāḥ //
290.d:
इत्येवमभिषिक्तैनमारोहेत शुभे नृपः /
तस्यानुगमनं कुर्युः सशस्त्रनवसद्गजाः //
290.m:
Having consecrated him in this manner, the king should mount him at an auspicious moment.
Nine good elephants, equipped with weapons, should follow him.

290.s:
śālāsvasau sthaṇḍile 'bje dikapālādīn yajedvahiḥ /
keśareṣu balaṃ nāgaṃ bhuvañcaica sarasvatīṃ //
290.d:
शालास्वसौ स्थण्डिले ऽब्जे दिकपालादीन् यजेद्वहिः /
केशरेषु बलं नागं भुवञ्चैच सरस्वतीं //
290.m:
In the stables, on an earthen altar, on a lotus, he should worship the regents of the directions on the outside,
and on the filaments Bala, Nāga, Bhū, and Sarasvatī.

290.s:
madhyeṣu ḍiṇḍimaṃ prārcya gandhamālyānulepanaiḥ /
hutvā deyastu kalaso rasapūrṇo dvijāya ca //
290.d:
मध्येषु डिण्डिमं प्रार्च्य गन्धमाल्यानुलेपनैः /
हुत्वा देयस्तु कलसो रसपूर्णो द्विजाय च //
290.m:
Having worshipped the drum in the center with scents, garlands, and ointments,
and having made fire offerings, a water-pot filled with fluids should be given to a twice-born.

290.s:
gajādhyakṣaṃ hastipañca gaṇitajñañca pūjayet /
gajādhyakṣāya tandadyāt ḍiṇḍimaṃ sopi vādayet /
śubhagambhīraśabdaiḥ syājjaghanastho 'bhivādayet //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe gajaśāntirnāma navatyadhikadviśatatamo
'dhyāyaḥ ||
:n
1 kṛdvānyasminniti kha.. , ja.. , ña.. ca
:p 79
:ś athaikanavatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
śāntyāyurvedaḥ
290.d:
गजाध्यक्षं हस्तिपञ्च गणितज्ञञ्च पूजयेत् /
गजाध्यक्षाय तन्दद्यात् डिण्डिमं सोपि वादयेत् /
शुभगम्भीरशब्दैः स्याज्जघनस्थो ऽभिवादयेत् //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे गजशान्तिर्नाम नवत्यधिकद्विशततमो
ऽध्यायः ||
:न्
1 कृद्वान्यस्मिन्निति ख.. , ज.. , ञ.. च
:प् 79
:श् अथैकनवत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
शान्त्यायुर्वेदः
290.m:
One should worship the superintendent of elephants, the elephant-trainer, and the astrologer.
One should give that drum to the superintendent of elephants, and he should beat it;
sitting on the elephant's haunches, he should sound it with auspicious, deep tones.
Thus in the Mahāpurāṇa composed by Agni, the two hundred and ninetieth chapter, entitled “Pacification Rite for Elephants.”
[Footnote]
[Footnote 1: "kṛtvānyasmin" in mss. kha, ja, and ña]
[Page 79]
Now the two hundred and ninety-first chapter.
The pacification medicine.

291.s:
dhanvantarir uvāca
goviprapālanaṃ karyaṃ rajñā gośāntimāvade /
gāvaḥ pavitrā māṅgalyā goṣu lokāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ //
291.d:
धन्वन्तरिर् उवाच
गोविप्रपालनं कर्यं रज्ञा गोशान्तिमावदे /
गावः पवित्रा माङ्गल्या गोषु लोकाः प्रतिष्ठिताः //
291.m:
Dhanvantari said:
The protection of cows and Brahmins must be performed by the king. I shall speak of the pacification rite for cows.
Cows are pure and auspicious; the worlds are established in cows.

291.s:
śakṛnmūtraṃ paraṃ tāsāmalakṣmīnāśanaṃ paraṃ /
gavāṃ kaṇḍūyanaṃ vāri śṛṅgasyāghaughamardanam //
291.d:
शकृन्मूत्रं परं तासामलक्ष्मीनाशनं परं /
गवां कण्डूयनं वारि शृङ्गस्याघौघमर्दनम् //
291.m:
Their dung and urine are supreme, supreme destroyers of misfortune.
Scratching cows and their horn-water crush a multitude of sins.

291.s:
gomūtraṃ gomayaṃ kṣīraṃ dadhi sarpaś ca rocanā /
śaḍaṅgaṃ paramaṃ pāne duḥsvapnādyādivāraṇaṃ //
291.d:
गोमूत्रं गोमयं क्षीरं दधि सर्पश् च रोचना /
शडङ्गं परमं पाने दुःस्वप्नाद्यादिवारणं //
291.m:
Cow-urine, cow-dung, milk, curd, clarified butter, and yellow pigment (rocanā):
this six-fold substance is supreme for drinking, warding off bad dreams and the like.

291.s:
rocanā viṣarakṣoghnī grāsadaḥ svargago gavāṃ /
yadgṛhe duḥkhitā gāvaḥ sa yāti narakannaraḥ //
291.d:
रोचना विषरक्षोघ्नी ग्रासदः स्वर्गगो गवां /
यद्गृहे दुःखिता गावः स याति नरकन्नरः //
291.m:
Rocanā destroys poison and demons. One who gives fodder to cows goes to heaven.
A man in whose house cows are distressed goes to hell.

291.s:
paragogrāsadaḥ svargī gohito brahmalokabhāk /
godānātkīrtanādrakṣāṃ kṛtvā coddharate kulam //
291.d:
परगोग्रासदः स्वर्गी गोहितो ब्रह्मलोकभाक् /
गोदानात्कीर्तनाद्रक्षां कृत्वा चोद्धरते कुलम् //
291.m:
One who gives mouthfuls of grass to another's cows attains heaven; one who is benevolent to cows attains the world of Brahmā.
By the gift of cows, by praising them, and by providing them protection, one delivers one's family.

291.s:
gavāṃ śvāsāt pavitrā bhūḥ sparśanātkilviṣakṣayaḥ /
gomūtraṃ gomayaṃ kṣīraṃ dadhi sarpiḥ kuśodakam //
291.d:
गवां श्वासात् पवित्रा भूः स्पर्शनात्किल्विषक्षयः /
गोमूत्रं गोमयं क्षीरं दधि सर्पिः कुशोदकम् //
291.m:
The earth is purified by the breath of cows; sins are destroyed by touching them.
Cow-urine, cow-dung, milk, curd, clarified butter, and kuśa-grass water—

291.s:
ekarātropavāsaś ca śvapākamapi śodhayet /
sarvāśubhavināśāya purācīratamīśvaraiḥ //
291.d:
एकरात्रोपवासश् च श्वपाकमपि शोधयेत् /
सर्वाशुभविनाशाय पुराचीरतमीश्वरैः //
291.m:
fasting for a single night [and drinking this] purifies even an outcaste.
In ancient times, this was practiced by the lords to destroy all inauspiciousness.

291.s:
pratyekañca tryahābhyamtaṃ mahāsāntapanaṃ smṛtaṃ /
sarvakāmapradañcaitat sarvāśubhavimardanam //
291.d:
प्रत्येकञ्च त्र्यहाभ्यम्तं महासान्तपनं स्मृतं /
सर्वकामप्रदञ्चैतत् सर्वाशुभविमर्दनम् //
291.m:
Consuming each of these for three days is remembered as the Mahāsāntapana penance;
it bestows all desires and crushes all misfortune.

291.s:
kṛcchrātikṛcchraṃ payasā divasānekaviṃśatiṃ /
nirmalāḥ sarvakāmāptyā syurgagāḥ spur natottamāḥ //
:p 80
291.d:
कृच्छ्रातिकृच्छ्रं पयसा दिवसानेकविंशतिं /
निर्मलाः सर्वकामाप्त्या स्युर्गगाः स्पुर् नतोत्तमाः //
:प् 80
291.m:
The Kṛcchrātikṛcchra penance consists of [subsisting solely on] milk for twenty-one days.
Spotless through attaining all desires, cows should be […]
[page 80]

291.s:
tryahamuṣṇaṃ pivenmūtraṃ tryahamuṣṇaṃ ghṛtaṃ pivet /
tryahamuṣṇaṃ payaḥ pītvā vāyubhakṣaḥ paraṃ tryaham //
291.d:
त्र्यहमुष्णं पिवेन्मूत्रं त्र्यहमुष्णं घृतं पिवेत् /
त्र्यहमुष्णं पयः पीत्वा वायुभक्षः परं त्र्यहम् //
291.m: For three days one should drink warm [cow] urine, for three days drink warm ghee; / having drunk warm milk for three days, one subsists on air for the next three days.

291.s:
taptakṛcchravrataṃ sarvapāpaghnaṃ brahmalokadaṃ /
śītaistu śītakṛcchraṃ syādbrahmoktaṃ brahmalokadaṃ //
291.d:
तप्तकृच्छ्रव्रतं सर्वपापघ्नं ब्रह्मलोकदं /
शीतैस्तु शीतकृच्छ्रं स्याद्ब्रह्मोक्तं ब्रह्मलोकदं //
291.m: The taptakṛcchra votive observance destroys all sins and bestows the world of Brahmā; / while with cold [ingredients] it is the śītakṛcchra, proclaimed by Brahmā, bestowing the world of Brahmā.

291.s:
gomūtreṇācaretsnānaṃ vṛttiṃ kuryācca gorasaiḥ /
gobhirvrajecca bhuktāsu bhuñjītātha ca govratī //
291.d:
गोमूत्रेणाचरेत्स्नानं वृत्तिं कुर्याच्च गोरसैः /
गोभिर्व्रजेच्च भुक्तासु भुञ्जीताथ च गोव्रती //
291.m: One should bathe with cow urine and make one's living with cow products; / one observing the cow observance should walk with the cows and eat after they have eaten.

291.s:
māsenaikena niṣpāpo golokī svargago bhavet /
vidyāñca gomatīṃ japtvā golokaṃ paramaṃ vrajet //
291.d:
मासेनैकेन निष्पापो गोलोकी स्वर्गगो भवेत् /
विद्याञ्च गोमतीं जप्त्वा गोलोकं परमं व्रजेत् //
291.m: In one month, freed from sin, he attains Goloka and goes to heaven; / and having recited the Gomatī-vidyā, he goes to supreme Goloka.

291.s:
gitair nṛtyair apsarobhirvimāne tatra modate /
gāvaḥ surabhayo nityaṃ gāvo guggulagandhikāḥ //
291.d:
गितैर् नृत्यैर् अप्सरोभिर्विमाने तत्र मोदते /
गावः सुरभयो नित्यं गावो गुग्गुलगन्धिकाः //
291.m: He rejoices there in an aerial chariot with singing, dancing, and apsarases. / Cows are ever fragrant, cows smell of guggulu;

291.s:
gāvaḥ pratiṣṭhā bhūtānāṃ gāvaḥ svastyayanaṃ paraṃ /
annameva paraṃ gāvo devānāṃ haviruttamam //
291.d:
गावः प्रतिष्ठा भूतानां गावः स्वस्त्ययनं परं /
अन्नमेव परं गावो देवानां हविरुत्तमम् //
291.m: cows are the support of beings, cows are the supreme blessing; / cows are the highest food, the supreme oblation of the gods.

291.s:
pāvanaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ kṣaranti ca vadanti ca /
haviṣā mantrapūtena tarpayantyamarāndivi //
291.d:
पावनं सर्वभूतानां क्षरन्ति च वदन्ति च /
हविषा मन्त्रपूतेन तर्पयन्त्यमरान्दिवि //
291.m: They yield and are spoken of as the purifier of all beings; / with oblation purified by mantra, they satisfy the immortals in heaven.

291.s:
ṛṣīṇāmagnihotreṣu gāvo homeṣu yojitāḥ /
sarveṣāmeva bhūtānāṃ gāvaḥ śaraṇamuttamaṃ //
291.d:
ऋषीणामग्निहोत्रेषु गावो होमेषु योजिताः /
सर्वेषामेव भूतानां गावः शरणमुत्तमं //
291.m: In the agnihotras and fire oblations of the sages, cows are employed; / cows are indeed the supreme refuge of all living beings.

291.s:
gāvaḥ pavitraṃ paramaṃ gāvo māṅgalyamuttamaṃ /
gāvaḥ svargasya sopānaṃ gāvo dhanyāḥ sanātanāḥ //
291.d:
गावः पवित्रं परमं गावो माङ्गल्यमुत्तमं /
गावः स्वर्गस्य सोपानं गावो धन्याः सनातनाः //
291.m: Cows are the supreme purifier, cows are the highest auspiciousness; / cows are the stairway to heaven, cows are blessed and eternal.

291.s:
namo gobhyaḥ śrīmatībhyaḥ saurabheyībhya eva ca /
namo brahmasutābhyaś ca pavitrābhyo namo namaḥ //
291.d:
नमो गोभ्यः श्रीमतीभ्यः सौरभेयीभ्य एव च /
नमो ब्रह्मसुताभ्यश् च पवित्राभ्यो नमो नमः //
291.m: Homage to the cows, the auspicious daughters of Surabhi; / homage to the daughters of Brahmā, and homage, homage to the pure ones!

291.s:
brāhmaṇāś caiva gāvaś ca kulamekaṃ dvidhā kṛtam /
ekatra mantrāstiṣṭhanti havirekatra tiṣṭhati //
:p 81
291.d:
ब्राह्मणाश् चैव गावश् च कुलमेकं द्विधा कृतम् /
एकत्र मन्त्रास्तिष्ठन्ति हविरेकत्र तिष्ठति //
:प् 81
291.m:
Brāhmaṇas and cows are one single family made into two: / in one place reside the mantras, and in the other resides the oblation.
[page 81]

291.s:
devabrāhmaṇagosādhusādhvībhiḥ sakalaṃ jagat /
dhāryate vai sadā tasmāt sarve pūjyatamā matāḥ //
291.d:
देवब्राह्मणगोसाधुसाध्वीभिः सकलं जगत् /
धार्यते वै सदा तस्मात् सर्वे पूज्यतमा मताः //
291.m: The entire universe is indeed constantly sustained by gods, brāhmaṇas, cows, virtuous men, and virtuous women; / therefore all are regarded as most worthy of worship.

291.s:
pivanti yatra tattīrthaṃ gaṅgādyā gāva eva hi /
gavāṃ māhātmyamuktaṃ hi cikitsāñca tathā śṛṇu //
291.d:
पिवन्ति यत्र तत्तीर्थं गङ्गाद्या गाव एव हि /
गवां माहात्म्यमुक्तं हि चिकित्साञ्च तथा शृणु //
291.m: The place where cows drink is indeed a sacred ford like the Gaṅgā and the rest. / The greatness of cows has thus been told; now listen to their medical treatment.

291.s:
śṛṅgāmayeṣu dhenūnāṃ tailaṃ dadyāt sasaindhavaṃ /
śṛṅgaverabalāmāṃsakalkasiddhaṃ samākṣikaṃ //
291.d:
शृङ्गामयेषु धेनूनां तैलं दद्यात् ससैन्धवं /
शृङ्गवेरबलामांसकल्कसिद्धं समाक्षिकं //
291.m: In diseases of the horns of cows, one should give oil with rock salt, / prepared with a paste of ginger, balā, and māṃsī, along with honey.

291.s:
karṇaśūleṣu sarveṣu mañjiṣṭhāhiṅgusaindhavaiḥ /
siddhaṃ tailaṃ pradātavyaṃ rasonenātha vā punaḥ //
291.d:
कर्णशूलेषु सर्वेषु मञ्जिष्ठाहिङ्गुसैन्धवैः /
सिद्धं तैलं प्रदातव्यं रसोनेनाथ वा पुनः //
291.m: In all earaches, oil prepared with mañjiṣṭhā, asafoetida, and rock salt / should be administered, or else with garlic.

291.s:
bilvamūlamapāmārgandhātakī casapāṭalā /
kuṭajandantamūleṣu lepāttacchūlanāśanaṃ //
291.d:
बिल्वमूलमपामार्गन्धातकी चसपाटला /
कुटजन्दन्तमूलेषु लेपात्तच्छूलनाशनं //
291.m: Bilva root, apāmārga, dhātakī, and pāṭalā, / [applied] as a paste on the roots of the teeth, destroys their toothache.

291.s:
dantaśūlaharair dravyair ghṛtaṃ rāma vipācitaṃ /
mukharogaharaṃ jñeyaṃ jihvārogeṣu saindhavaṃ //
291.d:
दन्तशूलहरैर् द्रव्यैर् घृतं राम विपाचितं /
मुखरोगहरं ज्ञेयं जिह्वारोगेषु सैन्धवं //
291.m: Ghee cooked with substances that alleviate toothache, O Rāma, / is known to alleviate diseases of the mouth; in tongue diseases, rock salt [is prescribed].

291.s:
śṛṅgaveraṃ haridre dve triphalā ca galagrahe /
hṛcchūle vastiśūle ca vātaroge kṣaye tathā //
291.d:
शृङ्गवेरं हरिद्रे द्वे त्रिफला च गलग्रहे /
हृच्छूले वस्तिशूले च वातरोगे क्षये तथा //
291.m: Ginger, the two turmerics, and triphalā [are prescribed] in throat obstruction; / in heart pain, bladder pain, wind disorders, and consumption,

291.s:
triphalā ghṛtamiśrā ca gavāṃ pāne praśasyate /
atīsāre haridre dve pāṭhāñcaiva pradāpayet //
291.d:
त्रिफला घृतमिश्रा च गवां पाने प्रशस्यते /
अतीसारे हरिद्रे द्वे पाठाञ्चैव प्रदापयेत् //
291.m: triphalā mixed with ghee is recommended as a drink for cows; / in diarrhoea, one should give the two turmerics and pāṭhā.

291.s:
sarveṣu koṣṭharogeṣu tathāśākhāgadeṣu ca /
śṛṅgaverañca bhārgīñca kāse śvāse pradāpayet //
291.d:
सर्वेषु कोष्ठरोगेषु तथाशाखागदेषु च /
शृङ्गवेरञ्च भार्गीञ्च कासे श्वासे प्रदापयेत् //
291.m: In all diseases of the belly and afflictions of the limbs, / and in cough and shortness of breath, one should give ginger and bhārgī.

291.s:
dātavyā bhagnasandhāne priyaṅgurlabaṇānvitā /
tailaṃ vātaharaṃ pitte madhuyaṣṭīvipācitaṃ //
291.d:
दातव्या भग्नसन्धाने प्रियङ्गुर्लबणान्विता /
तैलं वातहरं पित्ते मधुयष्टीविपाचितं //
291.m: Priyaṅgu combined with salt should be given for uniting fractures; / oil cooked with liquorice alleviates wind, and [ghee cooked with it alleviates] pitta.

291.s:
kaphe vyoṣañca samadhu sapuṣṭakarajo 'sraje /
tailājyaṃ haritālañca bhagnakṣatiśṛtandadet //
291.d:
कफे व्योषञ्च समधु सपुष्टकरजो ऽस्रजे /
तैलाज्यं हरितालञ्च भग्नक्षतिशृतन्ददेत् //
291.m: In [diseases of] phlegm, [one should administer] the three pungents with honey; in [diseases of] the blood, [the same] with karanja seed powder. / One should give oil, ghee, and orpiment, boiled for fractures and wounds.

291.s:
māsāstilāḥ sagodhūmāḥ paśukṣīraṃ ghṛtaṃ tathā /
:p 82
eṣāṃ piṇḍī salavaṇā vatsānāṃ puṣṭidātviyaṃ //
291.d:
मासास्तिलाः सगोधूमाः पशुक्षीरं घृतं तथा /
:प् 82
एषां पिण्डी सलवणा वत्सानां पुष्टिदात्वियं //
291.m:
Urad, sesame seeds, with wheat, milk of animals, and ghee—
[p. 82]
A ball of these with salt brings nourishment to calves.

291.s:
balapradā viṣāṇāṃ syadgrahanāśāya dhūpakaḥ /
devadāru vacā māṃsī guggulurhiṅgusarṣapāḥ //
291.d:
बलप्रदा विषाणां स्यद्ग्रहनाशाय धूपकः /
देवदारु वचा मांसी गुग्गुलुर्हिङ्गुसर्षपाः //
291.m: It gives strength to the horns. An incense for destroying evil spirits [is]: / deodar, sweet flag, spikenard, guggulu, asafoetida, and mustard seeds.

291.s:
grahādigadanāśāya eṣa dhūpo gavāṃ hitaḥ /
ghaṇṭhā caiva gavāṃ kāryā dhūpenānena bhūpitā //
291.d:
ग्रहादिगदनाशाय एष धूपो गवां हितः /
घण्ठा चैव गवां कार्या धूपेनानेन भूपिता //
291.m: This incense is beneficial for cows, for destroying evil spirits and other diseases. / And a bell for cows should be made fumigated with this incense.

291.s:
aśvagandhātilaiḥ śuklaṃ tena gauḥ kṣīriṇī bhavet /
rasāyanañca pinyākaṃ matto yo dhāryate gṛhe //
291.d:
अश्वगन्धातिलैः शुक्लं तेन गौः क्षीरिणी भवेत् /
रसायनञ्च पिन्याकं मत्तो यो धार्यते गृहे //
291.m: With aśvagandhā and sesame seeds, [the discharge becomes] white, [and] thereby the cow becomes rich in milk. / And oil-cake is an elixir; it is kept in the house by one who is wise.

291.s:
bhavāṃ purīṣe pañcabhyāṃ nityaṃ śāntyai śriyaṃ yajet /
vāsudevañca gandhādyair aparā śāntirucyate //
291.d:
भवां पुरीषे पञ्चभ्यां नित्यं शान्त्यै श्रियं यजेत् /
वासुदेवञ्च गन्धाद्यैर् अपरा शान्तिरुच्यते //
291.m: One should daily worship Śrī in cow dung on the fifth [lunar day] for appeasement, / and Vāsudeva with perfumes and the like. Another appeasement rite is proclaimed:

291.s:
aśvayukśuklapakṣasya pañcadaśyāṃ yajeddhariṃ /
harirudramajaṃ sūryaṃ śriyamagniṃ ghṛtena ca //
291.d:
अश्वयुक्शुक्लपक्षस्य पञ्चदश्यां यजेद्धरिं /
हरिरुद्रमजं सूर्यं श्रियमग्निं घृतेन च //
291.m: On the fifteenth [tithi] of the bright fortnight of Āśvina, one should worship Hari, / Hari, Rudra, the Unborn [Brahmā], Sūrya, Śrī, and Agni with ghee.

291.s:
dadhi samprāśya gāḥ pūjya kāryaṃ vāhnipradakṣiṇaṃ /
vṛṣāṇāṃ yojeyed yuddhaṃ gītavādyaravair vahiḥ //
291.d:
दधि सम्प्राश्य गाः पूज्य कार्यं वाह्निप्रदक्षिणं /
वृषाणां योजेयेद् युद्धं गीतवाद्यरवैर् वहिः //
291.m: Having consumed curd and worshipped the cows, circumambulation of the fire should be performed. / One should stage a fight of bulls outside, accompanied by the sounds of song and instrumental music.

291.s:
gavāntu lavaṇandeyaṃ brāhmaṇānāñca dakṣiṇā /
naimittike mākarādau yajedviṣṇuṃ saha śriyā //
291.d:
गवान्तु लवणन्देयं ब्राह्मणानाञ्च दक्षिणा /
नैमित्तिके माकरादौ यजेद्विष्णुं सह श्रिया //
291.m: Salt should be given to cows, and a sacrificial fee to brāhmaṇas. / In occasional rites at the entrance of the sun into Capricorn and the like, one should worship Viṣṇu along with Śrī.

291.s:
sthaṇḍilebje madhyagate dikṣu keśaragān surān /
subhadrājo raviḥ pūjyo bahurūpo balirvahiḥ //
291.d:
स्थण्डिलेब्जे मध्यगते दिक्षु केशरगान् सुरान् /
सुभद्राजो रविः पूज्यो बहुरूपो बलिर्वहिः //
291.m: On a bare ground on a lotus placed in the center, and the gods situated on the filaments in the cardinal directions, / the Sun born of Subhadrā is to be worshipped, [and] a multiform oblation [made] outside.

291.s:
khaṃ viśvarūpā siddhiś ca ṛddhiḥ śāntiś ca rohiṇī /
digdhenavo hi pūrvādyāḥ kṛśaraiś candra īśvaraḥ //
291.d:
खं विश्वरूपा सिद्धिश् च ऋद्धिः शान्तिश् च रोहिणी /
दिग्धेनवो हि पूर्वाद्याः कृशरैश् चन्द्र ईश्वरः //
291.m: Kha, Viśvarūpā, Siddhi, Ṛddhi, Śānti, and Rohiṇī / are indeed the cows of the directions, beginning with the east. The Moon, the Lord [Śiva],

291.s:
dikpālāḥ padmapatreṣu kumbheṣvagnau ca homayet /
kṣīravṛkṣasya samidhaḥ sarṣapākṣatataṇḍulān //
291.d:
दिक्पालाः पद्मपत्रेषु कुम्भेष्वग्नौ च होमयेत् /
क्षीरवृक्षस्य समिधः सर्षपाक्षततण्डुलान् //
291.m: and the guardians of the directions [are to be worshipped] with rice boiled with pulses on lotus leaves, jars, and in fire. One should offer into the fire / kindling sticks of milky trees, mustard seeds, and unblemished whole grains of rice.

291.s:
śataṃ śataṃ suvarṇañca kāṃsyādikaṃ dvije dadet /
gāvaḥ pūjyā vimoktavyāḥ śāntyai kṣīrādisaṃyutāḥ //
:p 83
291.d:
शतं शतं सुवर्णञ्च कांस्यादिकं द्विजे ददेत् /
गावः पूज्या विमोक्तव्याः शान्त्यै क्षीरादिसंयुताः //
:प् 83
291.m:
One should give to a twice-born a hundred [pieces of] gold and bronze and other metals. / Cows are to be worshipped and set free, provided with milk and the like, for appeasement.
[p. 83]

291.s:
agnir uvāca
śālihotraḥ suśrutāya hayāyurvedamuktavān /
pālakāpyo 'ṅgarājāya gajāyurvedamabravīt //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe śāntyāyurvedo
nāmaikanavatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:ś atha dvinavatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
mantraparibhāṣā
291.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
शालिहोत्रः सुश्रुताय हयायुर्वेदमुक्तवान् /
पालकाप्यो ऽङ्गराजाय गजायुर्वेदमब्रवीत् //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे शान्त्यायुर्वेदो
नामैकनवत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
:श् अथ द्विनवत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
मन्त्रपरिभाषा
291.m:
Agni said: / Śālihotra taught the veterinary science of horses to Suśruta; / Pālakāpya spoke the veterinary science of elephants to the king of Aṅga.
Thus ends the two hundred and ninety-first chapter, named 'The Veterinary Science of Appeasement', in the Mahāpurāṇa taught by Agni.
Now begins the two hundred and ninety-second chapter.
Terminology of Mantras

292.s:
agnir uvāca
mantravidyāhariṃ vakṣye bhuktimuktipradaṃ śṛṇu /
viṃśatyarṇādhikā mantrā mālāmantrāḥ smṛtā dvija //
292.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
मन्त्रविद्याहरिं वक्ष्ये भुक्तिमुक्तिप्रदं शृणु /
विंशत्यर्णाधिका मन्त्रा मालामन्त्राः स्मृता द्विज //
292.m: Agni said: / I shall declare Hari in the form of mantra-lore, granting worldly enjoyment and liberation; listen: / Mantras containing more than twenty syllables are remembered as mālā-mantras, O twice-born.

292.s:
daśākṣarādhikā mantrāstadarvāgvījasaṃjñitāḥ /
vardhakye siddhidā hy ete mālāmantrāstu yauvena //
292.d:
दशाक्षराधिका मन्त्रास्तदर्वाग्वीजसंज्ञिताः /
वर्धक्ये सिद्धिदा ह्य् एते मालामन्त्रास्तु यौवेन //
292.m: Mantras of more than ten syllables [are also designated thus]; those below that are termed seed-syllables. / These indeed grant accomplishment in old age, but mālā-mantras in youth.

292.s:
pañcākṣarādhikā mantrāḥ siddhidāḥ sarvadāpare /
strīpuṃnapuṃsakatvena tridhāḥ syurmantrajātayaḥ //
292.d:
पञ्चाक्षराधिका मन्त्राः सिद्धिदाः सर्वदापरे /
स्त्रीपुंनपुंसकत्वेन त्रिधाः स्युर्मन्त्रजातयः //
292.m: The other mantras of more than five syllables grant accomplishment at all times. / The classes of mantras are threefold by way of feminine, masculine, and neuter.

292.s:
strīmantrā vahnijāyantā namontāś ca napuṃsakāḥ /
śeṣāḥ pumāṃsaste śastā vakṣyoccāṭaviṣeṣu ca(1) //
292.d:
स्त्रीमन्त्रा वह्निजायन्ता नमोन्ताश् च नपुंसकाः /
शेषाः पुमांसस्ते शस्ता वक्ष्योच्चाटविषेषु च(1) //
292.m: Feminine mantras end with the wife of Agni [Svāhā], and neuter ones end with 'namaḥ'. / The remaining are masculine; they are recommended in eradication of rivals and poisons.

292.s:
kṣudrakriyāmayadhvaṃse striyo 'nyatra(2) napuṃsakāḥ /
mantrāvāgneyasaumyākhyau tārādyantārdvayorjapet //
292.d:
क्षुद्रक्रियामयध्वंसे स्त्रियो ऽन्यत्र(2) नपुंसकाः /
मन्त्रावाग्नेयसौम्याख्यौ ताराद्यन्तार्द्वयोर्जपेत् //
292.m: Feminine [mantras] are [used] in the destruction of petty magical acts and diseases; elsewhere neuter ones [are used]. / Mantras are designated fiery and gentle; one should recite both preceded by the praṇava [and ending with it].

292.s:
tārāntyāgniviyatprāyo mantra āgneya iṣyate /
śiṣṭaḥ saumyaḥ praśastau tau karmaṇoḥ krūrasaumyayoḥ //
:n
1 bandhoccāṭavaśeṣu ceti ja..
2 striyo nātreti kha..
:p 84
292.d:
तारान्त्याग्निवियत्प्रायो मन्त्र आग्नेय इष्यते /
शिष्टः सौम्यः प्रशस्तौ तौ कर्मणोः क्रूरसौम्ययोः //
:न्
1 बन्धोच्चाटवशेषु चेति ज..
2 स्त्रियो नात्रेति ख..
:प् 84
292.m:
A mantra consisting largely of the stars, the ending, fire, and ether is regarded as fiery. / The rest is gentle; those two are recommended respectively in cruel and gentle rites.
[Footnote]
1. 'bandhoccāṭavaśeṣu ca' according to manuscript ja.
2. 'striyo nātra' according to manuscript kha.
[p. 84]

292.s:
āgneyamantraḥ saumyaḥ syātprāyaśo 'nte namo 'nvitaḥ /
saumyamantras tathāgneyaḥ phaṭkāreṇāntato yutaḥ //
292.d:
आग्नेयमन्त्रः सौम्यः स्यात्प्रायशो ऽन्ते नमो ऽन्वितः /
सौम्यमन्त्रस् तथाग्नेयः फट्कारेणान्ततो युतः //
292.m: A fiery mantra becomes gentle, generally, when endowed with 'namaḥ' at the end. / Likewise, a gentle mantra becomes fiery when joined with the syllable 'phaṭ' at the end.

292.s:
suptaḥ prabuddhamātro vā mantraḥ siddhiṃ na yacchati /
śvāpakālo mahāvāho jāgaro dakṣiṇāvahaḥ //
292.d:
सुप्तः प्रबुद्धमात्रो वा मन्त्रः सिद्धिं न यच्छति /
श्वापकालो महावाहो जागरो दक्षिणावहः //
292.m: A sleeping mantra or one that has just awakened does not grant accomplishment. / The time of sleep is the left nostril, O mighty-armed one; the awake state is the flow through the right [nostril].

292.s:
āgneyasya manoḥ saumyamantrasyaitadviparyayāt /
prabodhakālaṃ jānīyādubhayorubhayorahaḥ //
292.d:
आग्नेयस्य मनोः सौम्यमन्त्रस्यैतद्विपर्ययात् /
प्रबोधकालं जानीयादुभयोरुभयोरहः //
292.m: Of a fiery mantra [the waking state is in the right nostril], and of a gentle mantra it is the reverse of this. / One should know the time of awakening of each of the two, day by day.

292.s:
duṣṭarkṣarāśividveṣivarṇādīn varjayenmanūn /
rājyalābhopakārāya prārabhyāriḥ svaraḥ kurūn //
292.d:
दुष्टर्क्षराशिविद्वेषिवर्णादीन् वर्जयेन्मनून् /
राज्यलाभोपकाराय प्रारभ्यारिः स्वरः कुरून् //
292.m:
One should avoid mantras having inauspicious asterisms, zodiacal signs, inimical syllables, and the like.
For the sake of gaining a kingdom, an enemy [letter] beginning with a vowel [destroys] the Kurus.

292.s:
gopālakakuṭīṃ prāyāt pūrṇāmityuditā lipiḥ /
nakṣetrekṣakramādyojyā svarāntyau revatīyujau //
292.d:
गोपालककुटीं प्रायात् पूर्णामित्युदिता लिपिः /
नक्षेत्रेक्षक्रमाद्योज्या स्वरान्त्यौ रेवतीयुजौ //
292.m:
The script is declared [by the mnemonic]: 'He went to the cowherd's hut, which was full.'
One should apply it in the order of asterisms and glances; the last two vowels are joined to Revatī.

292.s:
velā guruḥ svarāḥ śoṇaḥ karmaṇaivetibheditāḥ /
lipyarṇā vaśiṣu jñeyā ṣaṣṭheśādīṃś ca yojayet //
292.d:
वेला गुरुः स्वराः शोणः कर्मणैवेतिभेदिताः /
लिप्यर्णा वशिषु ज्ञेया षष्ठेशादींश् च योजयेत् //
292.m:
The times, the heavy syllables, the vowels, and the red [letters] are distinguished precisely by ritual action;
the letters of the alphabet are to be known among subjugating [factors], and one should apply the lord of the sixth [house] and others.

292.s:
lipau catuṣpathasthāyāmākhyavarṇapadāntarāḥ /
siddhāḥ sādhyā dvitīyasthāḥ susiddhā vairiṇaḥ pare //
292.d:
लिपौ चतुष्पथस्थायामाख्यवर्णपदान्तराः /
सिद्धाः साध्या द्वितीयस्थाः सुसिद्धा वैरिणः परे //
292.m:
When the alphabet is placed in a crossroad [diagram], the letters positioned within one's own name
are 'accomplished' (siddha); those in the second are 'to be accomplished' (sādhya); those [in the third] are 'well-accomplished' (susiddha); the others are enemies (vairin).

292.s:
siddhādīn kalpayedevaṃ siddhātyantaguṇair api(1) /
siddhe siddho japāt sādhyo japapūjāhutādinā(2) //
292.d:
सिद्धादीन् कल्पयेदेवं सिद्धात्यन्तगुणैर् अपि(1) /
सिद्धे सिद्धो जपात् साध्यो जपपूजाहुतादिना(2) //
292.m:
Thus one should determine the accomplished and the rest, even by the extreme qualities of the accomplished:
for an accomplished practitioner, [the mantra] is accomplished through recitation; the 'to-be-accomplished' through recitation, worship, fire oblation, and the like.

292.s:
susiddho dhyānamātreṇa sādhakaṃ nāśayedariḥ /
duṣṭārṇapracuro yaḥ syānmantraḥ sarvavininditaḥ //
292.d:
सुसिद्धो ध्यानमात्रेण साधकं नाशयेदरिः /
दुष्टार्णप्रचुरो यः स्यान्मन्त्रः सर्वविनिन्दितः //
292.m:
The 'well-accomplished' [yields success] by mere meditation; the 'enemy' would destroy the practitioner.
A mantra that abounds in inauspicious syllables is condemned in every respect.

292.s:
praviśya vidhivaddīkṣāmabhiṣekāvasānikām /
śrutvā tantraṃ guror labdhaṃ sādhayedīpsitaṃ manum //
292.d:
प्रविश्य विधिवद्दीक्षामभिषेकावसानिकाम् /
श्रुत्वा तन्त्रं गुरोर् लब्धं साधयेदीप्सितं मनुम् //
292.m:
Having undergone initiation according to rule, concluding with consecration by aspersion,
and having heard the Tantra obtained from the guru, one should accomplish the desired mantra.

292.s:
dhīro dakṣaḥ śucirbhakto japadhyānāditatparaḥ /
:n
1 siddhadyantadalair apīti ja..
2 japapūrṇāhutādineti kha..
:p 85
siddhastapasvī kuśalastantrajñaḥ satyabhāṣaṇaḥ //
292.d:
धीरो दक्षः शुचिर्भक्तो जपध्यानादितत्परः /
:न्
1 सिद्धद्यन्तदलैर् अपीति ज..
2 जपपूर्णाहुतादिनेति ख..
:प् 85
सिद्धस्तपस्वी कुशलस्तन्त्रज्ञः सत्यभाषणः //
292.m:
A steadfast, competent, pure, devoted person intent on recitation, meditation, and the like,
[Footnote]
[Variant reading: 1 ...]
[Variant reading: 2 ...]
[Page 85]
accomplished, practicing ascetic austerity, skilled, knowing the Tantras, speaking the truth,

292.s:
nigrahānugrahe śakto gururityabhidhīyate /
śānto dāntaḥ paṭuścīrṇabrahmacaryo haviṣyabhuk //
292.d:
निग्रहानुग्रहे शक्तो गुरुरित्यभिधीयते /
शान्तो दान्तः पटुश्चीर्णब्रह्मचर्यो हविष्यभुक् //
292.m:
capable of punishment and favor—such a one is designated a guru.
Calm, restrained, clever, having observed celibacy, eating sacrificial food,

292.s:
kurvannācāryaśuśrūṣāṃ siddhotsāhī sa śiṣyakaḥ /
sa tūpadeśyaḥ putraś ca vinayī vasudas tathā //
292.d:
कुर्वन्नाचार्यशुश्रूषां सिद्धोत्साही स शिष्यकः /
स तूपदेश्यः पुत्रश् च विनयी वसुदस् तथा //
292.m:
performing service to the teacher, enthusiastic for success—he is a disciple.
He should be instructed, as should a son, one who is humble, and one who offers wealth.

292.s:
mantrandadyāt susiddhau tu sahasraṃ deśikaṃ japet /
yadṛcchayā śrutaṃ mantraṃ chalenātha balena vā //
292.d:
मन्त्रन्दद्यात् सुसिद्धौ तु सहस्रं देशिकं जपेत् /
यदृच्छया श्रुतं मन्त्रं छलेनाथ बलेन वा //
292.m:
When [a mantra] is well-accomplished, he may impart it; but the spiritual teacher should recite it a thousand [times].
A mantra heard by chance, or acquired by trickery or by force,

292.s:
patre sthitañca gāthāñca janayedyadyanarthakam /
mantraṃ yaḥ sādhayedekaṃ japahomārcanādibhiḥ //
292.d:
पत्रे स्थितञ्च गाथाञ्च जनयेद्यद्यनर्थकम् /
मन्त्रं यः साधयेदेकं जपहोमार्चनादिभिः //
292.m:
or written on a leaf, or a metrical song, would produce misfortune.
If one accomplishes a single mantra by recitation, fire oblations, worship, and the like,

292.s:
kriyābhirbhūribhistasya sidhyante svalpasādhanāt /
samyaksiddhaikamantrasya nāsādhyamiha kiñcana //
292.d:
क्रियाभिर्भूरिभिस्तस्य सिध्यन्ते स्वल्पसाधनात् /
सम्यक्सिद्धैकमन्त्रस्य नासाध्यमिह किञ्चन //
292.m:
through numerous ritual acts, [other mantras] will succeed for him with little effort.
For one who has completely accomplished a single mantra, nothing here is unattainable.

292.s:
bahumantravataḥ puṃsaḥ kā kathā śiva eva saḥ /
daśalakṣajapādeka varṇo mantraḥ prasidhyati //
292.d:
बहुमन्त्रवतः पुंसः का कथा शिव एव सः /
दशलक्षजपादेक वर्णो मन्त्रः प्रसिध्यति //
292.m:
What is there to say of a man possessing many mantras? He is Śiva himself.
By a million recitations, a single-syllable mantra is accomplished.

292.s:
varṇavṛddhyā japahrāsastenānyeṣāṃ samūhayet /
vījāddvitriguṇānmantrānmālāmantre japakriyā //
292.d:
वर्णवृद्ध्या जपह्रासस्तेनान्येषां समूहयेत् /
वीजाद्द्वित्रिगुणान्मन्त्रान्मालामन्त्रे जपक्रिया //
292.m:
With an increase in syllables comes a decrease in recitation; by this [rule] one should calculate for others.
From the seed-syllable to mantras doubled or tripled, the act of recitation is [calculated] for a garland-mantra.

292.s:
saṅkhyānuktau śataṃ sāṣṭaṃ sahasraṃ vā japādiṣu /
japāddaśāṃśaṃ sarvatra sābhiśekaṃ hutaṃ viduḥ //
292.d:
सङ्ख्यानुक्तौ शतं साष्टं सहस्रं वा जपादिषु /
जपाद्दशांशं सर्वत्र साभिशेकं हुतं विदुः //
292.m:
When the number is not stated, [it is] one hundred and eight or a thousand in recitation and the like.
Everywhere, an oblation accompanied by consecration by aspersion is known to be one-tenth of the recitation.

292.s:
dravyānuktau ghṛtaṃ home japo 'śaktasya sarvataḥ /
mūlamantrāddaśāṃśaḥ syādaṅgādīnāṃ japādikam //
292.d:
द्रव्यानुक्तौ घृतं होमे जपो ऽशक्तस्य सर्वतः /
मूलमन्त्राद्दशांशः स्यादङ्गादीनां जपादिकम् //
292.m:
When the substance is not stated, ghee is [offered] in the fire oblation; recitation is [prescribed] everywhere for one who is unable.
The recitation and other rites for the limb[-mantras] and the rest should be one-tenth of the root-mantra.

292.s:
japātsaśaktimantrasya kāmadā mantradevatāḥ /
sādhakasya bhavet tṛptā dhyānahomārcanādinā //
292.d:
जपात्सशक्तिमन्त्रस्य कामदा मन्त्रदेवताः /
साधकस्य भवेत् तृप्ता ध्यानहोमार्चनादिना //
292.m:
Through recitation of an empowered mantra, the deities of the mantra grant desires;
they become satisfied with the practitioner through meditation, fire oblation, worship, and the like.

292.s:
uccairjapādviśiṣṭaḥ syādupāṃśurdaśabhirguṇaiḥ /
jihvājape śataguṇaḥ sahasro mānasaḥ smṛtaḥ //
:p 86
292.d:
उच्चैर्जपाद्विशिष्टः स्यादुपांशुर्दशभिर्गुणैः /
जिह्वाजपे शतगुणः सहस्रो मानसः स्मृतः //
:प् 86

292.s:
prāṅmukho 'vāṅmukho vāpi mantrakarma samārabhet /
praṇavādyāḥ sarvamantrā vāgyato vihitāśanaḥ //
292.d:
प्राङ्मुखो ऽवाङ्मुखो वापि मन्त्रकर्म समारभेत् /
प्रणवाद्याः सर्वमन्त्रा वाग्यतो विहिताशनः //
292.m:
Facing east or facing north, one should undertake the ritual of the mantra.
All mantras begin with Praṇava (Oṃ), [recited] with restrained speech, eating prescribed food.

292.s:
āsīnastu japenmantrāndevatācāryatulyadṛk /
kuṭīviviktā deśāḥ syurdevālayanadīhradāḥ //
292.d:
आसीनस्तु जपेन्मन्त्रान्देवताचार्यतुल्यदृक् /
कुटीविविक्ता देशाः स्युर्देवालयनदीह्रदाः //
292.m:
Seated, one should recite the mantras, viewing deity and teacher as equal.
The places should be an isolated hut, a temple, a river, or a lake.

292.s:
siddhau yavāgūpūpair vā payo bhakṣyaṃ haviṣyakam /
mantrasya devatā tāvat(1) tithivāreṣu vai japet //
292.d:
सिद्धौ यवागूपूपैर् वा पयो भक्ष्यं हविष्यकम् /
मन्त्रस्य देवता तावत्(1) तिथिवारेषु वै जपेत् //
292.m:
For accomplishment, his food should be sacrificial food—gruel, cakes, or milk.
One should recite the mantra's deity on the [prescribed] lunar days and weekdays,

292.s:
kṛṣṇāṣṭamīcaturdaśyorgrahaṇādau ca sādhakaḥ /
dasro yamo 'nalo dhātā śaśī rudro gururditiḥ //
292.d:
कृष्णाष्टमीचतुर्दश्योर्ग्रहणादौ च साधकः /
दस्रो यमो ऽनलो धाता शशी रुद्रो गुरुर्दितिः //
292.m:
on the eighth and fourteenth lunar days of the dark fortnight, and during an eclipse and the like, as a practitioner.
Dasra (Aśvinī), Yama (Bharaṇī), Anala (Kṛttikā), Dhātṛ (Rohiṇī), Śaśin (Mṛgaśīrṣa), Rudra (Ārdrā), Guru (Punarvasu), Diti (Puṣya),

292.s:
sarpāḥ pitaro 'tha bhago 'ryamā śotetaradyutiḥ /
tvaṣṭā maruta indrāgnī mitrendrau nirṛtirjalam //
292.d:
सर्पाः पितरो ऽथ भगो ऽर्यमा शोतेतरद्युतिः /
त्वष्टा मरुत इन्द्राग्नी मित्रेन्द्रौ निरृतिर्जलम् //
292.m:
the Serpents (Āśleṣā), the Ancestors (Maghā), then Bhaga (Pūrvaphālgunī), Aryaman (Uttaraphālgunī), the non-white light (Savitṛ, Hastā),
Tvaṣṭṛ (Citrā), the Maruts (Svātī), Indrāgnī (Viśākhā), Mitra and Indra (Anurādhā and Jyeṣṭhā), Nirṛti (Mūla), the Water (Pūrvāṣāḍhā),

292.s:
viśvedevā hṛṣīkeśo vāyavaḥ salilādhipaḥ /
ajaikapādahirvradhnaḥ pūṣāśvinyādidevatāḥ //
292.d:
विश्वेदेवा हृषीकेशो वायवः सलिलाधिपः /
अजैकपादहिर्व्रध्नः पूषाश्विन्यादिदेवताः //
292.m:
the Viśvedevas (Uttarāṣāḍhā), Hṛṣīkeśa (Śravaṇa), the Vāyus (Śraviṣṭhā/Dhaniṣṭhā), the Lord of Waters (Śatabhiṣaj),
Ajaikapād (Pūrvabhādrapadā), Ahirbudhnya (Uttarabhādrapadā), Pūṣan (Revatī)—these are the deities beginning with Aśvinī.

292.s:
agnidasrāvumā nighno nāgaś candro divākaraḥ /
mātṛdurgā diśāmīśaḥ kṛṣṇo vaivasvataḥ śivaḥ //
292.d:
अग्निदस्रावुमा निघ्नो नागश् चन्द्रो दिवाकरः /
मातृदुर्गा दिशामीशः कृष्णो वैवस्वतः शिवः //
292.m:
Agni, the two Dasras, Umā, Vighnahartṛ (Gaṇeśa), the Nāga, the Moon, the Sun,
the Mothers, Durgā, the Lord of Directions (Yama), Kṛṣṇa, Vaivasvata, Śiva,

292.s:
pañcadaśyāḥ śaśāṅkastu pitarastithidevatāḥ /
haro durgā gururviṣṇurbrahmā lakṣmīrdhaneśvaraḥ //
292.d:
पञ्चदश्याः शशाङ्कस्तु पितरस्तिथिदेवताः /
हरो दुर्गा गुरुर्विष्णुर्ब्रह्मा लक्ष्मीर्धनेश्वरः //
292.m:
and for the fifteenth [lunar day], the Moon (Pūrṇimā) or the Ancestors (Amāvāsyā)—these are the deities of the lunar days.
Hara, Durgā, Guru, Viṣṇu, Brahmā, Lakṣmī, and the Lord of Wealth (Kubera)—

292.s:
ete suryādivāreśā lipinyāso 'tha kathyate /
keśānteṣu ca vṛtteṣu cakṣuṣoḥ śravaṇadvaye //
292.d:
एते सुर्यादिवारेशा लिपिन्यासो ऽथ कथ्यते /
केशान्तेषु च वृत्तेषु चक्षुषोः श्रवणद्वये //
292.m:
these are the lords of the days beginning with Sunday. Now the ritual deposition of the alphabet is described:
at the edge of the hair, on the rounded regions [of the face], on the two eyes, on the two ears,

292.s:
nāsāgaṇḍauṣṭhadantānāṃ dve dve mūrdhasyayoḥ kramāt /
varṇān pañcasuvargānāṃ(2) bāhucaraṇasandhiṣu //
292.d:
नासागण्डौष्ठदन्तानां द्वे द्वे मूर्धस्ययोः क्रमात् /
वर्णान् पञ्चसुवर्गानां(2) बाहुचरणसन्धिषु //
292.m:
two each on the nose, cheeks, lips, and teeth, in the head and mouth in order;
the letters of the five groups [of consonants] on the joints of the arms and feet,

292.s:
pārśvayoḥ pṛṣṭhato nābhau hṛdaye ca kramānnyaset /
:n
1 tareti kha..
2 pañcasvaravargāṇāmiti kha..
:p 87
yādīṃś ca hṛdaye nyasyedeṣāṃ syuḥ saptadhātavaḥ //
292.d:
पार्श्वयोः पृष्ठतो नाभौ हृदये च क्रमान्न्यसेत् /
:न्
1 तरेति ख..
2 पञ्चस्वरवर्गाणामिति ख..
:प् 87
यादींश् च हृदये न्यस्येदेषां स्युः सप्तधातवः //
292.m:
on the two flanks, behind on the back, at the navel, and at the heart, one should deposit in order.
[Footnote]
[Variant reading: 1 ...]
[Variant reading: 2 ...]
[Page 87]
One should deposit the letters beginning with ya at the heart; these correspond to the seven bodily tissues:

292.s:
tvagasṛṅmāṃsakasnāyumedomajjāśukrāṇi dhātavaḥ /
vasāḥ payo vāsako likhyante caiva lipīśvarāḥ //
292.d:
त्वगसृङ्मांसकस्नायुमेदोमज्जाशुक्राणि धातवः /
वसाः पयो वासको लिख्यन्ते चैव लिपीश्वराः //
292.m:
skin, blood, flesh, sinew, fat, marrow, and semen are the tissues;
lymph, chyle, and muscle. And the lords of the alphabet are written:

292.s:
śrīkaṇṭho 'nantasūkṣmau ca trimūrtiramareśvaraḥ /
agnīśo bhāvabhūtiś ca tithīśaḥ sthānuko haraḥ //
292.d:
श्रीकण्ठो ऽनन्तसूक्ष्मौ च त्रिमूर्तिरमरेश्वरः /
अग्नीशो भावभूतिश् च तिथीशः स्थानुको हरः //
292.m:
Śrīkaṇṭha, Ananta and Sūkṣma, Trimūrti, Amareśvara,
Agnīśa, Bhāvabhūti, Tithīśa, Sthāṇuka, Hara,

292.s:
daṇḍīśo bhautikaḥ sadyojātaścānugraheśvaraḥ /
akrūraś ca mahāsenaḥ śaraṇyā devatā amūḥ //
292.d:
दण्डीशो भौतिकः सद्योजातश्चानुग्रहेश्वरः /
अक्रूरश् च महासेनः शरण्या देवता अमूः //
292.m:
Daṇḍīśa, Bhautika, Sadyojāta, Anugraheśvara,
Akrūra, and Mahāsena—these are the protective deities.

292.s:
tataḥ krodhīśattaṇḍau ca pañcāntakaśivottamau /
tathaiva rudrakūrmau ca trinetrau caturānanaḥ //
292.d:
ततः क्रोधीशत्तण्डौ च पञ्चान्तकशिवोत्तमौ /
तथैव रुद्रकूर्मौ च त्रिनेत्रौ चतुराननः //
292.m:
Then Krodhīśa and Caṇḍa, Pañcāntaka and Śivottama,
likewise Rudra and Kūrma, Trinetra, and Caturānana,

292.s:
ajeśaḥ śarmasoneśau tathā lāṅgalidārukau /
ardhanārīśvaraścomā kāntaścāṣāḍhidaṇḍinau //
292.d:
अजेशः शर्मसोनेशौ तथा लाङ्गलिदारुकौ /
अर्धनारीश्वरश्चोमा कान्तश्चाषाढिदण्डिनौ //
292.m:
Ajeśa, Śarva and Someśa, likewise Lāṅgalin and Dāruka,
Ardhanārīśvara, Umākānta, Āṣāḍhin and Daṇḍin,

292.s:
atrirmonaś ca meṣaś ca lohitaś ca śikhī tathā /
chagalaṇḍadviraṇḍau dvau samahākālavālinau //
292.d:
अत्रिर्मोनश् च मेषश् च लोहितश् च शिखी तथा /
छगलण्डद्विरण्डौ द्वौ समहाकालवालिनौ //
292.m:
Atri, Mona, Meṣa, Lohita, and Śikhin,
Chagalaṇḍa and Dviraṇḍa, along with Mahākāla and Vālin,

292.s:
bhujaṅgaś ca pinākī ca khaḍgīśaś ca vakaḥ punaḥ /
śveto bhṛgurlaguḍīśākṣaś ca sambartakaḥ smṛtaḥ //
292.d:
भुजङ्गश् च पिनाकी च खड्गीशश् च वकः पुनः /
श्वेतो भृगुर्लगुडीशाक्षश् च सम्बर्तकः स्मृतः //
292.m:
Bhujaṅga, Pinākin, Khaḍgīśa, and Baka again,
Śveta, Bhṛgu, Laguḍīśa, Akṣa, and Saṃvartaka is remembered.

292.s:
rudrātmaśaktān likhyādīn namontān vinyaset kramāt /
aṅgāni vinyasetsarve mantrāḥ sāṅgāstu siddhidāḥ //
292.d:
रुद्रात्मशक्तान् लिख्यादीन् नमोन्तान् विन्यसेत् क्रमात् /
अङ्गानि विन्यसेत्सर्वे मन्त्राः साङ्गास्तु सिद्धिदाः //
292.m:
One should deposit in order [these deities who are] identical with the powers of Rudra, ending with 'namaḥ', beginning with the vowels.
One should deposit the limb[-mantras]; all mantras endowed with limbs grant accomplishment.

292.s:
hṛllekhāvyomasapūrvāṇyetānyaṅgāni vinyaset /
hṛdādīnyaṅgamantrāntair yo japeddhṛdaye namaḥ //
292.d:
हृल्लेखाव्योमसपूर्वाण्येतान्यङ्गानि विन्यसेत् /
हृदादीन्यङ्गमन्त्रान्तैर् यो जपेद्धृदये नमः //
292.m:
One should deposit these limbs preceded by Hṛllekhā and Vyoman.
One who recites ending with the limb-mantras: 'hṛdayāya namaḥ' at the heart,

292.s:
svāhā śirasyatha vaṣaṭśikhāyāṃ kavace c hūṃ /
vauṣat netre 'strāya phaṭasyāt pañcāṅgaṃ netravarjitam //
292.d:
स्वाहा शिरस्यथ वषट्शिखायां कवचे च् हूं /
वौषत् नेत्रे ऽस्त्राय फटस्यात् पञ्चाङ्गं नेत्रवर्जितम् //
292.m:
'svāhā' at the head, then 'vaṣaṭ' at the crest, and 'hūṃ' on the armor,
'vauṣaṭ' on the eyes, 'astrāya phaṭ' for the weapon; the five-limbed [nyāsa] lacks the eyes.

292.s:
niraṅgasyātmanā cāṅgaṃ nyasyemānniyutaṃ japet /
kramābhyāṃ devīṃ vāgīśīṃ yathoktāṃstu tilān hunet //
:p 88
292.d:
निरङ्गस्यात्मना चाङ्गं न्यस्येमान्नियुतं जपेत् /
क्रमाभ्यां देवीं वागीशीं यथोक्तांस्तु तिलान् हुनेत् //
:प् 88
292.m:
For [a mantra] without limbs, having deposited the limbs with one's self, one should recite these a hundred thousand times.
In both ways, one should sacrifice sesame seeds as prescribed to the goddess Vāgīśī.
[Page 88]

292.s:
lipidevī sākṣasūtrakumbhapustakapadmadhṛk /
kavitvādi prayaccheta karmādau siddhaye nyaset /
niṣkavirnirmalaḥ sarve mantrāḥsidhyanti mātṛbhiḥ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe mantraparibhāṣā nāma
dvinavatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:ś atha trinavatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
nāgalakṣaṇāni
agnirucāca
292.d:
लिपिदेवी साक्षसूत्रकुम्भपुस्तकपद्मधृक् /
कवित्वादि प्रयच्छेत कर्मादौ सिद्धये न्यसेत् /
निष्कविर्निर्मलः सर्वे मन्त्राःसिध्यन्ति मातृभिः //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे मन्त्रपरिभाषा नाम
द्विनवत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
:श् अथ त्रिनवत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
नागलक्षणानि
अग्निरुचाच
292.m:
Lipidevī holds a rosary, a water-pot, a book, and a lotus;
she bestows poetic skill and the like; one should perform the ritual deposition at the beginning of rites for success.
One becomes free of flaw and stainless; all mantras become accomplished by means of the Mother [syllables].
Thus ends the two hundred and ninety-second chapter in the great Agni Purāṇa, entitled 'General Definitions of Mantras'.
Now follows the two hundred and ninety-third chapter.
Characteristics of Serpents.
Agni said:

293.s:
nāgādayo 'tha bhāvādidaśasthānāni karma ca /
sūtakaṃ daṣṭaceṣṭeti saptalakṣaṇamucyate //
293.d:
नागादयो ऽथ भावादिदशस्थानानि कर्म च /
सूतकं दष्टचेष्टेति सप्तलक्षणमुच्यते //
293.m:
The classes of serpents and others, the ten conditions and locations, and the action,
the astrological birth-omen, and the behavior of the bitten—these are declared to be the seven characteristics.

293.s:
śeṣavāsukitakṣākhyāḥ karkaṭo 'bjo mahāmbujaḥ /
śaṅkhapālaś ca kulika ity aṣṭaunāgavaryakāḥ //
293.d:
शेषवासुकितक्षाख्याः कर्कटो ऽब्जो महाम्बुजः /
शङ्खपालश् च कुलिक इत्य् अष्टौनागवर्यकाः //
293.m: Śeṣa, Vāsuki, named Takṣaka, Karkaṭa, Abja, Mahāmbuja, / Śaṅkhapāla, and Kulika—these are the eight chief serpents.

293.s:
daśāṣṭapañcatriguṇaśatamūrdhānvitau kramāt /
viprau nṛpo viśau śūdrau dvau dvau nāgeṣu kīrtitau //
293.d:
दशाष्टपञ्चत्रिगुणशतमूर्धान्वितौ क्रमात् /
विप्रौ नृपो विशौ शूद्रौ द्वौ द्वौ नागेषु कीर्तितौ //
293.m: Endowed with ten, eight, five, and three times a hundred hoods in order, / two are declared brāhmaṇas, one king, two vaiśyas, and two śūdras among serpents.

293.s:
tadanvayāḥ pañcaśataṃ tebhyo jātā asaṃkhyakāḥ /
phaṇimaṇḍalirājīlavātapittakaphātmakāḥ //
293.d:
तदन्वयाः पञ्चशतं तेभ्यो जाता असंख्यकाः /
फणिमण्डलिराजीलवातपित्तकफात्मकाः //
293.m: Their lineage consists of five hundred, and innumerable ones were born from them. / Hooded, circulatory, and striped [snakes] consist of wind, bile, and phlegm [respectively].

293.s:
vyantarā doṣamiśrāste sarpāṃ darvīkarāḥ smṛtāḥ /
rathāṅgalāṅgalacchatrasvastikāṅkuśadhāriṇaḥ(1) //
293.d:
व्यन्तरा दोषमिश्रास्ते सर्पां दर्वीकराः स्मृताः /
रथाङ्गलाङ्गलच्छत्रस्वस्तिकाङ्कुशधारिणः(1) //
293.m: Intermediate [snakes] have mixed humors; hooded snakes are known as darvīkaras, / bearing [the marks of] a chariot-wheel, a plough, an umbrella, a svastika, or an elephant-goad.

293.s:
gonasā mandagā dīrghā maṇḍalair vidhaiścitāḥ(2) /
:n
1 rathāṅgalāṅgalatramuṣṭikāṅkuśadhāriṇa iti kha..
2 sthitā iti kha..
:p 89
rājilāścitritāḥ snigdhāstiryagūrdhvañca vājibhiḥ //
293.d:
गोनसा मन्दगा दीर्घा मण्डलैर् विधैश्चिताः(2) /
:न्
1 रथाङ्गलाङ्गलत्रमुष्टिकाङ्कुशधारिण इति ख..
2 स्थिता इति ख..
:प् 89
राजिलाश्चित्रिताः स्निग्धास्तिर्यगूर्ध्वञ्च वाजिभिः //
293.m:
Gonasas are slow-moving, long, and covered with circles of various kinds.
[Footnote]
1. 'rathāṅgalāṅgalatramuṣṭikāṅkuśadhāriṇaḥ' according to manuscript kha.
2. 'sthitāḥ' according to manuscript kha.
[p. 89]
Rājilas are variegated, glossy, and [marked] horizontally and vertically with stripes.

293.s:
vyantarā miśracihnāś ca bhūvarṣāgneyavāyavaḥ /
caturvidhāste ṣaḍviṃśabhedāḥ ṣoḍaśa gonasāḥ //
293.d:
व्यन्तरा मिश्रचिह्नाश् च भूवर्षाग्नेयवायवः /
चतुर्विधास्ते षड्विंशभेदाः षोडश गोनसाः //
293.m: Intermediate snakes have mixed marks; [they are divided according to] earth, rain, fire, and wind. / They are of four kinds with twenty-six varieties; the gonasas are sixteen [varieties].

293.s:
trayodaśa ca rājīlā vyantarā ekaviṃśatiḥ /
ye 'nuktakāle jāyante sarpāste vyantarāḥ smṛtāḥ //
293.d:
त्रयोदश च राजीला व्यन्तरा एकविंशतिः /
ये ऽनुक्तकाले जायन्ते सर्पास्ते व्यन्तराः स्मृताः //
293.m: The rājilas are thirteen, and the intermediate ones are twenty-one. / Snakes that are born at an improper time are remembered as intermediate snakes.

293.s:
āṣāḍhāditrimāsaiḥ syādgarbho māṣacatuṣṭaye /
aṇḍkānāṃ śate dve ca catvāriṃśat prasūyate //
293.d:
आषाढादित्रिमासैः स्याद्गर्भो माषचतुष्टये /
अण्ड्कानां शते द्वे च चत्वारिंशत् प्रसूयते //
293.m: Conception occurs in the three months beginning with Āṣāḍha; in four months [the embryo develops]. / Two hundred and forty eggs are laid.

293.s:
sarpā grasanti sūtaughān vinā strīpunnapuṃsakān /
unmīlate 'kṣi saptāhāt kṛṣṇo māsādbhavedvahiḥ //
293.d:
सर्पा ग्रसन्ति सूतौघान् विना स्त्रीपुन्नपुंसकान् /
उन्मीलते ऽक्षि सप्ताहात् कृष्णो मासाद्भवेद्वहिः //
293.m: The serpents swallow their brood of offspring, except for females, males, and neuters. / The eyes open after seven days; after a month [the snake] becomes dark outside.

293.s:
dvādaśāhāt subodhaḥ syāt dantāḥ syuḥ sūryadarśanāt /
dvātriṃśaddinaviṃśatyā catasrasteṣu daṃṣtrikāḥ //
293.d:
द्वादशाहात् सुबोधः स्यात् दन्ताः स्युः सूर्यदर्शनात् /
द्वात्रिंशद्दिनविंशत्या चतस्रस्तेषु दंष्त्रिकाः //
293.m: From twelve days there is clear awareness; teeth emerge from the sight of the sun. / In thirty-two days or twenty, among them there are four fangs:

293.s:
karālī makarī kālarātrī ca yamadūtikā /
etāstāḥ saviṣā daṃṣṭrā vāmadakṣiṇapārśvagāḥ //
293.d:
कराली मकरी कालरात्री च यमदूतिका /
एतास्ताः सविषा दंष्ट्रा वामदक्षिणपार्श्वगाः //
293.m: Karālī, Makarī, Kālarātrī, and Yamadūtikā. / These are the poisonous fangs situated on the left and right sides.

293.s:
ṣanmāsānmucyate kṛttiṃ jovetsaṣṭisamādvayaṃ /
nāgāḥ sūryādivāreśāḥ sapta uktā divā niśi //
293.d:
षन्मासान्मुच्यते कृत्तिं जोवेत्सष्टिसमाद्वयं /
नागाः सूर्यादिवारेशाः सप्त उक्ता दिवा निशि //
293.m: After six months it sheds its skin; it lives for one hundred and twenty years. / The seven serpents are declared the lords of the days beginning with Sunday, day and night.

293.s:
sveṣāṃ ṣaṭ prativāreṣu kulikaḥ sarvasandhiṣu /
śaṅkhena vā mahābjena saha tasyodayo 'thavā //
293.d:
स्वेषां षट् प्रतिवारेषु कुलिकः सर्वसन्धिषु /
शङ्खेन वा महाब्जेन सह तस्योदयो ऽथवा //
293.m: Kulika [presides] in all junctions, with six [portions] for their own respective days; / or its rising occurs together with Śaṅkha or Mahābja,

293.s:
dvayīrvā nāḍikāmantramantrakaṃ(1) kulikodayaḥ /
duṣṭaḥ sa kālaḥ sarvatra sarpadaṃśe viśeṣataḥ(2) //
293.d:
द्वयीर्वा नाडिकामन्त्रमन्त्रकं(1) कुलिकोदयः /
दुष्टः स कालः सर्वत्र सर्पदंशे विशेषतः(2) //
293.m: or the rising of Kulika lasts for a measure of two nāḍikās. / That time is inauspicious everywhere, especially in snakebites.

293.s:
kṛttikā bharaṇī svātī mūlaṃ pūrvatrayāśvanī /
viśākhārdrā maghāśleṣā citrā śravaṇarohiṇī //
293.d:
कृत्तिका भरणी स्वाती मूलं पूर्वत्रयाश्वनी /
विशाखार्द्रा मघाश्लेषा चित्रा श्रवणरोहिणी //
293.m: Kṛttikā, Bharaṇī, Svātī, Mūla, the three Pūrvas, Aśvinī, / Viśākhā, Ārdrā, Maghā, Āśleṣā, Citrā, Śravaṇā, Rohiṇī,

293.s:
hastā mandakujau vārau pañcamī cāṣṭamī tithiḥ /
:n
1 nāḍikāmātrasantrakamiti ña..
2 vinirdiśediti ka.. , kha.. , ja.. , ṭa.. ca
:p 90
ṣaṣṭhī raiktā śivā nindyā pañcamī ca caturdaśī //
293.d:
हस्ता मन्दकुजौ वारौ पञ्चमी चाष्टमी तिथिः /
:न्
1 नाडिकामात्रसन्त्रकमिति ञ..
2 विनिर्दिशेदिति क.. , ख.. , ज.. , ट.. च
:प् 90
षष्ठी रैक्ता शिवा निन्द्या पञ्चमी च चतुर्दशी //
293.m:
Hastā, the days of Saturn and Mars, the fifth and eighth lunar days,
[Footnote]
1. 'nāḍikāmātrasantrakam' according to manuscript ña.
2. 'vinirdiśet' according to manuscripts ka, kha, ja, and ṭa.
[p. 90]
the sixth, empty, and auspicious [tithis are deemed] reprehensible, as well as the fifth and fourteenth.

293.s:
sandhyācatuṣṭayaṃ duṣṭaṃ dagdhayogāś ca rāśayaḥ /
ekadvibahavo daṃśā daṣṭaviddhañca khaṇḍitam //
293.d:
सन्ध्याचतुष्टयं दुष्टं दग्धयोगाश् च राशयः /
एकद्विबहवो दंशा दष्टविद्धञ्च खण्डितम् //
293.m: The four twilights are inauspicious, as are burnt configurations and zodiacal signs. / The bites are one, two, or many, and [classified as] bitten, pierced, and torn.

293.s:
adaṃśamavaguptaṃ(1) syāddaṃśamevaṃ caturvidham /
trayo dvyekakṣatā daṃśā vedanā rudhirolvaṇā //
293.d:
अदंशमवगुप्तं(1) स्याद्दंशमेवं चतुर्विधम् /
त्रयो द्व्येकक्षता दंशा वेदना रुधिरोल्वणा //
293.m: [The bite] without fang-marks is concealed; thus the bite is of four kinds. / Bites may have three, two, or one puncture, with pain and profuse bleeding.

293.s:
naktantvekāṅghrikūrmābhā daṃśāś ca yamacoditāḥ /
dīhīpipīlikāsparśī kaṇṭhaśotharujānvitaḥ(2) //
293.d:
नक्तन्त्वेकाङ्घ्रिकूर्माभा दंशाश् च यमचोदिताः /
दीहीपिपीलिकास्पर्शी कण्ठशोथरुजान्वितः(2) //
293.m: Bites at night resembling a turtle with one foot are impelled by Yama. / Bites that feel like creeping ants, accompanied by swelling and pain in the throat,

293.s:
satodo ranthito daṃśaḥ saviṣo nyastanirviṣaḥ /
devālaye śūnyagṛhe valmīkodyānakoṭare //
293.d:
सतोदो रन्थितो दंशः सविषो न्यस्तनिर्विषः /
देवालये शून्यगृहे वल्मीकोद्यानकोटरे //
293.m: with pricking pain and hardening, are venomous; the rest are non-venomous. / [A bite inflicted] in a temple, an abandoned house, an anthill, the hollow of a garden [tree],

293.s:
rathyāsandhau śmaśāne ca nadyāñca sindhusaṅgame /
dvīpe catuṣpathe saudhe gṛhe 'bje parvatāgrataḥ //
293.d:
रथ्यासन्धौ श्मशाने च नद्याञ्च सिन्धुसङ्गमे /
द्वीपे चतुष्पथे सौधे गृहे ऽब्जे पर्वताग्रतः //
293.m: at a road junction, in a cremation ground, at a river, at a confluence with the ocean, / on an island, at a crossroads, in a palace, in a house, at a lotus pond, before a mountain,

293.s:
vilahadvāre jīrṇakūpe jīrṇaveśmani kuḍyake /
śigruśleṣmātakākṣeṣu jambū ḍumbareṇeṣu ca //
293.d:
विलहद्वारे जीर्णकूपे जीर्णवेश्मनि कुड्यके /
शिग्रुश्लेष्मातकाक्षेषु जम्बू डुम्बरेणेषु च //
293.m: at the opening of a hole, in an old well, in a ruined house, against a wall, / on a moringa, a śleṣmātaka, an akṣa tree, or among jambū and udumbara trees,

293.s:
vaṭe ca jīrṇaprākāre khāsyahṛtkakṣajatruṇi /
tālau śaṅkhe gale mūrdhni civuke nābhipādayoḥ //
293.d:
वटे च जीर्णप्राकारे खास्यहृत्कक्षजत्रुणि /
तालौ शङ्खे गले मूर्ध्नि चिवुके नाभिपादयोः //
293.m: or on a banyan tree, an old rampart, or on the cavity of the mouth, heart, armpit, collarbone, / palate, temple, throat, head, chin, navel, or feet—

293.s:
daṃśo 'śubhaḥ śubho dūtaḥ puṣpahastaḥ suvāk sudhīḥ /
liṅgavarṇasamānaś ca śuklavastro 'malaḥ śuciḥ //
293.d:
दंशो ऽशुभः शुभो दूतः पुष्पहस्तः सुवाक् सुधीः /
लिङ्गवर्णसमानश् च शुक्लवस्त्रो ऽमलः शुचिः //
293.m: such a bite is inauspicious. An auspicious messenger has flowers in hand, speaks well, is wise, / is equal in gender and caste [to the bitten person], wears white garments, is clean, and is pure.

293.s:
apadvāragataḥ śastrī pramādī bhūgatekṣaṇaḥ /
vivarṇavāsāḥ pāśādihasto gadgadavarṇabhāk //
293.d:
अपद्वारगतः शस्त्री प्रमादी भूगतेक्षणः /
विवर्णवासाः पाशादिहस्तो गद्गदवर्णभाक् //
293.m: One who approaches by the wrong door, carries a weapon, is careless, looks at the ground, / wears discoloured garments, holds a noose or the like, speaks with a stammering voice,

293.s:
śuṣkakāṣṭhāśritaḥ khinnastilāktakakarāṃśukaḥ /
ārdravāsāḥ kṛṣṇaraktapuṣpayuktaśiroruhaḥ //
293.d:
शुष्ककाष्ठाश्रितः खिन्नस्तिलाक्तककरांशुकः /
आर्द्रवासाः कृष्णरक्तपुष्पयुक्तशिरोरुहः //
293.m: leans on dry wood, is depressed, has hands smeared with sesamum, wears rags, / wears wet clothes, has black and red flowers in the hair,

293.s:
kucamardī nakhacchedī gudaspṛk pādalekhakaḥ /
:n
1 sadaṃśamavaluptamiti ña..
2 kaṇṭhaśoṣarujāntrita iti ña..
:p 91
keśamuñcī tṛṇacchedī duṣṭā dūtāstathaikaśaḥ //
293.d:
कुचमर्दी नखच्छेदी गुदस्पृक् पादलेखकः /
:न्
1 सदंशमवलुप्तमिति ञ..
2 कण्ठशोषरुजान्त्रित इति ञ..
:प् 91
केशमुञ्ची तृणच्छेदी दुष्टा दूतास्तथैकशः //
293.m:
presses the breast, cuts nails, touches the anus, scratches the feet,
[Footnote]
1. Variant reading: 'with a bite, obscured' in manuscript ña.
2. Variant reading: 'accompanied by dryness and pain in the throat' in manuscript ña. / [Page 91]
pulls hair, or cuts grass—such messengers are evil, one and all.

293.s:
iḍānyā vā vaheddvedhā yadi dūtasya cātmanaḥ /
ābhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ puṣṭayāsmān vidyāstrīpunnapuṃsakān //
293.d:
इडान्या वा वहेद्द्वेधा यदि दूतस्य चात्मनः /
आभ्यां द्वाभ्यां पुष्टयास्मान् विद्यास्त्रीपुन्नपुंसकान् //
293.m: Whether the iḍā or the other [nāḍī] flows in two ways, if of the messenger or of oneself, / from both of these, through its strength, one should recognise female, male, or neuter.

293.s:
dūtaḥ spṛśati yadgātraṃ tasmin daṃśamudāharet /
dūtāṅghricalanaṃ duṣṭhamutthitirniś calā śubhā //
293.d:
दूतः स्पृशति यद्गात्रं तस्मिन् दंशमुदाहरेत् /
दूताङ्घ्रिचलनं दुष्ठमुत्थितिर्निश् चला शुभा //
