293.m: The limb that the messenger touches, at that limb one should declare the bite. / The movement of the messenger's foot is evil; standing still is auspicious.

293.s:
jīvapārśve śubho dūto duṣṭo 'nyatra sammāgataḥ /
jīvo gatāgatair duṣṭaḥ śubho dūtanivedane //
293.d:
जीवपार्श्वे शुभो दूतो दुष्टो ऽन्यत्र सम्मागतः /
जीवो गतागतैर् दुष्टः शुभो दूतनिवेदने //
293.m: A messenger on the living [favourable] side is auspicious; one arriving on the other is evil. / The living breath that comes and goes is inauspicious; it is auspicious during the messenger's report.

293.s:
dūtasya vāk praduṣṭā sā pūrvāmajārdhaninditā /
vibhaktaistasya vākyāntairviṣarnirviṣakālatā(?) //
293.d:
दूतस्य वाक् प्रदुष्टा सा पूर्वामजार्धनिन्दिता /
विभक्तैस्तस्य वाक्यान्तैर्विषर्निर्विषकालता(?) //
293.m: The messenger's speech is corrupted if spoken with the first half censured; / by dividing the ends of his speech, the venomous or non-venomous period [is known].

293.s:
ādyaiḥ svaraiś ca kādyaś ca vargair bhinnalipirdvidhā /
svarajo vasumānvargī itikṣepā ca mātṛkā //
293.d:
आद्यैः स्वरैश् च काद्यश् च वर्गैर् भिन्नलिपिर्द्विधा /
स्वरजो वसुमान्वर्गी इतिक्षेपा च मातृका //
293.m: By the initial vowels and the vargas beginning with ka, the script is twofold. / The vowel-born possesses wealth; the varga-born and its dismissal make up the mātṛkā.

293.s:
vātāgnīndrajalātmāno vargeṣu ca catuṣṭayam /
napuṃsakāḥ pañcamāḥ syuḥ svarāḥ śakrāmbuyonayaḥ //
293.d:
वाताग्नीन्द्रजलात्मानो वर्गेषु च चतुष्टयम् /
नपुंसकाः पञ्चमाः स्युः स्वराः शक्राम्बुयोनयः //
293.m: The four [letters] in the vargas have the nature of wind, fire, Indra, and water; / the fifth [letters] are neuter; the vowels originate from Indra and water.

293.s:
duṣṭau dūtasya vākpādau vātāgnī madhyamo hariḥ /
praśastā vāruṇā varṇā atiduṣṭā napuṃsakāḥ //
293.d:
दुष्टौ दूतस्य वाक्पादौ वाताग्नी मध्यमो हरिः /
प्रशस्ता वारुणा वर्णा अतिदुष्टा नपुंसकाः //
293.m: The speech and feet of the messenger are evil [if belonging to] wind and fire; the middle one is Viṣṇu. / Letters belonging to Varuṇa are praised; neuter letters are extremely evil.

293.s:
prasthāne maṅgalaṃ vākyaṃ garjitaṃ meghahastinoḥ /
pradakṣiṇaṃ phale vṛkṣe vāmasya ca rutaṃ jitaṃ //
293.d:
प्रस्थाने मङ्गलं वाक्यं गर्जितं मेघहस्तिनोः /
प्रदक्षिणं फले वृक्षे वामस्य च रुतं जितं //
293.m: At departure, auspicious speech, the roar of clouds or elephants, / a clockwise circumambulation, a fruitful tree, and a sound on the left bring victory.

293.s:
śubhā gītādiśabdāḥ syurīdṛśaṃ syādasiddhaye /
anarthagīrathākrando dakṣiṇe virutaṃ kṣutam //
293.d:
शुभा गीतादिशब्दाः स्युरीदृशं स्यादसिद्धये /
अनर्थगीरथाक्रन्दो दक्षिणे विरुतं क्षुतम् //
293.m: Auspicious are sounds of singing and the like; the contrary leads to failure: / inauspicious songs, lamentation, a cry on the right, or a sneeze.

293.s:
veśyā kṣuto nṛpaḥ kanyā gaurdantī murajadhvajau /
kṣīrājyadadhiśaṅkhāmbu chatraṃ bherī phalaṃ surāḥ //
293.d:
वेश्या क्षुतो नृपः कन्या गौर्दन्ती मुरजध्वजौ /
क्षीराज्यदधिशङ्खाम्बु छत्रं भेरी फलं सुराः //
293.m: A courtesan, one who sneezed, a king, a maiden, a cow, an elephant, a tabor, a banner, / milk, clarified butter, curds, a conch, water, an umbrella, a kettle-drum, fruit, spirits,

293.s:
taṇḍulā hema rupyañca siddhaye 'bhimukhā amī /
sakāṣṭhaḥ sānalaḥ kārurmalināmbarabhāvabhṛt //
:p 92
293.d:
तण्डुला हेम रुप्यञ्च सिद्धये ऽभिमुखा अमी /
सकाष्ठः सानलः कारुर्मलिनाम्बरभावभृत् //
:प् 92
293.m:
rice grains, gold, and silver—these, met facing forward, lead to success. / One carrying wood, fire, an artisan, one wearing dirty garments,
[Page 92]

293.s:
galasthaṭaṅgo gomāyugṛdhrolūkakapardikāḥ /
tailaṃ kapālakārpāsā niṣedhe bhasma naṣṭaye //
293.d:
गलस्थटङ्गो गोमायुगृध्रोलूककपर्दिकाः /
तैलं कपालकार्पासा निषेधे भस्म नष्टये //
293.m: one with an axe at the neck, a jackal, a vulture, an owl, cowries, / oil, a skull, cotton—[these encountered] upon forbidding lead to destruction, and ashes bring ruin.

293.s:
viṣarogāś ca sapta syurdhātordhātvantarāptitaḥ /
viṣadaṃśo lalāṭaṃ yātyatonetraṃ tatau sukham /
āsyācca vacanīnāḍyau dhātūna prāpnoti hi kramāt //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe nāgalakṣaṇadirnāma
trinavatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:ś atha caturnavatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
daṣṭacikitsā
293.d:
विषरोगाश् च सप्त स्युर्धातोर्धात्वन्तराप्तितः /
विषदंशो ललाटं यात्यतोनेत्रं ततौ सुखम् /
आस्याच्च वचनीनाड्यौ धातून प्राप्नोति हि क्रमात् //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे नागलक्षणदिर्नाम
त्रिनवत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
:श् अथ चतुर्नवत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
दष्टचिकित्सा
293.m:
The stages of venom are seven, through its passage from one bodily tissue to another. / The venomous bite travels to the forehead, then to the eye, then to the mouth, / and from the mouth to the vocal channels; thus it reaches the bodily tissues in succession.
Thus in the great Purāṇa of Agni, the two hundred and ninety-third chapter, entitled 'Characteristics of Serpents and the Like'.
Now, the two hundred and ninety-fourth chapter.
Treatment of snakebite.

294.s:
agnir uvāca
mantradhyānauṣadhair daṣṭacikitsāṃ pravadāmi te /
oṃ namo bhagavate nīlakaṇṭhāyeti /
japanādviṣahāniḥ syadauṣadhaṃ jīvarakṣaṇaṃ //
294.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
मन्त्रध्यानौषधैर् दष्टचिकित्सां प्रवदामि ते /
ओं नमो भगवते नीलकण्ठायेति /
जपनाद्विषहानिः स्यदौषधं जीवरक्षणं //
294.m: Agni said: / I will explain to you the treatment of snakebite through mantras, meditation, and medicines. / By repeating 'oṃ namo bhagavate nīlakaṇṭhāya', venom is destroyed; medicine protects life.

294.s:
sājyaṃ sakṛdrasaṃ peyaṃ dvividhaṃ viṣamucyate /
jaṅgamaṃ sarpabhūṣādi śṛṅgyādi sthāvaraṃ viṣaṃ //
294.d:
साज्यं सकृद्रसं पेयं द्विविधं विषमुच्यते /
जङ्गमं सर्पभूषादि शृङ्ग्यादि स्थावरं विषं //
294.m: Juice with clarified butter is to be drunk at once. Venom is declared to be of two kinds: / mobile, such as from serpents and insects; and immobile venom, such as from poisonous tubers and plants.

294.s:
śāntasvarānvito brahmā lohitaṃ tārakaṃ(1) śivaḥ /
viyaternāmamantro 'yaṃ tārkṣaḥ śabdamayaḥ smṛtaḥ //
oṃ jvala mahāmate hṛdayāya garuḍavirālaśirase(2) garuḍaśikhāyai
garuḍa viṣabhañjana prabhedana prabhedana vitrāsaya vitrāsaya
vima-[!!!]
:n
1 tārakaḥ iti kha..
2 garuḍavilāsaśirase iti kha..
:p 93
rdaya vimardaya kavacāya apratihataśāmanaṃ vaṃ hūṃ phaṭ astrāya
ugrarūpavāraka sarvabhayaṅkara bhīṣaya sarvaṃ daha daha bhasmīkuru
kuru svāhā netrāya
saptavargāntayugmāṣṭadigdalasvara keśarādivarṇaruddhaṃ
vahnirābhūtakarṇakaṃ mātṛkāmbujaṃ
294.d:
शान्तस्वरान्वितो ब्रह्मा लोहितं तारकं(1) शिवः /
वियतेर्नाममन्त्रो ऽयं तार्क्षः शब्दमयः स्मृतः //
ओं ज्वल महामते हृदयाय गरुडविरालशिरसे(2) गरुडशिखायै
गरुड विषभञ्जन प्रभेदन प्रभेदन वित्रासय वित्रासय
विम-[!!!]
:न्
1 तारकः इति ख..
2 गरुडविलासशिरसे इति ख..
:प् 93
र्दय विमर्दय कवचाय अप्रतिहतशामनं वं हूं फट् अस्त्राय
उग्ररूपवारक सर्वभयङ्कर भीषय सर्वं दह दह भस्मीकुरु
कुरु स्वाहा नेत्राय
सप्तवर्गान्तयुग्माष्टदिग्दलस्वर केशरादिवर्णरुद्धं
वह्निराभूतकर्णकं मातृकाम्बुजं
294.m:
Brahmā accompanied by a calm vowel, red, the deliverer, is Śiva. / This is the name-mantra of Garuda (the son of Vinatā); it is remembered as consisting of sound.
"Oṃ, blaze, O high-minded one, to the heart; to the cat-headed Garuḍa, to the head; to Garuḍa's crest; / O Garuḍa, breaker of venom, piercer, piercer, terrify, terrify, crush, [crush]..."
[Footnote]
1. Variant reading: 'tārakaḥ' in manuscript kha.
2. Variant reading: 'to the playful head of Garuḍa' in manuscript kha. / [Page 93]
"...crush, crush, for the armour; unimpeded pacification, vaṃ hūṃ phaṭ for the weapon; / averter of terrifying forms, causing all fear, frighten! Burn everything, burn, reduce to ashes, svāhā to the eyes."
A lotus of the mātṛkā enclosed by the letters of the eight directions of petals and the vowels of the filaments, ending in the seven vargas, / having a pericarp formed by the essence of fire,

294.s:
kṛtvā hṛdisthaṃ tanmantrī vāmahastatale smaret /
aṅgaṣṭhādau nyasedvarṇānviyaterbheditāḥ kalāḥ(1) //
294.d:
कृत्वा हृदिस्थं तन्मन्त्री वामहस्ततले स्मरेत् /
अङ्गष्ठादौ न्यसेद्वर्णान्वियतेर्भेदिताः कलाः(1) //
294.m: having placed it in the heart, the practitioner of mantras should visualise it in the palm of the left hand. / He should deposit the syllables on the thumb and other fingers as divided parts of Garuḍa:

294.s:
pītaṃ vajracatuṣkoṇaṃ pārthivaṃ śakradaivataṃ /
vṛttārdhamāpyapadmārdhaṃ śuklaṃ varūṇadaivataṃ //
294.d:
पीतं वज्रचतुष्कोणं पार्थिवं शक्रदैवतं /
वृत्तार्धमाप्यपद्मार्धं शुक्लं वरूणदैवतं //
294.m: yellow, four-cornered with vajras, earthy, presided over by Śakra; / a half-circle, half a watery lotus, white, presided over by Varuṇa;

294.s:
tryastraṃ svastikayuktañca taijasaṃ vahnidaivataṃ /
vṛttaṃ vinduvṛtaṃ vāyudaivataṃ kṛṣṇamālinam //
294.d:
त्र्यस्त्रं स्वस्तिकयुक्तञ्च तैजसं वह्निदैवतं /
वृत्तं विन्दुवृतं वायुदैवतं कृष्णमालिनम् //
294.m: triangular and furnished with a svastika, fiery, presided over by Agni; / circular, surrounded by a dot, presided over by Vāyu, garlanded in black.

294.s:
aṅguṣṭhādyaṅgulīmadhye paryasteṣu svaveśmasu /
suvarṇanāgavāhena veṣṭhiteṣu nyaset kramāt //
294.d:
अङ्गुष्ठाद्यङ्गुलीमध्ये पर्यस्तेषु स्ववेश्मसु /
सुवर्णनागवाहेन वेष्ठितेषु न्यसेत् क्रमात् //
294.m: In the middle of the fingers beginning with the thumb, turned downward in their own abodes, / encircled by the golden mount of snakes (Garuḍa), he should deposit them in order.

294.s:
viyateś caturo varṇān sumaṇḍalasamatviṣaḥ /
arūpe ravatanmātre(2) ākāśeśivadevate //
294.d:
वियतेश् चतुरो वर्णान् सुमण्डलसमत्विषः /
अरूपे रवतन्मात्रे(2) आकाशेशिवदेवते //
294.m: The four syllables of Garuḍa, having splendour equal to the auspicious maṇḍalas; / in formless ether consisting of sound, presided over by Śiva,

294.s:
kaniṣṭhāmadhyaparvasthe nyasettasyādyamakṣaram /
nāgānāmādivarṇāṃś ca svamaṇḍalagatānnyaset //
294.d:
कनिष्ठामध्यपर्वस्थे न्यसेत्तस्याद्यमक्षरम् /
नागानामादिवर्णांश् च स्वमण्डलगतान्न्यसेत् //
294.m: situated on the middle joint of the little finger, he should deposit its first syllable; / and he should deposit the initial letters of the serpents situated in their own maṇḍalas.

294.s:
bhūtādivarṇān vinyasedaṅguṣṭādyantaparvasu /
tanmātrādiguṇābhyarṇānaṅgulīṣu nyasedbudhaḥ //
294.d:
भूतादिवर्णान् विन्यसेदङ्गुष्टाद्यन्तपर्वसु /
तन्मात्रादिगुणाभ्यर्णानङ्गुलीषु न्यसेद्बुधः //
294.m: He should deposit the letters of the elements on the end joints beginning with the thumb; / the wise one should deposit [the letters] near to the subtle elements and other qualities on the fingers.

294.s:
sparśanādevatārkṣeṇa haste hanyādviṣadvayaṃ /
maṇḍalādiṣu tān varṇān viyateḥ kavayo jitān //
294.d:
स्पर्शनादेवतार्क्षेण हस्ते हन्याद्विषद्वयं /
मण्डलादिषु तान् वर्णान् वियतेः कवयो जितान् //
294.m: Merely by the touch of Garuḍa in the hand, he destroys the two types of venom. / The wise have conquered those syllables of Garuḍa on the maṇḍalas and the rest;

294.s:
śreṣṭhadvyaṅgulibhirdehanābhisthāneṣu parvasu /
:n
1 bhedikāstatheti kha..
2 varatanmatre iti kha..
:p 94
ājānutaḥ suvarṇābhamānābhestuhinaprabham //
294.d:
श्रेष्ठद्व्यङ्गुलिभिर्देहनाभिस्थानेषु पर्वसु /
:न्
1 भेदिकास्तथेति ख..
2 वरतन्मत्रे इति ख..
:प् 94
आजानुतः सुवर्णाभमानाभेस्तुहिनप्रभम् //
294.m:
with the two best fingers, on the joints in the regions of the body and the navel,
[Footnote]
1. Variant reading: 'so the dividers' in manuscript kha.
2. Variant reading: 'varatanmātre' in manuscript kha. / [Page 94]
up to the knees having the lustre of gold, up to the navel possessing the brilliance of snow,

294.s:
kuṅkumāruṇamākaṇṭhādākeśāntāt sitetaraṃ /
brahmāṇḍavyāpinaṃ tārkṣañcandrākhyaṃ nāgabhūṣaṇam //
294.d:
कुङ्कुमारुणमाकण्ठादाकेशान्तात् सितेतरं /
ब्रह्माण्डव्यापिनं तार्क्षञ्चन्द्राख्यं नागभूषणम् //
294.m: saffron-red up to the throat, and other than white (black) up to the hair ends; / pervading the universe, named Garuḍa, adorned with serpents,

294.s:
nīlogranāśamātmānaṃ mahāpakṣaṃ smaredbudhaḥ /
evantātkṣātmano vākyānmantraḥ syānmantriṇo viṣe //
294.d:
नीलोग्रनाशमात्मानं महापक्षं स्मरेद्बुधः /
एवन्तात्क्षात्मनो वाक्यान्मन्त्रः स्यान्मन्त्रिणो विषे //
294.m: the wise one should meditate on oneself having a dark, fierce beak and large wings. / Thus, from the utterance of the one whose self is Garuḍa, the mantra belongs to the mantrin against venom.

294.s:
suṣṭistārkṣakarasyāntaḥsthitāṅguṣṭhaviṣāpahā /
tārkṣaṃ hastaṃ samudyamya tatpañcāṅgulicālanāt //
294.d:
सुष्टिस्तार्क्षकरस्यान्तःस्थिताङ्गुष्ठविषापहा /
तार्क्षं हस्तं समुद्यम्य तत्पञ्चाङ्गुलिचालनात् //
294.m: The fist of Garuḍa's hand, with the thumb placed within, removes venom. / Raising Garuḍa's hand, by moving its five fingers,

294.s:
kuryādviṣasya stambhādīṃstaduktamadavīṣayā /
ākāśādeṣa bhūvījaḥ pañcārṇādhipatirmanuḥ //
294.d:
कुर्याद्विषस्य स्तम्भादींस्तदुक्तमदवीषया /
आकाशादेष भूवीजः पञ्चार्णाधिपतिर्मनुः //
294.m: he should effect the arrest and so forth of the venom, as declared, with the purpose of subduing pride. / Originating from space, this is the earth seed; the mantra is the master of five syllables.

294.s:
saṃstambhayetiviṣato bhāṣayā stambhyedviṣam /
vyatyastabhūṣayā vījo mantro 'yaṃ sādhusādhitaḥ //
294.d:
संस्तम्भयेतिविषतो भाषया स्तम्भ्येद्विषम् /
व्यत्यस्तभूषया वीजो मन्त्रो ऽयं साधुसाधितः //
294.m: With the utterance 'Paralyze! Paralyze!', one should immobilize the poison. / When properly mastered, this mantra, whose seed syllable is transposed, is well perfected.

294.s:
saṃplavaḥ plāvaya yamaḥ(1) śabdādyaḥ saṃharedviṣaṃ /
daṇḍamutthāpayedeṣa sujaptāmbho 'bhiṣekataḥ //
294.d:
संप्लवः प्लावय यमः(1) शब्दाद्यः संहरेद्विषं /
दण्डमुत्थापयेदेष सुजप्ताम्भो ऽभिषेकतः //
294.m: Beginning with the words 'deluge, inundate, Yama', it destroys the poison. / It should raise the staff through consecration by aspersion with water over which the recitation has been well performed.

294.s:
sujaptaśaṅkhabheryādinisvanaśravaṇena vā /
saṃdahatyeva saṃyukto bhūtejovyatyayāt sthitaḥ //
294.d:
सुजप्तशङ्खभेर्यादिनिस्वनश्रवणेन वा /
संदहत्येव संयुक्तो भूतेजोव्यत्ययात् स्थितः //
294.m: Or by hearing the sound of conches, kettledrums, and other instruments over which the recitation was well performed; / united [with it], it burns [the poison] away, abiding through the inversion of earth and fire.

294.s:
bhūvāyuvyatyayānmantro viṣaṃ saṃkrāmayatyasau /
antastho nijaveśmastho vījāgnīndujalātmabhiḥ //
294.d:
भूवायुव्यत्ययान्मन्त्रो विषं संक्रामयत्यसौ /
अन्तस्थो निजवेश्मस्थो वीजाग्नीन्दुजलात्मभिः //
294.m: Through the inversion of earth and wind, this mantra transfers the poison, / staying within one's own dwelling, with the natures of the seed syllable, fire, moon, and water.

294.s:
etat karma nayenmantrī garuḍākṛtivigrahaḥ /
tārkṣavarṇagehasthastajjapānnāśayedviṣam //
294.d:
एतत् कर्म नयेन्मन्त्री गरुडाकृतिविग्रहः /
तार्क्षवर्णगेहस्थस्तज्जपान्नाशयेद्विषम् //
294.m: The mantra practitioner, his body having the form of Garuḍa, should carry out this rite. / Abiding in the house of Garuḍa's color, he destroys the poison through the recitation of it.

294.s:
jāmudaṇḍīdamuditaṃ svadhāśrīvījalāñchitaṃ /
snānapānātsarvaviṣaṃ jvarātogāpamṛtyujit //
294.d:
जामुदण्डीदमुदितं स्वधाश्रीवीजलाञ्छितं /
स्नानपानात्सर्वविषं ज्वरातोगापमृत्युजित् //
294.m: This is stated as the Jāmudaṇḍī [mantra], marked with the seed syllables of Svadhā and Śrī. / By bathing in it and drinking it, it overcomes all poisons, fever, and untimely death.

294.s:
pakṣi pakṣi mahāpakṣi mahāpakṣi vidhi svāhā /
:n
1 yaśa iti ña..
:p 95
pakṣi pakṣi mahāpakṣi mahāpakṣi kṣi kṣi svāhā //
dvāvetau pakṣirāḍmantrau viṣaghnāvabhimantraṇāt
pakṣirājāya vidhmahe pakṣidevāya dhīmahi tatro garuḍa
pracodayāt
vahnisthau pārśvatatpūrvau dantaśrīkau ca daṇḍinau ||
294.d:
पक्षि पक्षि महापक्षि महापक्षि विधि स्वाहा /
:न्
1 यश इति ञ..
:प् 95
पक्षि पक्षि महापक्षि महापक्षि क्षि क्षि स्वाहा //
द्वावेतौ पक्षिराड्मन्त्रौ विषघ्नावभिमन्त्रणात्
पक्षिराजाय विध्महे पक्षिदेवाय धीमहि तत्रो गरुड
प्रचोदयात्
वह्निस्थौ पार्श्वतत्पूर्वौ दन्तश्रीकौ च दण्डिनौ ||
294.m:
'Pakṣi pakṣi mahāpakṣi mahāpakṣi vidhi svāhā!'
[Footnote]
1. In manuscript ña: "yaśaḥ".
[Page 95]
'Pakṣi pakṣi mahāpakṣi mahāpakṣi kṣi kṣi svāhā!'
These two mantras of the king of birds destroy poison through consecration.
'We know the king of birds; we meditate upon the deity of birds; may that Garuḍa inspire us!' / The two standing in fire, beside and before that, having teeth and glory, and holding staffs,

294.s:
sakālo lāṅgalī ceti nīlakaṇṭhādyamīritaṃ /
vakṣaḥkaṇṭhaśikhāśvetaṃ nyasetstambhe susaṃskṛtau //
hara hara hṛdayāya namaḥ kapardine ca śirase nīlakaṇṭhāya vai
śikhāṃ kālakūṭaviṣabhakṣaṇāya svāhā
atha varma ca kaṇṭhe netraṃ kṛttivāsāstrinetraṃ pūrvādyair ānanair
yuktaṃ śvetapītāruṇāsitaiḥ
294.d:
सकालो लाङ्गली चेति नीलकण्ठाद्यमीरितं /
वक्षःकण्ठशिखाश्वेतं न्यसेत्स्तम्भे सुसंस्कृतौ //
हर हर हृदयाय नमः कपर्दिने च शिरसे नीलकण्ठाय वै
शिखां कालकूटविषभक्षणाय स्वाहा
अथ वर्म च कण्ठे नेत्रं कृत्तिवासास्त्रिनेत्रं पूर्वाद्यैर् आननैर्
युक्तं श्वेतपीतारुणासितैः
294.m:
possessing Time, and holding a plow—thus is described that which begins with Nīlakaṇṭha. / White on the chest, throat, and crest, one should place it on the post in good preparation.
'Hara, Hara, homage to the heart! To the one with matted hair, to the head! To the blue-throated one, to the crest! To the devourer of the Kālakūṭa poison, svāhā!'
Then the armor; on the throat, the eye; the three-eyed one clad in animal skins, endowed with faces beginning with the east—white, yellow, reddish, and dark—

294.s:
abhayaṃ varadaṃ cāpaṃ vāsukiñca dadhadbhujaiḥ /
yasyoparītapārśvasthagaurīrudro 'sya devatā //
294.d:
अभयं वरदं चापं वासुकिञ्च दधद्भुजैः /
यस्योपरीतपार्श्वस्थगौरीरुद्रो ऽस्य देवता //
294.m: holding gesture of fearlessness, gesture of granting boons, bow, and Vāsuki in his arms, / above whom, on the side, stands Gaurī—Rudra is his deity.

294.s:
pādajānuguhānābhihṛtkaṇṭhānanamūrdhasu /
mantrārṇānnyasya karayoraṅguṣṭhādyaṅgulīṣu ca //
294.d:
पादजानुगुहानाभिहृत्कण्ठाननमूर्धसु /
मन्त्रार्णान्न्यस्य करयोरङ्गुष्ठाद्यङ्गुलीषु च //
294.m: Having placed the syllables of the mantra upon the feet, knees, genitals, navel, heart, throat, face, and head, / and on the hands, on the fingers beginning with the thumbs,

294.s:
tarjanyāditadantāsu sarvamaṅguṣṭhayor nyaset /
dhyātvaivaṃ saṃharet kṣipraṃ vaddhayā śūlamudrayā //
294.d:
तर्जन्यादितदन्तासु सर्वमङ्गुष्ठयोर् न्यसेत् /
ध्यात्वैवं संहरेत् क्षिप्रं वद्धया शूलमुद्रया //
294.m: on the index fingers and the rest ending with them, one should place everything upon the two thumbs. / Having meditated thus, one should quickly remove [the poison] with the trident ritual gesture bound.

294.s:
kaniṣṭhā jyeṣṭhayā vaddhā tiśro 'nyāḥ prasṛterjavāḥ /
viṣanāśe vāmahastamanyasmin dakṣiṇaṃ karaṃ //
oṃ namo bhagavate nīlakaṇṭhāya ciḥ amalakaṇṭhāya ciḥ
sarvajñakaṇṭhāya ciḥ kṣipa oṃ svāhā
amalanīlakaṇṭhāya naikasarvaviṣāpahāya
namaste rudramanyava itisarmārjanādviṣaṃ vinaśyati na sandehaḥ
karṇajāpyā upānahāvā
:p 96
294.d:
कनिष्ठा ज्येष्ठया वद्धा तिश्रो ऽन्याः प्रसृतेर्जवाः /
विषनाशे वामहस्तमन्यस्मिन् दक्षिणं करं //
ओं नमो भगवते नीलकण्ठाय चिः अमलकण्ठाय चिः
सर्वज्ञकण्ठाय चिः क्षिप ओं स्वाहा
अमलनीलकण्ठाय नैकसर्वविषापहाय
नमस्ते रुद्रमन्यव इतिसर्मार्जनाद्विषं विनश्यति न सन्देहः
कर्णजाप्या उपानहावा
:प् 96
294.m:
The little finger is bound with the thumb, while the other three are extended straight. / In the destruction of poison, [one uses] the left hand; in other [rites], the right hand.
'Oṃ, homage to the Blessed Lord, the blue-throated one, ciḥ! To the stainless-throated one, ciḥ!'
'To the omniscient-throated one, ciḥ! Cast it off, oṃ svāhā!'
'To the stainless, blue-throated one, the remover of manifold and all poisons!'
By wiping with 'Homage to your wrath, Rudra', poison is destroyed without doubt, / or by recitation in the ear, or by shoes.

294.s:
yajedrudravidhānena nīlagrīvaṃ maheśvaram /
viṣavyādhivināśaḥ syāt kṛtvā rudravidhānakaṃ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe daṣṭacikitsā nāma
caturṇavatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha pañcanavatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
pañcāṅgarudravidhānaṃ
294.d:
यजेद्रुद्रविधानेन नीलग्रीवं महेश्वरम् /
विषव्याधिविनाशः स्यात् कृत्वा रुद्रविधानकं //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे दष्टचिकित्सा नाम
चतुर्णवत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ पञ्चनवत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
पञ्चाङ्गरुद्रविधानं
294.m:
One should worship the blue-necked Maheśvara according to the rite of Rudra. / By performing the rite of Rudra, there will be the destruction of poison and diseases.
Thus ends the two hundred and ninety-fourth chapter, entitled 'Treatment of Bites', in the Great Purāṇa of Agni.
Now the two hundred and ninety-fifth chapter.
The Fivefold Rite of Rudra

295.s:
agnir uvāca
vakṣye rudravidhānantu pañcāṅgaṃ sarvadaṃ paraṃ /
hṛdayaṃ śivasaṅkalpaḥ śivaḥ sūktantu pauruṣam //
295.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
वक्ष्ये रुद्रविधानन्तु पञ्चाङ्गं सर्वदं परं /
हृदयं शिवसङ्कल्पः शिवः सूक्तन्तु पौरुषम् //
295.m: Agni said: / I shall declare the supreme fivefold rite of Rudra that grants everything: / the heart is the Śivasaṅkalpa hymn; the Śiva hymn is the Puruṣasūkta;

295.s:
śikhābhyaḥ sambhṛtaṃ sūktamāśuḥ kavacameva ca /
śatarudriyamastrañca rudrasyāṅgāni pañca hi //
295.d:
शिखाभ्यः सम्भृतं सूक्तमाशुः कवचमेव च /
शतरुद्रियमस्त्रञ्च रुद्रस्याङ्गानि पञ्च हि //
295.m: the hymn Sambhṛta represents the crest; the Āśu hymn is the armor; / and the Śatarudriya is the weapon—these are indeed the five limbs of Rudra.

295.s:
pañcāṅgānnyasya taṃ dhyātvā japedrudrāṃstaḥ kramāt /
yajjāgrata iti sūktaṃ yadṛcaṃ mānasaṃ viduḥ //
295.d:
पञ्चाङ्गान्न्यस्य तं ध्यात्वा जपेद्रुद्रांस्तः क्रमात् /
यज्जाग्रत इति सूक्तं यदृचं मानसं विदुः //
295.m: Having deposited the five limbs and contemplated him, one should recite the Rudra hymns in due order. / The hymn 'Yajjāgrataḥ', consisting of verses, is known as the mental [hymn].

295.s:
ṛṣiḥ syācchivamaṅkalpaśchandastriṣṭuvudāhṛtaṃ /
śivaḥ sahasraśīrṣeti tasya nārāyaṇo 'pyṛṣiḥ //
295.d:
ऋषिः स्याच्छिवमङ्कल्पश्छन्दस्त्रिष्टुवुदाहृतं /
शिवः सहस्रशीर्षेति तस्य नारायणो ऽप्यृषिः //
295.m: The seer is Śivasaṅkalpa, and the meter is declared to be Triṣṭubh. / The Śiva hymn is 'Sahasraśīrṣā'; its seer is Nārāyaṇa;

295.s:
devatā puruṣo 'nuṣṭupchando jñeyañca traiṣṭubham /
abhyaśrasambhṛtaṃ sūktamṛṣiruttaragonaraḥ(1) //
295.d:
देवता पुरुषो ऽनुष्टुप्छन्दो ज्ञेयञ्च त्रैष्टुभम् /
अभ्यश्रसम्भृतं सूक्तमृषिरुत्तरगोनरः(1) //
295.m: the deity is the Puruṣa; the meter is to be known as Anuṣṭubh and Triṣṭubh. / Of the hymn 'Abhyaśrasambhṛta', the seer is Uttaragonara;

295.s:
ādyānāntimṛṇāṃ triṣṭupchando 'nuṣṭhuvdvayorapi /
:n
1 uttaragonasa iti ja.. , ṭa.. ca
:p 97
chandastriṣṭubhamantyāyāḥ puruṣo 'syāpi deṣatā //
295.d:
आद्यानान्तिमृणां त्रिष्टुप्छन्दो ऽनुष्ठुव्द्वयोरपि /
:न्
1 उत्तरगोनस इति ज.. , ट.. च
:प् 97
छन्दस्त्रिष्टुभमन्त्यायाः पुरुषो ऽस्यापि देषता //
295.m:
the meter of the first three verses is Triṣṭubh, and Anuṣṭubh for two.
[Footnote]
1. In manuscripts ja and ṭa: "uttaragonasaḥ".
[Page 97]
The meter of the final verse is Triṣṭubh, and the Puruṣa is its deity.

295.s:
āśurintro dvādaśānāṃ chandastriṣṭuvudāhṛtaṃ /
ṛṣiḥ proktaḥ pratirathaḥ sūkte saptadaśārcake //
295.d:
आशुरिन्त्रो द्वादशानां छन्दस्त्रिष्टुवुदाहृतं /
ऋषिः प्रोक्तः प्रतिरथः सूक्ते सप्तदशार्चके //
295.m: The meter of the twelve verses of the Āśu hymn is declared to be Triṣṭubh. / In the seventeen-verse hymn, Pratiratha is proclaimed as the seer.

295.s:
pṛthak pṛthak devatāḥ syuḥ puruvidaṅgadevatā /
avaśiṣṭadaivateṣu chando 'nuṣṭuvudāhṛtaṃ //
295.d:
पृथक् पृथक् देवताः स्युः पुरुविदङ्गदेवता /
अवशिष्टदैवतेषु छन्दो ऽनुष्टुवुदाहृतं //
295.m: The deities are distinct; Puruṣa is known as the deity of the limbs. / For the remaining deities, the meter is declared to be Anuṣṭubh.

295.s:
asau yamo bhavitrīndraḥ puruliṅgoktadevatāḥ(1) /
paṅkticchando 'tha marmāṇi tvapaliṅgoktadevatāḥ //
295.d:
असौ यमो भवित्रीन्द्रः पुरुलिङ्गोक्तदेवताः(1) /
पङ्क्तिच्छन्दो ऽथ मर्माणि त्वपलिङ्गोक्तदेवताः //
295.m: Yama, Bhavitṛ, and Indra are the deities mentioned in masculine gender. / The meter is Paṅkti, while the deities spoken of in neuter gender are the vital spots.

295.s:
raudrādhyāye ca sarvasminnārṣaṃ syāt parameṣvapi /
prajāpatirvā devānāṃ kutsasya tisṛṇām punaḥ //
295.d:
रौद्राध्याये च सर्वस्मिन्नार्षं स्यात् परमेष्वपि /
प्रजापतिर्वा देवानां कुत्सस्य तिसृणाम् पुनः //
295.m: In the entire chapter on Rudra, the seer is Parameṣṭhin, / or Prajāpati of the gods; but of the three verses of Kutsa,

295.s:
manodvayorumaikā syādrudro rudrāś ca devatāḥ /
ādyonuvāko 'tha pūrva ekarudrākhyadaivataḥ //
295.d:
मनोद्वयोरुमैका स्याद्रुद्रो रुद्राश् च देवताः /
आद्योनुवाको ऽथ पूर्व एकरुद्राख्यदैवतः //
295.m: of two, Manu; of one, Umā; and the Rudras are the deities. / The first section before is of the deity called the sole Rudra.

295.s:
chando gāyatryamādyāyā anuṣṭup tisṛṇāmṛcām /
tisṛṇāñca tathā paṅktiranuṣṭuvatha saṃsmṛtam //
295.d:
छन्दो गायत्र्यमाद्याया अनुष्टुप् तिसृणामृचाम् /
तिसृणाञ्च तथा पङ्क्तिरनुष्टुवथ संस्मृतम् //
295.m: The meter of the first verse is Gāyatrī; of three verses, it is Anuṣṭubh; / and of three verses, Paṅkti; then Anuṣṭubh is traditionally remembered.

295.s:
dvayoś ca jagatīchando rudrāṇāmapyaśītayaḥ /
hiraṇyavāhavastisro namo vaḥ kirikāya ca //
295.d:
द्वयोश् च जगतीछन्दो रुद्राणामप्यशीतयः /
हिरण्यवाहवस्तिस्रो नमो वः किरिकाय च //
295.m: And of two, the meter is Jagatī, as well as of the eighties of the Rudras. / The three verses beginning with 'Hiraṇyabāhave' and 'Namo vaḥ kirikebhyaḥ',

295.s:
pañcarco rudradevāḥ syurmantre rudrānuvākakaḥ(2) /
viṃśake rudradevāstāḥ prathamā vṛhatī smṛtā //
295.d:
पञ्चर्चो रुद्रदेवाः स्युर्मन्त्रे रुद्रानुवाककः(2) /
विंशके रुद्रदेवास्ताः प्रथमा वृहती स्मृता //
295.m: the five verses, have the Rudras as deities in the section of Rudra mantras. / In the twentieth section, they have the Rudras as deities; the first is considered Bṛhatī,

295.s:
ṛgdvitīyā trijagatī triṣṭuveva ca /
anuṣṭubho yajustisra āryādijñaḥ susiddhibhāk //
295.d:
ऋग्द्वितीया त्रिजगती त्रिष्टुवेव च /
अनुष्टुभो यजुस्तिस्र आर्यादिज्ञः सुसिद्धिभाक् //
295.m: the second verse is Triṣṭubh and Jagatī; / the three Yajus verses are Anuṣṭubh. Knowing the seer and the rest, one attains true success.

295.s:
trailokyamohanenāpi viṣavyādhyarimardanaṃ(3) /

नमः /
अगुष्टुभं नृसिंहेन विषव्याधिविनाशनं //
295.m:
Also by means of the Trailokyamohana mantra, there is the crushing of poison, disease, and enemies:
[Footnote]
1. In manuscript kha: "bhavitrīti triṣṭup liṅgoktadevatā".
2. In manuscripts ja and ṭa: "rudrātmavācakaḥ".
3. In manuscript ja: "viṣavyādhivimardanam".
[Page 98]
'Iṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ hrauṃ hūṃ, to Viṣṇu, the deluder of the three worlds,'
'homage!'
The Anuṣṭubh verse dedicated to Nṛsiṃha destroys poison and disease:

295.s:
oṃ iṃ iṃ(2) ugravīraṃ maṃhāviṣṇuṃ jvalantaṃsarvatomukhaṃ /
nṛsiṃhaṃ bhīṣaṇaṃ mṛtyumṛtyumnamāmyahaṃ //
295.d:
ओं इं इं(2) उग्रवीरं मंहाविष्णुं ज्वलन्तंसर्वतोमुखं /
नृसिंहं भीषणं मृत्युमृत्युम्नमाम्यहं //
295.m: 'Oṃ iṃ iṃ, I bow to the ferocious hero, the Great Viṣṇu, blazing, facing in all directions, Nṛsiṃha, the terrifying one, the death of Death!'

295.s:
ayameva tu pañcāṅgo mantraḥ sarvārthasādhakaḥ /
dvādaśāṣṭākṣarau mantrau viṣavyādhivimardanau //
295.d:
अयमेव तु पञ्चाङ्गो मन्त्रः सर्वार्थसाधकः /
द्वादशाष्टाक्षरौ मन्त्रौ विषव्याधिविमर्दनौ //
295.m: This very five-limbed mantra accomplishes all purposes. / The twelve-syllable and eight-syllable mantras crush poison and disease.

kubjikā tripurā gaurī candrikā(3) viṣahāriṇī /

प्रसादमन्त्रो विषहृदायुरारोग्यवर्धनः //
सौरो विनायकस्तद्वद्रुद्रमन्त्राः सदाखिलाः //

ज्वलितपरशुपाणये च / नमो भगवते पक्षिरुद्राय दष्टकं
उत्थपय 2 दष्टकं कम्पय 2 जल्पय 2 सर्पदष्टमुत्थापय लल 2
