295.m:
Kubjikā, Tripurā, Gaurī, Candrikā remove poison. / The Prasāda mantra removes poison and increases life and health; / likewise the solar mantra, the mantra of Vināyaka, and constantly all mantras of Rudra.
Thus ends the two hundred and ninety-fifth chapter, entitled 'The Fivefold Rite of Rudra', in the Great Purāṇa of Agni.
Now the two hundred and ninety-sixth chapter.
Mantras and medicines that remove poison.
Agni said:
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed Rudra! Cut, cut the poison!
And to the one with a blazing battle-axe in hand! Homage to the Blessed Pakṣirudra! Raise the bitten one, raise him! Shake the bitten one, shake him! Make him speak, make him speak! Raise the snake-bitten one! Play, play! / Bind, bind! Guard, guard! O excellent Rudra, go, go! Slay, slay! Break, break! Terrify, terrify! With your fist destroy the poison! Ṭha ṭha!
[Footnote]
1. "oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūm" in ms. ña..
2. "oṃ hauṃ haṃ" in ms. ja..
3. "caṇḍikā" in ms. ña.. / p. 99
Verily, by [the grace of] Pakṣirudra, poison is destroyed through chanting this mantra.

295.s:
oṃ namo bhagavate rudra nāśaya viṣaṃ sthāvarajaṅgamaṃ
kṛtrimākṛtrimaviṣamupaviṣaṃ nāśaya nānāviṣaṃ
daṣṭakaviṣaṃ nāśaya dhama 2 dama 2 vama 2
meghāndhakāradhārākarṣanirviṣayībhava saṃhara 2 gaccha 2
āveśaya 2 viṣotthāpanarūpaṃ mantrāntādviṣadhāraṇaṃ oṃ
kṣipa oṃ kṣipa svāhā
oṃ hrīṃ khīṃ saḥ ṭhandrauṃ hrīṃ ṭhaḥ
295.d:
ओं नमो भगवते रुद्र नाशय विषं स्थावरजङ्गमं
कृत्रिमाकृत्रिमविषमुपविषं नाशय नानाविषं
दष्टकविषं नाशय धम 2 दम 2 वम 2
मेघान्धकारधाराकर्षनिर्विषयीभव संहर 2 गच्छ 2
आवेशय 2 विषोत्थापनरूपं मन्त्रान्ताद्विषधारणं ओं
क्षिप ओं क्षिप स्वाहा
ओं ह्रीं खीं सः ठन्द्रौं ह्रीं ठः
295.m:
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed Rudra! Destroy the poison, immobile and mobile, / artificial and natural poison, and secondary poison! Destroy the various poisons! / Destroy the poison of the bitten one! Blow, blow! Subdue, subdue! Vomit, vomit! / Pulling the streams [of rain] from the darkness of clouds, become free of poison! Destroy, destroy! Go, go! / Possess, possess! With the extraction of poison as its nature, ending with the mantra, holding the poison: Oṃ, cast it away! Oṃ, cast it away! Svāhā!
Oṃ hrīṃ khīṃ saḥ ṭhandrauṃ hrīṃ ṭhaḥ.

296.m: Mastered by means of recitation and the like, it perpetually binds serpents. // 1

296.s:
ekadvitricaturvījaḥ kṛṣṇacakrāṅgapañcakaḥ /
gopījanavallabhāya svāhā sarvārthasādhakaḥ //
oṃ namo bhagavate rudrāya pretādhipataye guttva 2(1) garja 2 bhrāmaya 2
muñca 2 muhya 2 kaṭa 2 āviśa 2 suvarṇapataṅga rudro jñāpayati ṭha
2
296.d:
एकद्वित्रिचतुर्वीजः कृष्णचक्राङ्गपञ्चकः /
गोपीजनवल्लभाय स्वाहा सर्वार्थसाधकः //
ओं नमो भगवते रुद्राय प्रेताधिपतये गुत्त्व 2(1) गर्ज 2 भ्रामय 2
मुञ्च 2 मुह्य 2 कट 2 आविश 2 सुवर्णपतङ्ग रुद्रो ज्ञापयति ठ
2
296.m:
Possessing one, two, three, or four seed-syllables, and the five limbs of Kṛṣṇa's disc, / "To the Beloved of the cowherd maidens, svāhā!" accomplishes all objectives.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed Rudra, the lord of the spirits! Guttva, guttva! Roar, roar! Whirl, whirl! / Release, release! Bewilder, bewilder! Burn, burn! Enter, enter, O golden bird! Rudra commands! Ṭha ṭha!

296.s:
pātālakṣobhamantroyaṃ mantraṇādviṣanāśanaḥ /
daṃśakāhidaṃśe sadyo daṣṭaḥ kāṣṭhaśilādinā //
296.d:
पातालक्षोभमन्त्रोयं मन्त्रणाद्विषनाशनः /
दंशकाहिदंशे सद्यो दष्टः काष्ठशिलादिना //
296.m: This mantra that agitates the underworld destroys poison through chanting. / When one is bitten by a biting snake, the one immediately bitten with wood, stone, or the like
for the pacification of the poison, [rubbing] the bite from the body with blazing red lotus and the like. / Śirīṣa seeds and flowers, calotropis milk, and the three pungents,

296.s:
viṣaṃ vināśayet pānalepanenāñjanādinā /
śirīṣapuśpasya rasabhāvitaṃ maricaṃ sitaṃ //
296.d:
विषं विनाशयेत् पानलेपनेनाञ्जनादिना /
शिरीषपुश्पस्य रसभावितं मरिचं सितं //
296.m: destroys poison through drinking, smearing, and applying as collyrium. / White pepper soaked in the juice of śirīṣa flowers,

296.s:
pānanasyāñjanādyaiś ca viṣaṃ hanyānna saṃśayaḥ /
koṣātakīvacāhiṅguśirīśārkapayoyutaṃ //
:n
1 gulu 2 iti ña..
2 jvālako kaladālineti kha..
:p 100
296.d:
पाननस्याञ्जनाद्यैश् च विषं हन्यान्न संशयः /
कोषातकीवचाहिङ्गुशिरीशार्कपयोयुतं //
:न्
1 गुलु 2 इति ञ..
2 ज्वालको कलदालिनेति ख..
:प् 100
296.m:
through drinking, errhine, collyrium, and the like, undoubtedly destroys poison. / Koṣātakī, sweet flag, asafoetida, śirīṣa, mixed with calotropis milk,
[Footnote]
1. "gulu 2" in ms. ña..
2. "jvālako kaladālinā" in ms. kha.. / p. 100

296.s:
kuṭutrayaṃ sameṣāmbho harennasyādinā viṣaṃ /
rāmaṭhekṣvākusarvāṅgacūrṇaṃ nasyādviṣāpahaṃ //
296.d:
कुटुत्रयं समेषाम्भो हरेन्नस्यादिना विषं /
रामठेक्ष्वाकुसर्वाङ्गचूर्णं नस्याद्विषापहं //
296.m: [and] the three pungents in equal water, removes poison through errhine and the like. / Powder of all parts of asafoetida and wild bitter gourd dispels poison through errhine.

296.s:
indrabalāgnikandroṇaṃ tulasī devikā sahā /
tadrasāktaṃ trikaṭukaṃ cūrṇambhakṣyayiṣāpahaṃ /
pañcāṅgaṃ kṛṣṇapañcabhyāṃ śirīṣasya viṣāpahaṃ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpuraṇe viṣahṛnmantrauṣadhaṃ nāma
ṣannavatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:ś atha saptanavatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
gonasādicikitsā
agnirucāca
296.d:
इन्द्रबलाग्निकन्द्रोणं तुलसी देविका सहा /
तद्रसाक्तं त्रिकटुकं चूर्णम्भक्ष्ययिषापहं /
पञ्चाङ्गं कृष्णपञ्चभ्यां शिरीषस्य विषापहं //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुरणे विषहृन्मन्त्रौषधं नाम
षन्नवत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
:श् अथ सप्तनवत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
गोनसादिचिकित्सा
अग्निरुचाच
296.m:
Indrabalā, agnikā, droṇapuṣpī, tulasī, devikā, and sahā: / the three pungents smeared with their juice and powdered, when eaten, dispels poison. / The five parts of śirīṣa gathered on the dark fifth lunar day dispels poison.
Thus ends the two hundred and ninety-sixth chapter, entitled "Mantras and Medicines that Remove Poison," in the great Agni Purāṇa.
Now begins the two hundred and ninety-seventh chapter.
Treatment of viper bites and others.
Agni said:

297.s:
gonasādicikitsāñca vaśiṣṭha śṛṇu vacmi te /
hrīṃ hrīṃ amalapakṣi svāhā
tāmbūlakhādanānmantrī harenmaṇḍalino viṣaṃ //
297.d:
गोनसादिचिकित्साञ्च वशिष्ठ शृणु वच्मि ते /
ह्रीं ह्रीं अमलपक्षि स्वाहा
ताम्बूलखादनान्मन्त्री हरेन्मण्डलिनो विषं //
297.m:
Listen, O Vasiṣṭha, I will speak to you of the treatment for viper [bites] and others:
"Hrīṃ hrīṃ to the pure-winged bird, svāhā!"
By chewing betel, the practitioner of mantras removes the poison of the Russell's viper.

297.s:
laśunaṃ rāmaṭhaphalaṃ kuṣṭhāgnivyoṣakaṃ viṣe /
snuhīkṣīraṃ gavyaghṛtaṃ pakṣaṃ pītvāhije viṣe //
297.d:
लशुनं रामठफलं कुष्ठाग्निव्योषकं विषे /
स्नुहीक्षीरं गव्यघृतं पक्षं पीत्वाहिजे विषे //
297.m: Garlic, asafoetida resin, costus, leadwort, and the three pungents in case of poison; / after drinking spurge milk, cow's ghee, [and] the decoction for poison born of serpents.

297.s:
atha rājiladaṣṭe ca peyā kṛṣṇā samaindhavā /
ājyakṣaudraśakṛttoyaṃ purītatyā viṣāpahaṃ //
297.d:
अथ राजिलदष्टे च पेया कृष्णा समैन्धवा /
आज्यक्षौद्रशकृत्तोयं पुरीतत्या विषापहं //
297.m: Now, when bitten by a striped krait, long pepper with rock salt should be drunk. / Ghee, honey, dung-water, [and] purītati dispel poison.

297.s:
sakṛṣṇākhaṇḍadugdhājyaṃ pātavyantena mākṣikaṃ /
vyoṣaṃ picchaṃ viḍālāsthi nakulāṅgaruhaiḥ samaiḥ //
297.d:
सकृष्णाखण्डदुग्धाज्यं पातव्यन्तेन माक्षिकं /
व्योषं पिच्छं विडालास्थि नकुलाङ्गरुहैः समैः //
297.m: Milk and ghee with long pepper sugar, and honey should be drunk by him. / The three pungents, peacock feathers, cat's bone, [and] mongoose hair in equal parts,

297.s:
cūrṇitair meṣadugdhāktair dhūpaḥ sarvaviṣāpahaḥ /
:p 101
romanirguṇḍikākokavarṇair vā laśunaṃ samaṃ //
297.d:
चूर्णितैर् मेषदुग्धाक्तैर् धूपः सर्वविषापहः /
:प् 101
रोमनिर्गुण्डिकाकोकवर्णैर् वा लशुनं समं //
297.m:
powdered and moistened with sheep's milk, make an incense that dispels all poisons.
p. 101
Or garlic equal in measure to the hairs of nirguṇḍī and ruddy goose feathers.

297.s:
munipatraiḥ kṛtasvedaṃ daṣṭaṃ kāñcikapācitaiḥ /
mūṣikāḥ ṣoḍaśa proktā rasaṅkārpāsajampivet //
297.d:
मुनिपत्रैः कृतस्वेदं दष्टं काञ्चिकपाचितैः /
मूषिकाः षोडश प्रोक्ता रसङ्कार्पासजम्पिवेत् //
297.m: One should foment the bite with agati leaves cooked in fermented sour gruel. / Sixteen mice are proclaimed; one should drink the juice born of cotton

297.s:
satailaṃ mūṣikārtighnaṃ phalinīkusumantathā /
sanāgaraguḍambhakṣyaṃ tadviṣārocakāpahaṃ //
297.d:
सतैलं मूषिकार्तिघ्नं फलिनीकुसुमन्तथा /
सनागरगुडम्भक्ष्यं तद्विषारोचकापहं //
297.m: mixed with oil, which destroys the affliction from mice. Likewise, the flower of priyaṅgu / eaten with ginger and jaggery dispels the poison and loss of appetite caused by them.

297.s:
cikitsā viṃṣatirbhūtā lūtāviṣaharo gaṇaḥ /
padmakaṃ pāṭalī kuṣṭhaṃ natamūśīracandanaṃ //
297.d:
चिकित्सा विंषतिर्भूता लूताविषहरो गणः /
पद्मकं पाटली कुष्ठं नतमूशीरचन्दनं //
297.m: The treatments are twenty in number. The group that destroys spider venom [consists of]: / padmaka, trumpet flower, costus, Indian valerian, vetiver, sandalwood,

297.s:
nirguṇḍī śārivā śelu lūtārtaṃ secayejjalaiḥ /
guñjānirguṇḍikaṅkolaparṇaṃ śuṇṭhī niśādvayaṃ //
297.d:
निर्गुण्डी शारिवा शेलु लूतार्तं सेचयेज्जलैः /
गुञ्जानिर्गुण्डिकङ्कोलपर्णं शुण्ठी निशाद्वयं //
297.m: nirguṇḍī, Indian sarsaparilla, [and] cordia: one should sprinkle the person afflicted by spider [venom] with their decoction. / Guñjā, nirguṇḍī, piper cubeba leaves, dry ginger, the two turmerics,

297.s:
karañjāsthi ca tatpaṅkaiḥ(1) vṛścikārtiharaṃ śṛṇu /
mañjiṣṭhā candanaṃ vyoṣapuṣpaṃ śirīṣakaumudaṃ //
297.d:
करञ्जास्थि च तत्पङ्कैः(1) वृश्चिकार्तिहरं शृणु /
मञ्जिष्ठा चन्दनं व्योषपुष्पं शिरीषकौमुदं //
297.m: and the seed of Indian beech; listen to what removes the suffering of scorpion stings through their pastes: / Indian madder, sandalwood, the three pungents, [and] śirīṣa flowers.

297.s:
saṃyojyāś caturo yogā lepādau vṛścikāpahāḥ /
oṃ namo bhagavate rudrāya civi 2(2) chinda 2 kiri 2 bhinda 2 khaḍge na chedaya
2 śūlena bhedaya 2 cakreṇa dāraya 2 oṃ hrūṃ phaṭ
mantreṇa mantrito deyo gardhabhādīnnikṛntati //
297.d:
संयोज्याश् चतुरो योगा लेपादौ वृश्चिकापहाः /
ओं नमो भगवते रुद्राय चिवि 2(2) छिन्द 2 किरि 2 भिन्द 2 खड्गे न छेदय
2 शूलेन भेदय 2 चक्रेण दारय 2 ओं ह्रूं फट्
मन्त्रेण मन्त्रितो देयो गर्धभादीन्निकृन्तति //
297.m:
When combined, the four formulations dispel [the sting of] scorpions by smearing and the like.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed Rudra! Civi, civi! Cut, cut! Kiri, kiri! Pierce, pierce! With the sword, strike, strike! With the trident, pierce, pierce! With the discus, tear apart, tear apart! Oṃ hrūṃ phaṭ!
Consecrated with this mantra, [the remedy] given cuts down the poison of asses and others.

297.s:
triphalośīramustāmbumāṃsīpadmakacandanaṃ /
ajākṣīreṇa pānādergardhabhāderviṣaṃ haret //
297.d:
त्रिफलोशीरमुस्ताम्बुमांसीपद्मकचन्दनं /
अजाक्षीरेण पानादेर्गर्धभादेर्विषं हरेत् //
297.m: The three myrobalans, vetiver, nut grass water, spikenard, padmaka, and sandalwood, / taken through drinking and the like with goat's milk, removes the poison of asses and others.

297.s:
haret śirīṣapañcāṅgaṃ vyoṣaṃ śatapadīviṣaṃ /
sakandharaṃ śirīṣāsthi haredundūrajaṃ viṣaṃ //
297.d:
हरेत् शिरीषपञ्चाङ्गं व्योषं शतपदीविषं /
सकन्धरं शिरीषास्थि हरेदुन्दूरजं विषं //
297.m: The five parts of śirīṣa [and] the three pungents remove centipede venom. / Śirīṣa seeds with ginger remove rat-born poison.

297.s:
vyoṣaṃ sasarpiḥ piṇḍītamūlamasya viṣaṃ haret /
:n
1 tatpakṣair iti ja.. , ña.. , ṭa.. ca
2 ciri 2 iti ja..
:p 102
kṣāravyoṣavacāḍiṅguviḍaṅgaṃ saindhavannataṃ //
297.d:
व्योषं ससर्पिः पिण्डीतमूलमस्य विषं हरेत् /
:न्
1 तत्पक्षैर् इति ज.. , ञ.. , ट.. च
2 चिरि 2 इति ज..
:प् 102
क्षारव्योषवचाडिङ्गुविडङ्गं सैन्धवन्नतं //
297.m:
The three pungents with ghee and the root of piṇḍīta remove its poison.
[Footnote]
1. "tatpakṣair" in mss. ja.., ña.., and ṭa..
2. "ciri 2" in ms. ja.. / p. 102
Alkali, the three pungents, sweet flag, asafoetida, false black pepper, rock salt, Indian valerian,

297.s:
ambaṣṭhātibalākuṣṭhaṃ sarvakīṭaviṣaṃ haret /
yaṣṭivyoṣaguḍakṣīrayogaḥ(1) śūno viṣāpahaḥ //
297.d:
अम्बष्ठातिबलाकुष्ठं सर्वकीटविषं हरेत् /
यष्टिव्योषगुडक्षीरयोगः(1) शूनो विषापहः //
297.m: ambaṣṭhā, country mallow, and costus remove all insect poison. / A combination of liquorice, the three pungents, jaggery, and milk dispels the poison of a dog.

297.s:
oṃ subhadrāyai namaḥ oṃ suprabhāyai namaḥ /
yānyauṣadhāni gṛhyante vidhānena vinā janaiḥ //
297.d:
ओं सुभद्रायै नमः ओं सुप्रभायै नमः /
यान्यौषधानि गृह्यन्ते विधानेन विना जनैः //
297.m: Oṃ, homage to Subhadrā! Oṃ, homage to Suprabhā! / Whatever medicinal herbs are gathered by people without ritual injunction,

297.s:
teṣāṃ vījantvyā grāhyamiti brahmābravīcca tām /
tāmpraṇamyauṣadhīmpaścāt yavān prakṣipya muṣṭinā //
297.d:
तेषां वीजन्त्व्या ग्राह्यमिति ब्रह्माब्रवीच्च ताम् /
ताम्प्रणम्यौषधीम्पश्चात् यवान् प्रक्षिप्य मुष्टिना //
297.m: their seed should be taken by you—thus Brahmā spoke to her. / Having bowed to that medicinal herb, and then scattering barley with a fist,

297.s:
daśa japtvā mantramidaṃ namaskuryāttadauṣadhaṃ /
tvāmuddharāmyūrdhvanetrāmanenaiva ca bhakṣayet //
297.d:
दश जप्त्वा मन्त्रमिदं नमस्कुर्यात्तदौषधं /
त्वामुद्धराम्यूर्ध्वनेत्रामनेनैव च भक्षयेत् //
297.m: having recited this mantra ten times, one should bow to that herb: / "I pull you up with eyes turned upward," and with this alone one should consume it:

297.s:
namaḥ puruṣasiṃhāya namo gopālakāya ca /
ātmanaivābhijānāti raṇe kṛṣṇaparājayaṃ //
297.d:
नमः पुरुषसिंहाय नमो गोपालकाय च /
आत्मनैवाभिजानाति रणे कृष्णपराजयं //
297.m: "Homage to the Lion among Men, and homage to the Cowherd! / He knows by Himself Kṛṣṇa's invincibility in battle.

297.s:
etena satyavākyena agado me 'stu sidhyatu /
namo vaidūryamāte tanna 2 rakṣa māṃ sarvaviṣebhyo gauri gāndhāri
cāṇḍāli mātaṅgini svāhā harimāye
auṣadhādau prayoktavyo mantro 'yaṃ sthāvare viṣe //
297.d:
एतेन सत्यवाक्येन अगदो मे ऽस्तु सिध्यतु /
नमो वैदूर्यमाते तन्न 2 रक्ष मां सर्वविषेभ्यो गौरि गान्धारि
चाण्डालि मातङ्गिनि स्वाहा हरिमाये
औषधादौ प्रयोक्तव्यो मन्त्रो ऽयं स्थावरे विषे //
297.m:
By this statement of truth, let my antidote be accomplished!"
Homage to the Mother of Lapis Lazuli! Tanna, tanna! Protect me from all poisons, O Gaurī, Gāndhārī, Cāṇḍālī, Mātaṅginī! Svāhā! O Harimāyā!
This mantra is to be employed in medicines and the like in the case of stationary poison.

297.s:
bhuktamātre sthite jvāle padmaṃ śītāmbusevitaṃ /
pāyayetsaghṛtaṃ kṣaudraṃ viṣañcettadanantaraṃ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe gonasādicikitsā nāma
saptanavatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:n
1 ṣaṣṭivyoṣaguḍakṣīrayoga iti ka.. , ja.. , ña.. , ṭa ca
:p 103
:ś athāṣṭanavatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
balagrahaharabālatantram
297.d:
भुक्तमात्रे स्थिते ज्वाले पद्मं शीताम्बुसेवितं /
पाययेत्सघृतं क्षौद्रं विषञ्चेत्तदनन्तरं //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे गोनसादिचिकित्सा नाम
सप्तनवत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
:न्
1 षष्टिव्योषगुडक्षीरयोग इति क.. , ज.. , ञ.. , ट च
:प् 103
:श् अथाष्टनवत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
बलग्रहहरबालतन्त्रम्
297.m:
When a burning sensation remains immediately after eating, [the root of] lotus treated with cold water / should be given to drink with ghee and honey, if poison is present immediately thereafter.
Thus ends the two hundred and ninety-seventh chapter, entitled “Treatment for Bites of the Large Pit Viper and Others,” in the great Agni Purāṇa.
[Footnote]
1. “ṣaṣṭivyoṣaguḍakṣīrayogaḥ” in manuscripts ka, ja, ña, and ṭa.
Now begins the two hundred and ninety-eighth chapter.
The pediatric tantra for subduing demonic seizures in children.

298.s:
agnir uvāca
bālatantraṃ pravakṣyāmi bālādigrahamardanaṃ /
atha jātadine vatsaṃ grahī gṛhṇāti pāpinī //
298.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
बालतन्त्रं प्रवक्ष्यामि बालादिग्रहमर्दनं /
अथ जातदिने वत्सं ग्रही गृह्णाति पापिनी //
298.m: Agni said: / I shall declare the pediatric tantra that crushes seizures affecting children and others. / Now, on the day of birth, a sinful female seizing spirit seizes the infant.

298.s:
gātrodvego nirāhāro nānāgrīvāvivartanaṃ /
tacceṣṭitamidaṃ tasyānmātṝṇāñca balaṃ haret //
298.d:
गात्रोद्वेगो निराहारो नानाग्रीवाविवर्तनं /
तच्चेष्टितमिदं तस्यान्मातॄणाञ्च बलं हरेत् //
298.m: Agitation of the limbs, refusal of food, and various twistings of the neck / are her symptomatic actions; one should offer a sacrificial offering to the Mothers.

298.s:
satsyamāṃsasurābhakṣyagandhasragdhūpadīpakaiḥ /
limpecca dhātakīlodhramañjiṣṭhātālacandanaiḥ //
298.d:
सत्स्यमांससुराभक्ष्यगन्धस्रग्धूपदीपकैः /
लिम्पेच्च धातकीलोध्रमञ्जिष्ठातालचन्दनैः //
298.m: With fish, meat, liquor, edible offerings, fragrant garlands, incense, and lamps [one should make offerings], / and anoint [the child] with dhātakī, lodhra, mañjiṣṭhā, tāla, and sandalwood.

298.s:
mahiṣākṣeṇa dhūpaś ca dvirātre bhauṣaṇī grahī /
tacceṣṭā kāsaniśvāsau gātrasaṅkocanaṃ muhuḥ //
298.d:
महिषाक्षेण धूपश् च द्विरात्रे भौषणी ग्रही /
तच्चेष्टा कासनिश्वासौ गात्रसङ्कोचनं मुहुः //
298.m: Incense [should be made] with bdellium. On the second night, the seizing spirit is Bhauṣaṇī; / her symptoms are cough, sighs, and constant flexing of the limbs.

298.s:
ājamūtrair lipet kṛṣṇāsevyāpāmārgacandanaiḥ /
gośṛṅgadantakeśaiś ca dhūpayet pūrvavadbaliḥ //
298.d:
आजमूत्रैर् लिपेत् कृष्णासेव्यापामार्गचन्दनैः /
गोशृङ्गदन्तकेशैश् च धूपयेत् पूर्ववद्बलिः //
298.m: One should anoint [the infant] with goat's urine mixed with pippalī, uśīra, apāmārga, and sandalwood, / fumigate with cow-horn, cow-teeth, and cow-hair, and offer the sacrificial offering as before.

298.s:
grahī trirātre ghaṇṭhālī tacceṣṭā krandanaṃ muhuḥ /
jṛmbhaṇaṃ svanitantrāso gātrodvegamarocanaṃ //
298.d:
ग्रही त्रिरात्रे घण्ठाली तच्चेष्टा क्रन्दनं मुहुः /
जृम्भणं स्वनितन्त्रासो गात्रोद्वेगमरोचनं //
298.m: On the third night the seizing spirit is Ghaṇṭālī; her symptoms are frequent crying, / yawning, sound-producing terror, agitation of the limbs, and loss of appetite.

298.s:
keśarāñjanagohastidantaṃ sājapayo lipet /
nakharājībilvadalair dhūpayecca baliṃ haret //
298.d:
केशराञ्जनगोहस्तिदन्तं साजपयो लिपेत् /
नखराजीबिल्वदलैर् धूपयेच्च बलिं हरेत् //
298.m: One should anoint [the infant] with saffron, collyrium, and teeth of cows and elephants mixed with goat's milk; / one should fumigate with tiger-claws and bilva leaves, and offer the sacrificial offering.

298.s:
grahī caturthī kākolī gātrodvegaprarocanaṃ /
phenodgāro diśo dṛṣṭiḥ kulmāṣaiḥ sāsavair baliḥ //
298.d:
ग्रही चतुर्थी काकोली गात्रोद्वेगप्ररोचनं /
फेनोद्गारो दिशो दृष्टिः कुल्माषैः सासवैर् बलिः //
298.m: The fourth seizing spirit is Kākolī; [the symptoms are] agitation of the limbs, vomiting, / spitting of froth, and staring into space. The sacrificial offering is made with boiled coarse grain mixed with liquor.

298.s:
gajadantāhinirmokavājimūtrapralepanaṃ /
sarājīnimbapatreṇa dhūtakeśena chūpayet //
298.d:
गजदन्ताहिनिर्मोकवाजिमूत्रप्रलेपनं /
सराजीनिम्बपत्रेण धूतकेशेन छूपयेत् //
298.m: Anointment is done with elephant tusk, cast snake-skin, and horse urine; / one should fumigate with mustard seed, neem leaves, and washed hair.

298.s:
haṃsādhikā pañcamī syājjṛmbhāśvāsordhadhāriṇī /
:p 104
muṣṭibandhaś ca tacceṣṭā baliṃ matsyādinā haret //
298.d:
हंसाधिका पञ्चमी स्याज्जृम्भाश्वासोर्धधारिणी /
:प् 104
मुष्टिबन्धश् च तच्चेष्टा बलिं मत्स्यादिना हरेत् //

298.s:
meṣaśṛṅgabalālodhraśilātālaiḥ śiśuṃ lipet /
phaṭkārī tu grahī ṣaṣṭhī bhayamohaprarodanaṃ //
298.d:
मेषशृङ्गबलालोध्रशिलातालैः शिशुं लिपेत् /
फट्कारी तु ग्रही षष्ठी भयमोहप्ररोदनं //
298.m: One should anoint the child with meṣaśṛṅgī, balā, lodhra, realgar, and orpiment. / The sixth seizing spirit is Phaṭkārī, causing fear, stupor, and weeping.

298.s:
nirāhāro 'ṅgavikṣepo harenmatsyādinā baliṃ /
rājīguggulukuṣṭhebhadantādyair dhūpalepanaiḥ //
298.d:
निराहारो ऽङ्गविक्षेपो हरेन्मत्स्यादिना बलिं /
राजीगुग्गुलुकुष्ठेभदन्ताद्यैर् धूपलेपनैः //
298.m: Refusal of food and convulsive twitching of the limbs [occur]; one should offer a sacrificial offering with fish and the like, / along with incense and unguents made with mustard, guggulu, kuṣṭha, elephant tusk, and the like.

298.s:
saptame muktakeśyārtaḥ pūtigandho vijṛmbhaṇaṃ /
sādaḥ prarodanaṅkāso dhūpo vyāghranakhair lipet //
298.d:
सप्तमे मुक्तकेश्यार्तः पूतिगन्धो विजृम्भणं /
सादः प्ररोदनङ्कासो धूपो व्याघ्रनखैर् लिपेत् //
298.m: On the seventh [day], afflicted by Muktakeśī, [the child exhibits] foul odor, excessive yawning, / exhaustion, weeping, and cough; fumigation is done with tiger-claws, and one should anoint [the infant].

298.s:
vacāgomayagomūtraiḥ śrīdaṇḍī cāṣṭame grahī /
diśo nirīkṣaṇaṃ jihvācālanaṅkāsarodanaṃ //
298.d:
वचागोमयगोमूत्रैः श्रीदण्डी चाष्टमे ग्रही /
दिशो निरीक्षणं जिह्वाचालनङ्कासरोदनं //
298.m: With sweet flag, cow dung, and cow urine [one makes an unguent]. On the eighth [day] the seizing spirit is Śrīdaṇḍī; / staring in all directions, darting of the tongue, coughing, and weeping [are her signs].

298.s:
baliḥ pūrvaiva matsyādyair dhūpalepe ca(1) hiṅgulā /
vacāsiddharthalaśunaiścordhvagrāhī mahāgrahī //
298.d:
बलिः पूर्वैव मत्स्याद्यैर् धूपलेपे च(1) हिङ्गुला /
वचासिद्धर्थलशुनैश्चोर्ध्वग्राही महाग्रही //
298.m: The sacrificial offering is just as before with fish and the like. For the fumigation and unguent: cinnabar, / sweet flag, white mustard, and garlic. The great seizing spirit is Ūrdhvagrāhī.

298.s:
udvejanordhvaniḥśvāsaḥ svamuṣṭidvayakhādanaṃ /
raktacandanakuṣṭhādyair dhūpayellepayecchiśuṃ //
298.d:
उद्वेजनोर्ध्वनिःश्वासः स्वमुष्टिद्वयखादनं /
रक्तचन्दनकुष्ठाद्यैर् धूपयेल्लेपयेच्छिशुं //
298.m: Agitation, upward sighing, and biting one's own two fists [are the symptoms]; / one should fumigate and anoint the child with red sandalwood, kuṣṭha, and the like.

298.s:
kapiromanakhair dhūpo daśamī rodanī grahī /
tacceṣṭā rodanaṃ śaśvat sugandho nīlavarṇatā //
298.d:
कपिरोमनखैर् धूपो दशमी रोदनी ग्रही /
तच्चेष्टा रोदनं शश्वत् सुगन्धो नीलवर्णता //
298.m: Fumigation is done with monkey hair and nails. On the tenth [day] the seizing spirit is Rodanī; / her symptoms are continual weeping, a fragrant scent, and bluish complexion.

298.s:
dhūpo nimbena bhūtograrājīsarjarasair lipet /
baliṃ vahirharellājakulmāṣakavakodanam(2) //
298.d:
धूपो निम्बेन भूतोग्रराजीसर्जरसैर् लिपेत् /
बलिं वहिर्हरेल्लाजकुल्माषकवकोदनम्(2) //
298.m: Fumigation is with neem; one should anoint with bhūtakeśī, ugrā, mustard, and sāla resin. / One should offer the sacrificial offering outside, consisting of parched grain, boiled coarse grain, and curds mixed with rice.

298.s:
yāvattrayodaśāhaṃ syādevaṃ dhūpādikā kriyā /
gṛhnāti māsikaṃ vatsaṃ pūtanāsaṅkulī grahī //
298.d:
यावत्त्रयोदशाहं स्यादेवं धूपादिका क्रिया /
गृह्नाति मासिकं वत्सं पूतनासङ्कुली ग्रही //
298.m: Such rites of fumigation and the rest should continue up to the thirteenth day. / The seizing spirit Pūtanāsaṅkulī seizes the one-month-old infant.

298.s:
kākavadrodanaṃ śvāso mūtragandho 'kṣimīlanaṃ /
gomūtrasnapanaṃ tasya godantena ca dhūpanam //
:n
1 dhūpadīpe ceti ṭa..
2 karakodanamiti kha..
:p 105
298.d:
काकवद्रोदनं श्वासो मूत्रगन्धो ऽक्षिमीलनं /
गोमूत्रस्नपनं तस्य गोदन्तेन च धूपनम् //
:न्
1 धूपदीपे चेति ट..
2 करकोदनमिति ख..
:प् 105
298.m:
Crying like a crow, gasping, the smell of urine, and closing of the eyes [are her signs]; / bathing him in cow urine and fumigating him with cow tooth [is the cure].
[Footnote]
1. “dhūpadīpe ca” in manuscript ṭa.
2. “karakodanam” in manuscript kha.

298.s:
pītavastraṃ dadedraktasraggandhau tailadīpakaḥ /
trividhaṃ pāyasammadyaṃ tilamāsañcaturvidham //
298.d:
पीतवस्त्रं ददेद्रक्तस्रग्गन्धौ तैलदीपकः /
त्रिविधं पायसम्मद्यं तिलमासञ्चतुर्विधम् //
298.m: One should offer yellow cloth, red garlands and scents, an oil lamp, / three kinds of milk-rice, liquor, and sesame with black gram, of four kinds.

298.s:
karañjādho yamadiśi saptāhaṃ tair baliṃ haret /
dvimāsikañca mukuṭā vapuḥ śītañca śītalaṃ //
298.d:
करञ्जाधो यमदिशि सप्ताहं तैर् बलिं हरेत् /
द्विमासिकञ्च मुकुटा वपुः शीतञ्च शीतलं //
298.m: Beneath a karañja tree in the southern quarter, one should present the sacrificial offering with these for seven days. / At two months, [the spirit is] Mukuṭā; the body becomes cold and chilled,

298.s:
chardhiḥ syānmukhaśoṣādipuṣpagandhāṃśukāni ca /
apūpamodanaṃ dīpaḥ kṛṣṇaṃ nīrādi dhūpakam //
298.d:
छर्धिः स्यान्मुखशोषादिपुष्पगन्धांशुकानि च /
अपूपमोदनं दीपः कृष्णं नीरादि धूपकम् //
298.m: there is vomiting, dryness of the mouth and the like, [and one offers] fragrant flowers, garments, / sweet cakes, boiled rice, a lamp, dark-colored water, and incense.

298.s:
tṛtīye gomukhī nidrā savinmūtraprarodanam /
yavāḥ priyaṅguḥ palanaṃ kulmāṣaṃ śākamodanam //
298.d:
तृतीये गोमुखी निद्रा सविन्मूत्रप्ररोदनम् /
यवाः प्रियङ्गुः पलनं कुल्माषं शाकमोदनम् //
298.m: At the third [month, the spirit is] Gomukhī; [the symptoms are] sleepiness, weeping accompanied by excretion of feces and urine; / [the offerings are] barley, priyaṅgu, meat, boiled coarse grain, vegetables, and boiled rice.

298.s:
kṣīraṃ pūrve dadenmadhye 'hani dhūpaś ca sarpiṣā /
pañcabhaṅgena tat snānaṃ caturthe piṅgalārtihṛt //
298.d:
क्षीरं पूर्वे ददेन्मध्ये ऽहनि धूपश् च सर्पिषा /
पञ्चभङ्गेन तत् स्नानं चतुर्थे पिङ्गलार्तिहृत् //
298.m: One should offer milk in the east, and at midday fumigation with clarified butter; / the bath is made with the five broken twigs. In the fourth [month, the spirit is] Piṅgalā, destroying comfort;

298.s:
tanuḥ śītā pūtigandhaḥ śoṣaḥ sa mriyate dhruvam /
pañcamī lalanā gātrasādaḥ syānmukhaśoṣaṇaṃ //
298.d:
तनुः शीता पूतिगन्धः शोषः स म्रियते ध्रुवम् /
पञ्चमी ललना गात्रसादः स्यान्मुखशोषणं //
298.m: the body is cold, has a foul smell, and emaciation occurs; he surely dies. / The fifth is Lalanā; there is exhaustion of the limbs and dryness of the mouth,

298.s:
apānaḥ pītavarṇaś ca matsyādyair dakṣiṇe baliḥ /
ṣaṇmāse paṅkajā ceṣṭā rodanaṃ vikṛtaḥ svaraḥ //
298.d:
अपानः पीतवर्णश् च मत्स्याद्यैर् दक्षिणे बलिः /
षण्मासे पङ्कजा चेष्टा रोदनं विकृतः स्वरः //
298.m: and the downward breath and stool are yellow; one should make a sacrificial offering with fish and the like in the south. / At six months, [the spirit is] Paṅkajā; her symptoms are weeping and an altered voice;

298.s:
matsyamāṃsasurābhaktapuṣpagandhādibhirbaliḥ /
saprame tu nirāhārā pūtigandhādidantaruk //
298.d:
मत्स्यमांससुराभक्तपुष्पगन्धादिभिर्बलिः /
सप्रमे तु निराहारा पूतिगन्धादिदन्तरुक् //
298.m: the sacrificial offering is made with fish, meat, liquor, cooked rice, flowers, scents, and the like. / In the seventh [month, the child is] without appetite, foul-smelling, and suffers tooth pain;

298.s:
piṣṭamāṃsasurāmāṃsair baliḥ syādyamunāṣṭame /
visphoṭaśoṣaṇādyaṃ syāt taccikitsānna kārayet //
298.d:
पिष्टमांससुरामांसैर् बलिः स्याद्यमुनाष्टमे /
विस्फोटशोषणाद्यं स्यात् तच्चिकित्सान्न कारयेत् //
298.m: the sacrificial offering is made with flour cakes, meat, and liquor. In the eighth [month, the spirit is] Yamunā; / pustules, wasting, and other symptoms occur; one should not attempt its treatment.

298.s:
navame kumbhakarṇyārto jvarī cchardati pālakam /
rodanaṃ māṃsakulmāṣamadyādyair vaiśvake baliḥ //
298.d:
नवमे कुम्भकर्ण्यार्तो ज्वरी च्छर्दति पालकम् /
रोदनं मांसकुल्माषमद्याद्यैर् वैश्वके बलिः //
298.m: In the ninth [month], afflicted by Kumbhakarṇī, the infant has fever and vomits milk, / and cries; the sacrificial offering is made in the northwest quarter with meat, boiled coarse grain, liquor, and the like.

298.s:
daśame tāpasī ceṣṭā nirāhārokṣimīlanam /
ghaṇṭā patākā piṣṭoktā surāmāṃsabaliḥ same //
298.d:
दशमे तापसी चेष्टा निराहारोक्षिमीलनम् /
घण्टा पताका पिष्टोक्ता सुरामांसबलिः समे //
298.m: In the tenth [month, the spirit is] Tāpasī; the symptoms are refusal of food and closing of the eyes; / a bell, a banner, [an image] made of dough, liquor, and meat constitute the sacrificial offering on level ground.

298.s:
rākṣasyekādaśī pīḍā netrādyaṃ na cikitsanam /
:p 106
cañcalā dvādaśe śvāsaḥ trāsādikaviceṣṭitam //
298.d:
राक्षस्येकादशी पीडा नेत्राद्यं न चिकित्सनम् /
:प् 106
चञ्चला द्वादशे श्वासः त्रासादिकविचेष्टितम् //

298.s:
baliḥ pūrve 'tha madhyāhne kulmāpādyaistilādibhiḥ /
yātanā tu dvitīye 'bde yātanaṃ rodanādikam //
298.d:
बलिः पूर्वे ऽथ मध्याह्ने कुल्मापाद्यैस्तिलादिभिः /
यातना तु द्वितीये ऽब्दे यातनं रोदनादिकम् //
298.m: the sacrificial offering is given in the eastern quarter at midday with boiled coarse grain, sesame, and the like. / In the second year, [the spirit is] Yātanā, causing torment, weeping, and the like.

298.s:
tilamāṃsamadyamāṃsair baliḥ snānādi pūrvavat /
tṛtīye rodanī kampo rodanaṃ raktamūtrakaṃ //
298.d:
तिलमांसमद्यमांसैर् बलिः स्नानादि पूर्ववत् /
तृतीये रोदनी कम्पो रोदनं रक्तमूत्रकं //
298.m: The sacrificial offering is with sesame, meat, liquor, and flesh; bathing and other rites are as before. / In the third year, [the spirit is] Rodanī; trembling, crying, and bloody urine [are the symptoms].

298.s:
guḍaudanaṃ tilāpūpaḥ pratimā tilapiṣṭajā /
tilasnānaṃ pañcapatrair dhūpo rājaphalatvacā //
298.d:
गुडौदनं तिलापूपः प्रतिमा तिलपिष्टजा /
तिलस्नानं पञ्चपत्रैर् धूपो राजफलत्वचा //
298.m: Boiled rice with jaggery, sesame cakes, an effigy made of sesame paste, / a sesame bath with leaves of five plants, and fumigation with the bark of rājaphala [are prescribed].

298.s:
caturthe caṭakāśopho jvaraḥ sarvāṅgasādanam /
matsyamāṃsatilādyaiś ca baliḥ snānañca dhūpanam //
298.d:
चतुर्थे चटकाशोफो ज्वरः सर्वाङ्गसादनम् /
मत्स्यमांसतिलाद्यैश् च बलिः स्नानञ्च धूपनम् //
298.m: In the fourth [year, the spirit is] Caṭakā; swelling, fever, and exhaustion of all limbs [occur]; / the sacrificial offering is made with fish, meat, sesame, and the like, along with bathing and fumigation.

298.s:
cañcalā pañcame 'bde tu jvarastrāso 'ṅgasādanam /
māṃsaudanādyaiś ca balirmeṣaśṛṅgeṇa dhūpanam //
298.d:
चञ्चला पञ्चमे ऽब्दे तु ज्वरस्त्रासो ऽङ्गसादनम् /
मांसौदनाद्यैश् च बलिर्मेषशृङ्गेण धूपनम् //
298.m: In the fifth year, [the spirit is] Cañcalā; fever, terror, and exhaustion of limbs [occur]; / the sacrificial offering is with meat, boiled rice, and the like, and fumigation is with meṣaśṛṅgī.

298.s:
palāśodumbarāśvatthavaṭabilvadalāmbudhṛk /
ṣaṣṭhe 'bde dhāvanīśoṣo vairasyaṃ(1) gātrasādanam //
298.d:
पलाशोदुम्बराश्वत्थवटबिल्वदलाम्बुधृक् /
षष्ठे ऽब्दे धावनीशोषो वैरस्यं(1) गात्रसादनम् //
298.m: Water infused with leaves of palāśa, udumbara, aśvattha, vaṭa, and bilva should be applied. / In the sixth year, [the spirit is] Dhāvanī; wasting, bad taste in the mouth, and exhaustion of limbs [occur].

298.s:
saptāhobhirbaliḥ pūrvair dhupasnānañca bhaṅgakaiḥ(2) /
saptame yamunācchardiravacohāsarodanam //
298.d:
सप्ताहोभिर्बलिः पूर्वैर् धुपस्नानञ्च भङ्गकैः(2) /
सप्तमे यमुनाच्छर्दिरवचोहासरोदनम् //
298.m: For seven days the sacrificial offerings should be as before, with fumigation and bathing with the five twig-leaves. / In the seventh year, [the spirit is] Yamunā; vomiting, muteness, laughter, and weeping [occur].

298.s:
māṃsapādyasamadyādyair baliḥ snānañca dhūpanam /
aṣṭame vā jātavedā nirāhāraṃ prarodanam //
298.d:
मांसपाद्यसमद्याद्यैर् बलिः स्नानञ्च धूपनम् /
अष्टमे वा जातवेदा निराहारं प्ररोदनम् //
298.m: The sacrificial offering is with meat, milk-rice, liquor, and the like, together with bathing and fumigation. / In the eighth year, [the spirit is] Jātavedā; refusal of food and excessive weeping [occur].

298.s:
kṛśarāpūpadadhyādyair baliḥ snānañca dhūpanam /
kālābde navame vāhvorāsphoṭo garjanaṃ bhayam //
298.d:
कृशरापूपदध्याद्यैर् बलिः स्नानञ्च धूपनम् /
कालाब्दे नवमे वाह्वोरास्फोटो गर्जनं भयम् //
298.m: The sacrificial offering is with kṛśarā, cakes, curd, and the like, along with bathing and fumigation. / In the ninth year of time, [the symptoms are] thrashing of the arms, roaring, and terror.

298.s:
baliḥ syāt kṛśarāpūpaśaktukulmāsapāyasaiḥ /
daśame 'bde kalahaṃsī dāho 'ṅgakṛśatā jvaraḥ //
:n
1 vaivarṇyamiti ṭha..
2 bhāgakair iti kha..
:p 107
298.d:
बलिः स्यात् कृशरापूपशक्तुकुल्मासपायसैः /
दशमे ऽब्दे कलहंसी दाहो ऽङ्गकृशता ज्वरः //
:न्
1 वैवर्ण्यमिति ठ..
2 भागकैर् इति ख..
:प् 107
298.m:
The sacrificial offering should consist of kṛśarā, sweet cakes, roasted grain flour, boiled coarse grain, and milk-rice. / In the tenth year, [the spirit is] Kalahaṃsī; burning sensation, emaciation of limbs, and fever [occur].
[Footnote]
1. “vaivarṇyam” in manuscript ṭha.
2. “bhāgakaiḥ” in manuscript kha.

298.s:
paulikāpūpadadhyannaiḥ pañcarātraṃ baliṃ haret /
nimbadhūpakuṣṭhalepa ekādaśamake grahī //
298.d:
पौलिकापूपदध्यन्नैः पञ्चरात्रं बलिं हरेत् /
निम्बधूपकुष्ठलेप एकादशमके ग्रही //
298.m: For five nights one should offer a sacrificial offering of stuffed pastries, sweet cakes, and curd-rice; / fumigation is with neem, and anointing is with kuṣṭha. In the eleventh [year], the seizing spirit

298.s:
devadūtī niṣṭhuravāk balirlepādi pūrvavat /
balikā dvādaśe balirlepādi pūrvavat //
298.d:
देवदूती निष्ठुरवाक् बलिर्लेपादि पूर्ववत् /
बलिका द्वादशे बलिर्लेपादि पूर्ववत् //
298.m: is Devadūtī; harsh speech [is the symptom]; the sacrificial offering, anointment, and the rest are as before. / In the twelfth [year, the spirit is] Balikā; the sacrificial offering, anointment, and the rest are as before.

298.s:
trayodaśe vāyavī ca mukhavāhyāṅgasādanam /
raktānnagandhamālyādyair baliḥ pañcadalaiḥ snapet //
298.d:
त्रयोदशे वायवी च मुखवाह्याङ्गसादनम् /
रक्तान्नगन्धमाल्याद्यैर् बलिः पञ्चदलैः स्नपेत् //
298.m: On the thirteenth [day], Vāyavī [seizes], causing affliction of the face and external limbs. / One should offer a tribute with red rice, fragrant substances, garlands, and the like, and bathe [the child] with [water infused with] five leaves.

298.s:
rājīnisvadalair dhūpo yakṣiṇī ca caturdaśe /
ceṣṭā śūlaṃ jvaro dāho māṃsabhakṣādikair baliḥ //
298.d:
राजीनिस्वदलैर् धूपो यक्षिणी च चतुर्दशे /
चेष्टा शूलं ज्वरो दाहो मांसभक्षादिकैर् बलिः //
298.m: Fumigation is done with mustard and its leaves. On the fourteenth, a Yakṣiṇī [seizes]; / [the symptoms are] spasms, colic, fever, and a burning sensation. Tribute consists of meat, food, and the like;

298.s:
snānādi pūrvavacchāntyai muṇḍikārtistripañcake /
tacceṣṭāsṛkśravaḥ śaśvatkuryāmmātṛcikitsanam //
298.d:
स्नानादि पूर्ववच्छान्त्यै मुण्डिकार्तिस्त्रिपञ्चके /
तच्चेष्टासृक्श्रवः शश्वत्कुर्याम्मातृचिकित्सनम् //
298.m: bathing and the rest are as before for pacification. On the fifteenth, Muṇḍikā causes distress; / her symptoms are continual discharge of blood. One should perform the treatment for Mothers.

298.s:
vānarī ṣoḍaśī bhūmau patennidrā sadā jvaraḥ /
pāyasādyaistrirātrañca valiḥ snānādi pūrvavat //
298.d:
वानरी षोडशी भूमौ पतेन्निद्रा सदा ज्वरः /
पायसाद्यैस्त्रिरात्रञ्च वलिः स्नानादि पूर्ववत् //
298.m: On the sixteenth, Vānarī [seizes]: [the child] falls to the ground, sleeps [excessively], and constantly has fever. / A tribute of milk-rice and the like [is given] for three nights, and bathing and the rest are as before.

298.s:
gandhavatī saptadaśe gātrodvegaḥ prarodanam /
kulmāṣādyair baliḥ snānadhūpalepādi pūrvavat //
298.d:
गन्धवती सप्तदशे गात्रोद्वेगः प्ररोदनम् /
कुल्माषाद्यैर् बलिः स्नानधूपलेपादि पूर्ववत् //
298.m: On the seventeenth, Gandhavatī [seizes]: trembling of the limbs and weeping [occur]. / Tribute consists of boiled mash and the like; bathing, fumigation, anointing, and the rest are as before.

298.s:
dineśāḥ pūtanā nāma varṣeśāḥ sukumārikāḥ /
oṃ namaḥ sarvamātṛbhyo bālapīḍāsaṃyogaṃ bhuñja bhuñja
cuṭa cuṭa sphoṭaya sphoṭaya sphura sphura gṛhṇa gṛhṇa
ākaṭṭaya ākaṭṭaya evaṃ siddharūpo jñāpayati / hare hare
nirdoṣaṃ kuru kuru bālikāṃ bālaṃ striyam puruṣaṃ vā
sarvagrahāṇāmupakramāt
cāmuṇḍe namo devyai hrūṃ hrūṃ hrīṃ apasara apasara
duṣṭagrahān hrūṃ tadyathā gacchantu gṛhyakāḥ anyatra
panthānaṃ rudro jñāpayati
sarvabālagraheṣu syānmantro 'yaṃ sarvakāmikaḥ //
oṃ namo bhagavati cāmuṇḍe muñca muñca baliṃ bālikāṃ vā
:p 108
298.d:
दिनेशाः पूतना नाम वर्षेशाः सुकुमारिकाः /
ओं नमः सर्वमातृभ्यो बालपीडासंयोगं भुञ्ज भुञ्ज
चुट चुट स्फोटय स्फोटय स्फुर स्फुर गृह्ण गृह्ण
आकट्टय आकट्टय एवं सिद्धरूपो ज्ञापयति / हरे हरे
निर्दोषं कुरु कुरु बालिकां बालं स्त्रियम् पुरुषं वा
सर्वग्रहाणामुपक्रमात्
चामुण्डे नमो देव्यै ह्रूं ह्रूं ह्रीं अपसर अपसर
दुष्टग्रहान् ह्रूं तद्यथा गच्छन्तु गृह्यकाः अन्यत्र
पन्थानं रुद्रो ज्ञापयति
सर्वबालग्रहेषु स्यान्मन्त्रो ऽयं सर्वकामिकः //
ओं नमो भगवति चामुण्डे मुञ्च मुञ्च बलिं बालिकां वा
:प् 108
298.m:
The rulers of the days are named Pūtanās; the rulers of the years are the Sukumārikās.
Om, homage to all the Mothers! Consume, consume the affliction of the child! / Split, split, burst, burst, flash, flash, seize, seize, / drag, drag! Thus one of perfected form commands. O Hari, O Hari, / make free from blemish, free from blemish, the girl, the boy, the woman, or the man / from the attack of all seizing spirits!
Homage to Goddess Cāmuṇḍā! Hrūṃ hrūṃ hrīṃ! Dispel, dispel / the evil spirits, hrūṃ! Thus, may the Gṛhyakas depart elsewhere, / [to another] path; Rudra commands!
This mantra is effective for all desires in cases of all seizing spirits of children.
Om, homage to the Blessed Lady Cāmuṇḍā! Release, release the tribute or the young girl!

298.s:
baliṃ gṛhṇa gṛhṇa jaya jaya vasa vasa /
sarvatra balidāne 'yaṃ rakṣākṛt paṭhyate manuḥ /
rakṣantu ca jvarābhyāntaṃ muñcantu ca kumārakam /
brahmā viṣṇuḥ śivaḥ skando gauro gaurīlakṣmīrgaṇādayaḥ //
:e ity āgnaye mahāpurāṇe bālagrahaharaṃ bālatantraṃ nāma
aṣṭanavatyadhikadviṣatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:ś atha navanavatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
grahahṛnmantrādikam
298.d:
बलिं गृह्ण गृह्ण जय जय वस वस /
सर्वत्र बलिदाने ऽयं रक्षाकृत् पठ्यते मनुः /
रक्षन्तु च ज्वराभ्यान्तं मुञ्चन्तु च कुमारकम् /
ब्रह्मा विष्णुः शिवः स्कन्दो गौरो गौरीलक्ष्मीर्गणादयः //
:ए इत्य् आग्नये महापुराणे बालग्रहहरं बालतन्त्रं नाम
अष्टनवत्यधिकद्विषततमो ऽध्यायः
:श् अथ नवनवत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
ग्रहहृन्मन्त्रादिकम्
298.m:
Take the tribute, take! Conquer, conquer! Abide, abide! / This mantra, which affords protection, is recited everywhere in the offering of tribute: / 'May Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva, Skanda, the Fair One, Gaurī, Lakṣmī, the Gaṇas, and the rest / protect [the child] afflicted with fever, and release the young boy!'
Thus ends the two hundred and ninety-eighth chapter in the great Agni Purāṇa, named the doctrine of children which removes seizing spirits of children.
Now begins the two hundred and ninety-ninth chapter:
Mantras and related rites for removing seizing spirits.

299.s:
agnir uvāca
grahāpahāramantrādīn vakṣye grahavimardanān /
harṣecchābhayaśokādiviruddhāśucibhojanāt //
299.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
ग्रहापहारमन्त्रादीन् वक्ष्ये ग्रहविमर्दनान् /
हर्षेच्छाभयशोकादिविरुद्धाशुचिभोजनात् //
299.m: Agni said: / I shall explain the mantras and methods that remove seizing spirits, which crush seizing spirits. / From joy, desire, fear, grief, and the like, from eating incompatible and impure food,

299.s:
gurudevādikopācca pañconmādā bhavanty atha /
tridoṣajāḥ sannipātā āganturiti te smṛtāḥ //
299.d:
गुरुदेवादिकोपाच्च पञ्चोन्मादा भवन्त्य् अथ /
त्रिदोषजाः सन्निपाता आगन्तुरिति ते स्मृताः //
299.m: and from the wrath of elders, deities, and others, the five forms of insanity arise. / They are known as originating from the three bodily humors, from their combined vitiation, and from external causes.

299.s:
devādayo grahā jātā rudrakrodhādanekadhā /
saritsarastaḍāgādau śailopavanasetuṣu //
299.d:
देवादयो ग्रहा जाता रुद्रक्रोधादनेकधा /
सरित्सरस्तडागादौ शैलोपवनसेतुषु //
299.m: Seizing spirits such as gods were born in many forms from the anger of Rudra. / In rivers, lakes, ponds, and the like, on mountains, in groves, and on bridges,

299.s:
nadīsaṅge śūnyagṛhe viladvāryekavṛkṣake /
grahā gṛhṇanti puṃsaś ca śriyaḥ(1) suptāñca garbhiṇīm //
299.d:
नदीसङ्गे शून्यगृहे विलद्वार्येकवृक्षके /
ग्रहा गृह्णन्ति पुंसश् च श्रियः(1) सुप्ताञ्च गर्भिणीम् //
299.m: at river confluences, in deserted houses, at the mouths of caves, and under solitary trees, / the seizing spirits seize men, and women who are asleep or pregnant,

299.s:
āsannapuṣpānnagnāñca ṛtusnānaṃ karoti yā /
avamānaṃ nṛṇāṃ vairaṃ vighnaṃ bhāgyaviparyayaḥ //
299.d:
आसन्नपुष्पान्नग्नाञ्च ऋतुस्नानं करोति या /
अवमानं नृणां वैरं विघ्नं भाग्यविपर्ययः //
299.m: those nearing menstruation, naked women, and one who takes the post-menstrual bath. / Dishonor, enmity among men, obstacles, adverse fortune,

299.s:
devatāgurudharmādisadācārādilaṅghanam /
:n
1 striya iti ña.. , ṭa.. ca
:p 109
patanaṃ śailavṛkṣādervidhunvanmūrdhajaṃ muhuḥ //
299.d:
देवतागुरुधर्मादिसदाचारादिलङ्घनम् /
:न्
1 स्त्रिय इति ञ.. , ट.. च
:प् 109
पतनं शैलवृक्षादेर्विधुन्वन्मूर्धजं मुहुः //
299.m:
transgression against deities, elders, religious duty, and good conduct,
[Footnote]
1. In manuscripts ña and ṭa: "striyaḥ".
[Page 109]
falling from mountains, trees, and the like, shaking the hair repeatedly,

299.s:
rudannṛtyati raktākṣo hūṃrūpo 'nugrahī naraḥ /
udvignaḥ śūladāhārtaḥ kṣuttṛṣṇārtaḥ śirortimān //
299.d:
रुदन्नृत्यति रक्ताक्षो हूंरूपो ऽनुग्रही नरः /
उद्विग्नः शूलदाहार्तः क्षुत्तृष्णार्तः शिरोर्तिमान् //
299.m: weeping and dancing with red eyes, uttering the sound 'hūṃ'—such is a possessed man. / Agitated, afflicted with colic and burning, suffering from hunger and thirst, with a headache,

299.s:
dehi dahīti yāceta balikāmagrahī naraḥ /
strīmālābhogasnānecchūratikāmagrahī naraḥ //
299.d:
देहि दहीति याचेत बलिकामग्रही नरः /
स्त्रीमालाभोगस्नानेच्छूरतिकामग्रही नरः //
299.m: the possessed man begs, 'Give, give!' longing for offerings of tribute. / A man seized by lustful spirits desires women, garlands, pleasures, and bathing.

299.s:
mahāsudarśano vyomavyāpī viṭapanāsikaḥ(1) /
pātālanārasiṃhādyā caṇḍīmantrā grahārdanāḥ //
299.d:
महासुदर्शनो व्योमव्यापी विटपनासिकः(1) /
पातालनारसिंहाद्या चण्डीमन्त्रा ग्रहार्दनाः //
299.m: The great Sudarśana, sky-pervading, branch-nosed, / Pātāla-Nārasiṃha, and the Caṇḍī mantras crush seizing spirits.

299.s:
pṛśnīhiṅguvacācakraśirīṣadayitamparam /
pāśāṅkuśadharaṃ devamakṣamālākapālinam //
299.d:
पृश्नीहिङ्गुवचाचक्रशिरीषदयितम्परम् /
पाशाङ्कुशधरं देवमक्षमालाकपालिनम् //
299.m: Pṛśnī, asafoetida, sweet flag, cakra, and siris are supreme favorites. / [One should meditate on] the god holding a noose and a goad, possessing a rosary and a skull,

299.s:
khaṭṭāṅgābjādiśiktiñca dadhānaṃ caturānanam /
antarvāhyādikhaṭṭāṅgapadmasthaṃ ravimaṇḍale //
299.d:
खट्टाङ्गाब्जादिशिक्तिञ्च दधानं चतुराननम् /
अन्तर्वाह्यादिखट्टाङ्गपद्मस्थं रविमण्डले //
299.m: wielding a skull-staff, a lotus, and other powers, four-faced, / situated on an inner and outer skull-staff and lotus within the orb of the sun.

299.s:
ādityādiyutaṃ prārcya uditerke 'rghyakaṃ dadet /
śvāsaviṣāgniviprakuṇḍīhṛllekhāsakalo bhṛguḥ //
299.d:
आदित्यादियुतं प्रार्च्य उदितेर्के ऽर्घ्यकं ददेत् /
श्वासविषाग्निविप्रकुण्डीहृल्लेखासकलो भृगुः //
299.m: Having first worshipped him accompanied by the Sun and others, one should offer the water offering when the sun has risen. / Breathing, poison, fire, Brahmin, water-pot, heart-letter, [and] Bhṛgu with all parts,

299.s:
arkāya bhūrbhuvaḥsvaś ca jvālinīṃ kulamudgaram /
padmāsano 'ruṇo raktavastrasadyutiviśvakaḥ //
299.d:
अर्काय भूर्भुवःस्वश् च ज्वालिनीं कुलमुद्गरम् /
पद्मासनो ऽरुणो रक्तवस्त्रसद्युतिविश्वकः //
299.m: for the Sun, 'Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ', Jvālinī, and the family club. / Seated on a lotus, reddish, endowed with red garments and splendor, universal,

299.s:
udāraḥ padmadhṛgdorbhyāṃ saumyaḥ sarvāṅgabhūṣitaḥ /
raktā hṛdādayaḥ saumyā varadāḥ padmadhāriṇaḥ //
299.d:
उदारः पद्मधृग्दोर्भ्यां सौम्यः सर्वाङ्गभूषितः /
रक्ता हृदादयः सौम्या वरदाः पद्मधारिणः //
299.m: noble, holding lotuses in two hands, gentle, adorned in all limbs; / the heart and other [limbs] are red, gentle, boon-granting, and holding lotuses.

299.s:
vidyutpuñjanibhaṃ vastraṃ śvetaḥ saumyo 'ruṇaḥ kujaḥ /
budhastadvadguruḥ pītaḥ śuklaḥ śukraḥ śanaiś caraḥ //
299.d:
विद्युत्पुञ्जनिभं वस्त्रं श्वेतः सौम्यो ऽरुणः कुजः /
बुधस्तद्वद्गुरुः पीतः शुक्लः शुक्रः शनैश् चरः //
299.m: His garment resembles a cluster of lightning; [the Moon is] white and gentle; Mars is reddish; / Mercury is likewise; Jupiter is yellow; Venus is white; Saturn

299.s:
kṛṣṇāṅgāranibho rāhurdhūmraḥ keturudāhṛtaḥ /
vāmoruvāmahastānte dakṣahastābhayapradā //
299.d:
कृष्णाङ्गारनिभो राहुर्धूम्रः केतुरुदाहृतः /
वामोरुवामहस्तान्ते दक्षहस्ताभयप्रदा //
299.m: resembles black charcoal; Rāhu is declared smoky, [as is] Ketu. / With their left hands on the left thigh and granting fearlessness with the right hands,

299.s:
svanāmādyantu vījāste hastau saṃśodhya cāstrataḥ /
:n
1 vipiṭanāsika iti ña..
:p 110
aṅguṣṭhādau tale netre hṛdādyaṃ vyāpakaṃ nyaset //
299.d:
स्वनामाद्यन्तु वीजास्ते हस्तौ संशोध्य चास्त्रतः /
:न्
1 विपिटनासिक इति ञ..
:प् 110
अङ्गुष्ठादौ तले नेत्रे हृदाद्यं व्यापकं न्यसेत् //
299.m:
their seed-syllables begin with their own names. Having purified both hands with the weapon-mantra,
[Footnote]
1. In manuscript ña: "vipiṭanāsikaḥ".
[Page 110]
one should perform the ritual deposition of the heart and other limbs pervading the thumb and other [fingers], the palm, and the eyes.

299.s:
mūlavījaistribhiḥ prāṇadhyāyakaṃ nyasya sāṅgakam /
prakṣālya pātramastreṇa mūlenāpūrya vāriṇā //
299.d:
मूलवीजैस्त्रिभिः प्राणध्यायकं न्यस्य साङ्गकम् /
प्रक्षाल्य पात्रमस्त्रेण मूलेनापूर्य वारिणा //
299.m: Having performed the ritual deposition of the vital breath along with the limbs using the three root seed-syllables, / washing the vessel with the weapon-mantra and filling it with water using the root mantra,

299.s:
gandhapuṣpākṣataṃ nyasya dūrvāmarghyañca mantrayet /
ātmānaṃ tena samprokṣya pūjādravyañca vai dhruvam //
299.d:
गन्धपुष्पाक्षतं न्यस्य दूर्वामर्घ्यञ्च मन्त्रयेत् /
आत्मानं तेन सम्प्रोक्ष्य पूजाद्रव्यञ्च वै ध्रुवम् //
299.m: depositing sandalwood paste, flowers, unbroken rice grains, and dūrvā grass, one should consecrate the water offering. / Having sprinkled oneself and the worship requisites with that, steadfastly,

299.s:
prabhūtaṃ vimalaṃ sāramārādhyaṃ paramaṃ sukham /
pīṭhādyān kalpayedetān hṛdā madhye vidikṣu ca //
299.d:
प्रभूतं विमलं सारमाराध्यं परमं सुखम् /
पीठाद्यान् कल्पयेदेतान् हृदा मध्ये विदिक्षु च //
299.m: one should imagine in the center and in the intermediate directions, using the heart-mantra, the seats [beginning with] / the Abundant, the Pure, the Essence, the Worthy of Worship, and the Supreme Bliss.

299.s:
pīṭhopari hṛdā madhye dikṣu caiva vidikṣu ca /
pīṭhopari hṛdābjañca keśaveṣvaṣṭaśaktayaḥ //
299.d:
पीठोपरि हृदा मध्ये दिक्षु चैव विदिक्षु च /
पीठोपरि हृदाब्जञ्च केशवेष्वष्टशक्तयः //
299.m: Upon the seat in the center, and in the cardinal and intermediate directions with the heart-mantra, / and upon the seat, the heart-lotus, with the eight powers in the filaments:

299.s:
vāṃ dīptāṃ vīṃ tathā sukṣmāṃ vuñjayāṃ vūñcabhādrikāṃ /
veṃ vibhūtīṃ vaiṃ vimalāṃ vomasighātavidyutām //
299.d:
वां दीप्तां वीं तथा सुक्ष्मां वुञ्जयां वूञ्चभाद्रिकां /
वें विभूतीं वैं विमलां वोमसिघातविद्युताम् //
299.m: Vāṃ Dīptā, Vīṃ Sūkṣmā, Vuṃ Jayā, Vūṃ Bhadrikā, / Veṃ Vibhūti, Vaiṃ Vimalā, Voṃ Amoghā,

299.s:
vauṃ sarvatomukhīṃ vaṃ pīṭhaṃ vaḥ prārcya raviṃ yajet /
āvāhya dadyāt pādyādi hṛtṣaḍaṅgena suvrata //
299.d:
वौं सर्वतोमुखीं वं पीठं वः प्रार्च्य रविं यजेत् /
आवाह्य दद्यात् पाद्यादि हृत्षडङ्गेन सुव्रत //
299.m: Vauṃ Vidyutā, Vaṃ Sarvatomukhī, and the seat Vaḥ; having worshipped these, one should worship the Sun. / Having invoked him, one should offer the foot-washing water and the rest with the heart and six limbs, O you of noble vows!

299.s:
khakārau daṇḍinau caṇḍau majjā daśanasaṃyutā /
māṃsadīrghā jaradvāyuhṛdaitat sarvadaṃ raveḥ //
299.d:
खकारौ दण्डिनौ चण्डौ मज्जा दशनसंयुता /
मांसदीर्घा जरद्वायुहृदैतत् सर्वदं रवेः //
299.m: The two kha-sounds, the staff-bearers, the Caṇḍas, marrow combined with teeth, / flesh, long [vowels], the ancient wind, and the heart: this yields all things for the Sun.

299.s:
vahnīśarakṣo marutām kikṣu pūjyā hṛdādayaḥ /
svamantraiḥ karṇikāntasthā dikṣvastraṃ purataḥ sadṛk //
299.d:
वह्नीशरक्षो मरुताम् किक्षु पूज्या हृदादयः /
स्वमन्त्रैः कर्णिकान्तस्था दिक्ष्वस्त्रं पुरतः सदृक् //
299.m: The heart and other limbs are to be worshipped in the directions of Fire, Īśa, Rakṣas, and the Wind, / each with their own mantras, stationed within the pericarp; the weapon is in the cardinal directions, facing in front.

299.s:
pūrvādidikṣu sampūjyāś candrajñagurubhārgavāḥ /
nasyāñjanādi kurvīta sājamūtrair grahāpahaiḥ //
299.d:
पूर्वादिदिक्षु सम्पूज्याश् चन्द्रज्ञगुरुभार्गवाः /
नस्याञ्जनादि कुर्वीत साजमूत्रैर् ग्रहापहैः //
299.m: The Moon, Mercury, Jupiter, and Venus are to be worshipped in the directions beginning with the east. / One should administer errhines, collyrium, and the like, with goat's urine, which dispel seizing spirits.

299.s:
pāṭhāpathyāvacāśigrusindhūvyoṣaiḥ pṛthak phalaiḥ /
ajākṣīrāḍhake pakvasarpiḥ sarvagrahān haret //
299.d:
पाठापथ्यावचाशिग्रुसिन्धूव्योषैः पृथक् फलैः /
अजाक्षीराढके पक्वसर्पिः सर्वग्रहान् हरेत् //
299.m: Ghee cooked with pāṭhā, chebulic myrobalan, sweet flag, drumstick tree, rock salt, and ginger-black pepper-long pepper, with different fruits, / in an āḍhaka measure of goat's milk, removes all seizing spirits.

299.s:
vṛścikālīphalīkuṣṭhaṃ lavaṇāni ca śārṅgakam /
apasmāravināśāya tajjalaṃ tvabhibhojayet //
:p 111
299.d:
वृश्चिकालीफलीकुष्ठं लवणानि च शार्ङ्गकम् /
अपस्मारविनाशाय तज्जलं त्वभिभोजयेत् //
:प् 111
299.m:
Heliotropium, Callicarpa macrophylla, saussurea, salts, and śārṅgaka: / for the destruction of epilepsy, one should administer that water as food.
[Page 111]

299.s:
vidārīkuśakāśekṣukvāthajaṃ pāyayet payaḥ /
droṇe sayaṣṭikuṣmāṇḍarase sarpiś ca saṃskṛtau //
299.d:
विदारीकुशकाशेक्षुक्वाथजं पाययेत् पयः /
द्रोणे सयष्टिकुष्माण्डरसे सर्पिश् च संस्कृतौ //
299.m: One should administer milk boiled with a decoction of vidārī, kuśa grass, kāśa grass, and sugarcane, / or ghee refined in a droṇa of juice of licorice and ash gourd,

299.s:
pañcagavyaṃ ghṛtaṃ tadvadyogaṃ jvaraharaṃ śṛṇu /
oṃ bhasmāstrāya vidmahe ekadaṃṣṭrāya dhīmahi tanno jvaraḥ
pracodayāt
kṛṣṇoṣaṇaniśārāsnādrākṣātailaṃ guḍaṃ lihet //
299.d:
पञ्चगव्यं घृतं तद्वद्योगं ज्वरहरं शृणु /
ओं भस्मास्त्राय विद्महे एकदंष्ट्राय धीमहि तन्नो ज्वरः
प्रचोदयात्
कृष्णोषणनिशारास्नाद्राक्षातैलं गुडं लिहेत् //

299.s:
śvāsavānatha vā bhārgīṃ sayaṣṭimadhusarpiṣā /
pāṭhā tiktā kaṇā bhārgī athavā madhunā lihet //
299.d:
श्वासवानथ वा भार्गीं सयष्टिमधुसर्पिषा /
पाठा तिक्ता कणा भार्गी अथवा मधुना लिहेत् //
299.m: or one suffering from asthma [should lick] clerodendrum with licorice, honey, and ghee; / or one should lick pāṭhā, picrorhiza, long pepper, and clerodendrum with honey.

299.s:
dhātrī viśvasitā kṛṣṇā mustā kharjūramāgadhī /
pivaraśceti hikkāghnaṃ tat trayaṃ madhunā lihet //
299.d:
धात्री विश्वसिता कृष्णा मुस्ता खर्जूरमागधी /
पिवरश्चेति हिक्काघ्नं तत् त्रयं मधुना लिहेत् //
299.m:
Myrobalan, dry ginger, sugar, long pepper, mustā, date, māgadhī,
and pivara: one should lick these three together with honey to destroy hiccups.

299.s:
kāmalī jīramāṇḍūkīniśādhātrīrasaṃ pivet /
vyoṣapadmakatriphalākiḍaṅgadevadāravaḥ /
rāsnācūrṇaṃ samaṃ khaṇḍair jagdhvā kāsaharaṃ dhruvam //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe grahahṛnmantrādikaṃ nāma
navanavatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha triśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
sūryārcanam
299.d:
कामली जीरमाण्डूकीनिशाधात्रीरसं पिवेत् /
व्योषपद्मकत्रिफलाकिडङ्गदेवदारवः /
रास्नाचूर्णं समं खण्डैर् जग्ध्वा कासहरं ध्रुवम् //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे ग्रहहृन्मन्त्रादिकं नाम
नवनवत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ त्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
सूर्यार्चनम्
299.m:
One suffering from jaundice should drink the juice of cumin, māṇḍūkī, turmeric, and myrobalan.
Trikatu, padmaka, triphalā, viḍaṅga, devadāru,
and powder of rāsnā eaten in equal parts with sugar definitely relieves cough.
Thus in the great Purāṇa of Agni, the two hundred and ninety-ninth chapter, named “Mantras for Relieving Planetary Afflictions and Other Rites.”
Now, the three hundredth chapter.
Worship of the Sun

300.s:
agnir uvāca
śayyā tu daṇḍisājeśapāvakaś caturānanaḥ /
sarvārthasādhakamidaṃ vījaṃ piṇḍārthamucyate //
300.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
शय्या तु दण्डिसाजेशपावकश् चतुराननः /
सर्वार्थसाधकमिदं वीजं पिण्डार्थमुच्यते //
300.m:
Agni said:
Śayyā, then Daṇḍin, the fire of Īśa with goats, and the four-faced [Brahmā]—
this seed-syllable, which accomplishes all ends, is stated for the purpose of the piṇḍa.

300.s:
svayaṃ dīrghasvarādyañca vījeṣvaṅgāni sarvaśaḥ /
khātaṃ sādhu viṣañcaiva savinduṃ sakalaṃ tathā //
:p 112
300.d:
स्वयं दीर्घस्वराद्यञ्च वीजेष्वङ्गानि सर्वशः /
खातं साधु विषञ्चैव सविन्दुं सकलं तथा //
:प् 112

300.s:
gaṇasya pañca vījāni pṛthagdṛṣṭaphalaṃ mahat /
gaṇaṃ jayāya namaḥ ekadaṃṣṭrāya acalakarṇine gajavaktrāya
mahoharahastāya
pañcāṅgaṃ sarvasāmānyaṃ siddhiḥ syāllakṣajāpyateḥ //
gaṇādhipataye gaṇeśvarāya gaṇanāyakāya gaṇakrīḍāya
300.d:
गणस्य पञ्च वीजानि पृथग्दृष्टफलं महत् /
गणं जयाय नमः एकदंष्ट्राय अचलकर्णिने गजवक्त्राय
महोहरहस्ताय
पञ्चाङ्गं सर्वसामान्यं सिद्धिः स्याल्लक्षजाप्यतेः //
गणाधिपतये गणेश्वराय गणनायकाय गणक्रीडाय
300.m:
There are five seed-syllables of the troop, each having a great visible result:
‘Obeisance to Gaṇa, to Jaya, to Ekadaṃṣṭra, to Acalakarṇin, to Gajavaktra,
to Mahodarahasta.’
This fivefold limb is common to all; success will result from a master reciting one hundred thousand [times].
‘To Gaṇādhipati, to Gaṇeśvara, to Gaṇanāyaka, to Gaṇakrīḍa.’

300.s:
digdale pūjayenmūrtīḥ purāvaccāṅgapañcakam /
vakratuṇḍāya ekadaṃṣṭrāya mahodarāya gajavaktrāya
vikaṭāya vighnarājāya dhūmravarṇāya
digvidikṣu yajedetāllokāṃśāṃś caiva mudrayā //
300.d:
दिग्दले पूजयेन्मूर्तीः पुरावच्चाङ्गपञ्चकम् /
वक्रतुण्डाय एकदंष्ट्राय महोदराय गजवक्त्राय
विकटाय विघ्नराजाय धूम्रवर्णाय
दिग्विदिक्षु यजेदेताल्लोकांशांश् चैव मुद्रया //
300.m:
One should worship the icons on the directional petals, as before, and the group of five limbs:
‘To Vakratuṇḍa, to Ekadaṃṣṭra, to Mahodara, to Gajavaktra,’
‘to Vikaṭa, to Vighnarāja, to Dhūmravarṇa.’
One should worship these and the regents of the worlds in the cardinal and intermediate directions with the ritual gesture.

The thumbs placed between the middle and forefingers, with both hands clenched in fists.
Four-armed, abundant in sweetmeats, equipped with staff, noose, and goad,

300.s:
dantabhakṣadharaṃ raktaṃ sābjaṃ pāśāḍkuśair vṛtam /
pūjayettaṃ caturthyāñca viśeṣenātha nityaśaḥ //
300.d:
दन्तभक्षधरं रक्तं साब्जं पाशाड्कुशैर् वृतम् /
पूजयेत्तं चतुर्थ्याञ्च विशेषेनाथ नित्यशः //
300.m:
bearing his tusk and food, red, holding a lotus, accompanied by a noose and goad—
one should worship him especially on the fourth [lunar day], and also daily.

300.s:
śvetārkamūlena kṛtaṃ sarvāptiḥ syāttilair ghṛtaiḥ /
taṇḍulair dadhimadhvājyaiḥ saubhāgyaṃ vaśyatā bhavet //
300.d:
श्वेतार्कमूलेन कृतं सर्वाप्तिः स्यात्तिलैर् घृतैः /
तण्डुलैर् दधिमध्वाज्यैः सौभाग्यं वश्यता भवेत् //
300.m:
Made from the root of white arka, it yields all attainments with sesamum and clarified butter;
with rice, curd, honey, and clarified butter, fortune and subjugation will arise.

300.s:
ghoṣāsṛkprāṇadhātvardī daṇḍī gārtaṇḍabhairavaḥ /
dharmārthakāmamokṣāṇāṃ kartā vimbapuṭāvṛtaḥ //
300.d:
घोषासृक्प्राणधात्वर्दी दण्डी गार्तण्डभैरवः /
धर्मार्थकाममोक्षाणां कर्ता विम्बपुटावृतः //
300.m:
Possessing sound, blood, life, and bodily elements, holding a staff, the fierce solar deity Mārtāṇḍa-Bhairava,
the bestower of dharma, wealth, pleasure, and liberation, is enclosed within the solar orb.

300.s:
hrasvāḥ syurmūrtaryaḥ pañca dīrghā aṅgāni tasya ca /
sindūrāruṇamīśāne vāmārdhadayitaṃ raviṃ //
300.d:
ह्रस्वाः स्युर्मूर्तर्यः पञ्च दीर्घा अङ्गानि तस्य च /
सिन्दूरारुणमीशाने वामार्धदयितं रविं //
300.m:
The five icons are short [vowels], and his limbs are the long ones.
In the northeast, the sun is crimson like vermilion, loving his left half.

In the corners beginning with the southeast are Mars, Saturn, Rāhu, and Ketu.
Having bathed according to the rules and worshipped the sun preceded by a water offering,

300.s:
kṛtāntamaiśe nirmālyaṃ tejaś caṇḍāya dīpitaṃ /
rocanā kuṅkumaṃ vāri raktagandhākṣatāṅkurāḥ //
:p 113
300.d:
कृतान्तमैशे निर्माल्यं तेजश् चण्डाय दीपितं /
रोचना कुङ्कुमं वारि रक्तगन्धाक्षताङ्कुराः //
:प् 113

300.s:
veṇuvījayavāḥśāliśyāmākatilarājikāḥ /
javāpuṣpānvitāṃ datvā pātraiḥ śirasi dhārya tat(1) //
300.d:
वेणुवीजयवाःशालिश्यामाकतिलराजिकाः /
जवापुष्पान्वितां दत्वा पात्रैः शिरसि धार्य तत्(1) //
300.m:
bamboo seed, barley, rice, millet, sesamum, and mustard,
together with hibiscus flowers—having placed them in vessels and held them on the head,

300.s:
jānubhyāmavanīṅgatvā sūryāyārghyaṃ nivedayet /
svavidyāmantritaiḥ kumbhair navabhiḥ prārcya vai grahān //
300.d:
जानुभ्यामवनीङ्गत्वा सूर्यायार्घ्यं निवेदयेत् /
स्वविद्यामन्त्रितैः कुम्भैर् नवभिः प्रार्च्य वै ग्रहान् //
300.m:
having touched the ground with both knees, one should offer the water offering to the Sun.
Having worshipped the planets with nine pitchers consecrated by their own mantras,

300.s:
grahādiśāntaye snānaṃ japtvārkaṃ sarvamāpnuyāt /
saṃgrāmavijayaṃ sāgniṃ vījadoṣaṃ savindukaṃ //
300.d:
ग्रहादिशान्तये स्नानं जप्त्वार्कं सर्वमाप्नुयात् /
संग्रामविजयं साग्निं वीजदोषं सविन्दुकं //
300.m:
the bath is for pacifying planetary afflictions; having recited [the mantra of] the Sun, one obtains everything:
victory in battle. With Agni, with the seed-syllables, and with the bindu,

300.s:
nyasya mūrdhādipādāntaṃ mūlaṃ pūjya tu mudrayā /
svāṅgāni ca yathānyāsamātmānaṃ bhāvayedraviṃ //
300.d:
न्यस्य मूर्धादिपादान्तं मूलं पूज्य तु मुद्रया /
स्वाङ्गानि च यथान्यासमात्मानं भावयेद्रविं //
300.m:
having performed the ritual deposition from the crown to the feet, and having worshipped the root mantra with the ritual gesture
and one's own limbs according to the ritual deposition, one should meditate on oneself as the Sun.

300.s:
dhyānañca māraṇastambhe pītagāpyāyane sitam /
ripughātavidhau(2) kṛṣṇaṃ mohayecchakracāpavat //
300.d:
ध्यानञ्च मारणस्तम्भे पीतगाप्यायने सितम् /
रिपुघातविधौ(2) कृष्णं मोहयेच्छक्रचापवत् //
300.m:
The meditation is yellow in killing and immobilising, white in nourishment,
black in rites for destroying enemies, and one should cause bewilderment like Indra's bow.

300.s:
yo 'bhiṣekajapadhyānapūjāhomaparaḥ sadā /
tejasvī hṛjayaḥ śrīmān samudrādau jayaṃ labhet //
300.d:
यो ऽभिषेकजपध्यानपूजाहोमपरः सदा /
तेजस्वी हृजयः श्रीमान् समुद्रादौ जयं लभेत् //
300.m:
One who is always devoted to consecration by aspersion, recitation, meditation, worship, and fire oblation
becomes radiant, victorious in heart, glorious, and attains victory upon the ocean and elsewhere.

300.s:
tāmbūlādāvidaṃ nyasya japtvā dadyāduśīrakaṃ /
nyastuvījena hastena sparśanaṃ tadvaśe smṛtaṃ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe sūryārcanaṃ nāma triśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
||
:ś athaikādhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
nānāmantrāḥ
300.d:
ताम्बूलादाविदं न्यस्य जप्त्वा दद्यादुशीरकं /
न्यस्तुवीजेन हस्तेन स्पर्शनं तद्वशे स्मृतं //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे सूर्यार्चनं नाम त्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
||
:श् अथैकाधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
नानामन्त्राः
300.m:
Having deposited this [mantra] on betel or the like and recited it, one should give uśīraka;
touching with a hand deposited with the seed-syllable is considered to bring about subjugation.
Thus in the great Purāṇa of Agni, the three hundredth chapter, named “Worship of the Sun.”
Now, the three hundred and first chapter.
Various Mantras
